## Problem Statement

Two forecasting classes exist only as "backwards-compatible entry points" extending the governance module. One is empty; the other adds a single override that flips a flag and accepts a constructor argument it never uses. They add names to learn and preserve a seam that varies across nothing.

## Solution

Fold the one override into the governance module, point the two callers and the tests at the real module, and delete both subclasses.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want one governance module, so that there is one interface to learn.
2. As a developer, I want the activation-readiness override to live in the module that owns readiness, so that behaviour is where it belongs.
3. As a developer, I want the empty subclass deleted, so that dead surface disappears.
4. As a developer, I want the ignored constructor argument removed, so that the interface stops lying.
5. As a developer, I want callers updated, so that the Administrator Model Review page uses the real module.
6. As a developer, I want contract tests updated, so that they assert behaviour rather than the existence of aliases.
7. As an Administrator, I want the approval flow unchanged.
8. As a Super Administrator, I want the promotion path unchanged.
9. As a developer, I want the activation-readiness flag toggle to have a named home in the real module.
10. As a developer, I want no new seam introduced.
11. As a developer, I want the deletion to be test-visible, so that the change is deliberate.
12. As a developer, I want the remaining module's responsibility documented.
13. As a developer, I want any backwards-compatibility need handled by the single module, so that no alias returns.
14. As a developer, I want the demo-model activation guard preserved.
15. As an operator, I want no visible change.

## Implementation Decisions

- Absorb the activation-readiness override (auto-accepting the technical review when automated quality gates pass and there is no rejection) into the governance module.
- Delete the empty promotion subclass and the activation subclass; update callers to the base governance module.
- Drop the ignored constructor parameter.
- Update the contract tests that assert the shims exist to assert behaviour on the single module instead.
- ADR-0022 (local Administrator approval) and ADR-0005 (single forecasting pipeline) are unchanged; this is a naming and structural cleanup only.
- Do this after the construction-cycle spec, since both touch the governance module.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external behaviour on the single module: activation readiness still auto-accepts only when automated gates pass and no technical rejection exists, and demo-model activation still throws.
- Prior art: `src/backend/tests/store_model_governance_contract.php`, `store_activation_contract.php`, and `model_promotion_contract.php`.
- Seam: the existing governance seam; no new seam.

## Out of Scope

- Changing approval or rollback semantics.
- Adding new governance capabilities.

## Further Notes

- Blocked by the governance/evaluation-cycle spec (both touch the same module).
- Honours ADR-0005 and ADR-0022.
title: Delete the governance shim subclasses

body:
## Problem Statement

Today, "is this Product's Demand Forecast usable for the Replenishment Recommendation?" is answered independently in three places: the Forecast Readiness page, the Replenishment Queue, and the forecast coverage view. Each re-derives the same decision — approved compatible Store model, complete 28-day Forecast Horizon, supported readiness level, not observation-only, not suspended, not superseded — from raw jobs and platform settings, and each speaks a slightly different status vocabulary.

Operators therefore see contradictory "usable / not usable" messages for the same Product, the same exclusion condition is worded three ways, and every rule change has to be repeated in three modules.

## Solution

Introduce one deep module, `ForecastUsability`, that owns the decision and its explanation. It exposes a small interface that takes a Product's aggregate Demand Forecast, the candidate job, and the governance context, and returns a single decision object: usable or not, plus the exclusion reason, category, and next action, and the status label. The three existing readers call this one interface. The status vocabulary and exclusion reasons stop drifting because they are produced in one place.

## User Stories

1. As an Inventory Manager, I want the Replenishment Queue and the Forecast Readiness page to agree on whether a Product's Demand Forecast is usable, so that I can trust the guidance.
2. As an Inventory Manager, I want the same exclusion reason text wherever a Demand Forecast is shown unusable, so that I know what to do without re-reading.
3. As an Administrator, I want Observation Mode and Recommendation Suspension to gate every surface identically, so that no page quietly shows a forecast that buying must ignore.
4. As a Super Administrator, I want an unapproved model surfaced as unapproved on every view, so that I know approval is pending.
5. As an Inventory Manager, I want a stale Demand Forecast (wrong Forecast Origin) marked consistently, so that I know to wait for the next Forecast Generation run.
6. As an Inventory Manager, I want an incomplete Demand Forecast (missing a full 28-day Forecast Horizon) rejected consistently, so that buying never relies on partial output.
7. As a Super Administrator, I want demo-versus-Store model mismatches reported the same everywhere, so that environment errors are obvious.
8. As an Administrator, I want the exclusion category (evidence / restriction / freshness / approval / recovery) consistent across surfaces, so that routing to the right action is reliable.
9. As a developer, I want to change the usability rule once, so that all callers update together.
10. As a developer, I want to test the usability decision through one interface, so that I do not have to stand up three page contexts.
11. As a developer, I want the status vocabulary defined once, so that the pages cannot diverge.
12. As an Inventory Manager, I want superseded runs identified against the latest usable job, so that I act on the freshest Demand Forecast.
13. As an Administrator, I want the Model Review and coverage surfaces to reuse the same decision, so that qualification and buying tell one story.
14. As a Super Administrator, I want the coverage page's operational issues to reuse usability reasons, so that the exception list matches the Replenishment Queue.
15. As a developer, I want the Forecast Readiness page to stop running its own forecast-status query, so that the page becomes a view over a module.
16. As a developer, I want the staleness rule (sales changed after generation) to live inside the module, so that it cannot be half-applied.
17. As an operator, I want no change to the visible labels I already rely on, so that the cleanup is invisible.
18. As a developer, I want the module to accept the governance context as an argument, so that tests substitute it instead of a database.
19. As an Inventory Manager, I want a fallback to stock rules whenever a Demand Forecast is unusable, so that replenishment guidance never disappears.
20. As a developer, I want the module to return a stable decision shape, so that callers and tests depend on one contract.

## Implementation Decisions

- New module `ForecastUsability` with a small interface. One call returns a decision for a single Product given: the aggregate Demand Forecast row, the candidate job metadata, and the governance context.
- Decision shape: `usable` (bool), `status` label, `exclusion_reason`, `exclusion_category`, `exclusion_action`.
- Governance context is passed in, not read inside the module: Observation Mode, Recommendation Suspension, approved model version, and demo/Store database flag. This keeps the module pure and testable.
- The three readers — the Forecast Readiness page helper, the Replenishment Queue, and forecast coverage — become callers. The Replenishment Queue keeps its stock-rule fallback when unusable.
- Preserve the exact existing exclusion reason strings and categories so user-visible behaviour does not change (this is a refactor, not a redesign).
- The readiness page's separate vocabulary (`Model Requires Retraining`, `Ready for training`, `Forecast Generated`, `Insufficient Data`) becomes labels the module can emit; the staleness rule moves in.
- Consumes the aggregate reader from the 28-day aggregate spec so the "complete Forecast Horizon" input is shared.
- Consumes the governance injection from the construction-cycle spec so the context is supplied without constructing services.
- ADR-0005 remains authoritative: Demand Forecasts and Replenishment Recommendations stay decision support and never create purchase orders, adjust inventory, or bypass human review. ADR-0022 approval semantics are unchanged.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external behaviour: given an aggregate and governance context, the module returns the expected decision, reason, category, and action. No assertions about SQL text or private helpers.
- Test `ForecastUsability` in isolation (pure): all combinations of Observation Mode, Recommendation Suspension, approval, staleness, completeness, readiness level, and demo mismatch.
- Test the three callers only for wiring/integration: that they delegate and render the module's output verbatim.
- Prior art: `src/backend/tests/replenishment_queue_contract.php`, `forecast_coverage_contract_test.php`, and the in-memory SQLite fixtures used across the forecasting contract tests.
- Seam: one new seam, `ForecastUsability`. The existing page/queue/coverage seams shrink to delegation.

## Out of Scope

- Changing any usability rule or user-visible copy (pure refactor).
- Retiring the legacy `stock_predictions` / `forecast_evaluations` columns.
- The aggregate query extraction and the governance injection beyond what is needed to call them.

## Further Notes

- Contradicts nothing in ADR-0005 or ADR-0022; both are honoured.
- Sequencing: best done after the 28-day aggregate spec and the construction-cycle spec so the module can consume both.
title: Deepen forecast usability into one module

body:
## Problem Statement

Model error metrics (MAE, RMSE, WAPE) and Forecast Readiness bands (Insufficient below 56 usable history days, Low 56–179, Medium 180–364, High 365 and above) are implemented independently in PHP services, PHP views, the Python worker, and a PHP test that re-implements the bands locally. Changing a band means editing four files across two runtimes, and the test can pass while production drifts.

## Solution

Create `ForecastMetrics`, a deep module holding the metric definitions and the readiness bands behind a small interface, plus a single shared band definition the Python worker reads so both runtimes agree by construction.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want Forecast Readiness levels defined once, so that labels mean the same thing everywhere.
2. As a Super Administrator, I want the Python worker and PHP to agree on bands, so that stored readiness never contradicts displayed readiness.
3. As a developer, I want to change a band in one place, so that PHP and Python update together.
4. As a developer, I want MAE, RMSE, and WAPE computed by one module, so that views stop doing arithmetic.
5. As an Administrator, I want WAPE labelled as an error metric rather than an accuracy percentage, consistently.
6. As a developer, I want a pure interface for metrics, so that tests need no database.
7. As a Super Administrator, I want the worker to read the shared band definition, so that a mismatch is impossible.
8. As a developer, I want the readiness-band test to call the real module, so that it cannot pass against a local copy.
9. As an Administrator, I want limitation-marker text tied to bands, so that "Early history" and "Standard history" wording stays consistent.
10. As a developer, I want the cross-language contract to be data rather than duplicated code, so that it is diffable and reviewable.
11. As a developer, I want candidate evaluation and prediction performance evidence to share metric helpers, so that their numbers agree.
12. As an Inventory Manager, I want the same readiness level in the Replenishment Queue and the forecast page, so that guidance is coherent.
13. As an Administrator, I want Store Reports error figures to match the Forecast Analytics page.
14. As a developer, I want a single place to change metric definition and rounding.
15. As a developer, I want a pure `readinessLevel` function, so that its boundaries are unit-testable.
16. As an operator, I want no visible change to metrics or bands.

## Implementation Decisions

- New module `ForecastMetrics` with pure functions: `mae`, `rmse`, and `wape` (per-horizon and aggregated), and `readinessLevel(usableHistoryDays)` returning the band plus limitation marker.
- Readiness bands are exposed as a single shared contract (a data file) that the Python worker reads; band literals are removed from the worker.
- PHP views (Forecast Analytics, Store Reports generation) call the module instead of inline arithmetic.
- Candidate evaluation and prediction performance evidence reuse the metric helpers.
- Band values are unchanged: 56 / 180 / 365. ADR-0005 fixes these bands; this spec only centralizes them.
- The test that re-implements bands is rewritten to call the module.
- This is a ports-and-adapters seam: one shared definition with a PHP adapter and a Python adapter.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external behaviour: for a set of predictions/actuals the metric equals the documented formula, and for a day count the band equals the documented range. No assertions about internal SQL or loops.
- Pure unit tests for all three metrics and for `readinessLevel` boundaries (55/56, 179/180, 364/365).
- A contract test asserting the Python worker's band source equals the shared PHP definition.
- Prior art: `src/backend/tests/forecast_generation_contract.php`, `candidate_evaluation_service_test.php`, and `prediction_performance_evidence_test.php`.
- Seam: one new seam, `ForecastMetrics`.

## Out of Scope

- Changing the Random Forest pipeline or how errors are collected.
- Changing any band threshold.
- Translating or restyling metric text.
- Reworking the Python evaluation algorithms themselves.

## Further Notes

- Honours ADR-0005 (bands and MAE-primary/RMSE-secondary/WAPE-for-comparison).
- Independent of the other forecasting deepening specs.
title: One forecast metrics module shared with the Python worker

body:
## Problem Statement

Two forecasting modules construct each other. The model-governance module creates a candidate-evaluation module, which constructs a governance module back, with no container. Neither can be built in isolation, so a unit test for either drags in the whole governance graph. Candidate evaluation also exposes six one-line pass-through methods to governance settings, adding interface with no depth.

## Solution

Inject one into the other at construction and remove the pass-throughs. Governance owns the settings; candidate evaluation receives governance (or the settings it needs) rather than constructing it.

## User Stories

1. As a developer, I want to construct either module alone, so that tests do not build the whole graph.
2. As a developer, I want a single owner of governance settings, so that there is no ambiguity.
3. As a developer, I want the six pass-through methods gone, so that the candidate-evaluation interface is smaller.
4. As an Administrator, I want Observation Mode, Recommendation Suspension, and thresholds read from one owner, so that behaviour is consistent.
5. As a developer, I want to test candidate evaluation with a fake governance module, so that I can simulate settings.
6. As a developer, I want to test governance with a fake evaluation module, so that I can simulate quality gates.
7. As a Super Administrator, I want Observation Mode and Recommendation Suspension toggles to take effect immediately everywhere, so that no stale second instance persists.
8. As a developer, I want no runtime change to public behaviour.
9. As a developer, I want the constructor seam to remain the test surface.
10. As a developer, I want the dependency direction documented, so that future code does not re-introduce the cycle.
11. As an Administrator, I want thresholds set and read through one path.
12. As a developer, I want removal of the mutual construction to reduce hidden coupling.
13. As a developer, I want existing contract tests to keep passing after being updated to inject dependencies.
14. As a developer, I want a clear default when the dependency is missing, rather than a silent second instance.
15. As an operator, I want no visible change.

## Implementation Decisions

- Dependency direction: governance depends only on PDO plus an optional injected evaluation module; evaluation depends on PDO plus an injected governance module. No back-construction.
- Remove the lazy internal construction that closes the cycle; require the dependency or create exactly one default instance.
- Delete `getThresholds`, `setThresholds`, `isObservationMode`, `setObservationMode`, `isRecommendationsSuspended`, and `setRecommendationsSuspended` pass-throughs on candidate evaluation; callers use governance directly.
- Preserve public method names used by contracts where governance is the real owner.
- No schema change.
- This unblocks the forecast-usability spec (governance context can be supplied) and the shim-deletion spec.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external behaviour with the other module stubbed: settings are read/written once, and quality gates behave as before.
- Inject fakes for both directions; assert each module works alone.
- Prior art: `src/backend/tests/store_model_governance_contract.php`, `candidate_evaluation_service_test.php`, and `store_model_observation_contract.php`.
- Seam: the existing constructor seam on the governance module; no new seam.

## Out of Scope

- Changing governance rules or the approval flow.
- Changing ADR-0022 approval semantics.

## Further Notes

- Honours ADR-0022 and ADR-0005.
- The shim-deletion spec should be done after this one, since both touch the governance module.
title: Break the governance/evaluation construction cycle

## Parent

Part of #421.

## What to build

Deliver a verified browser walkthrough of the prepared pipeline, restart instructions, and a truthful report of exercised and blocked stages.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Link the existing workflow: Forecast Data Import, Data Readiness, ML Operation, Model Review & Approval, Demand Forecast, Forecast Analytics, Forecast Exceptions, Replenishment Recommendations, Product Investigation, and historical M5 comparison.
- [ ] Extend existing forecasting/public-sales/M5 browser checks to save visible settings and verify effects, compare eligibility across pages, follow actual jobs, inspect real evaluation/review blockers, and verify forecast/replenishment explanations and saved totals.
- [ ] Verify AM/PM/timezone help, keyboard use, mobile layout, read-only model recipe, and removed ineffective inputs across the integrated workflow.
- [ ] Snapshot demo state before read-only review; verify unchanged sales, stock, imported history, jobs, and approvals. Confirm operational configuration and the Store database were not altered.
- [ ] Provide a working isolated local URL, demo-only account details, restart instructions for this machine, source/provenance summary, and actual training/evaluation results.
- [ ] Run syntax and focused regression checks for touched components, including controlled-clock scheduler checks. Document exercised stages and real blockers; claim Windows startup automation only if the installed task and execution were checked.
- [ ] Retain advisory purchasing and lifecycle/authorization safeguards. Never represent successful training or historical preview as operational approval.
title: Complete forecasting browser walkthrough and restart handoff

body:
## Parent

Part of #421.

## What to build

Show actual shared-worker candidate training and reproducible historical predicted-versus-actual comparisons in the isolated M5 Demo.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Queue and complete a real isolated candidate-training job through the existing asynchronous PHP/job/Python worker architecture. Use no parallel engine or mock result.
- [ ] Re-use the historical experiment/comparison importer for all three chronological 28-day held-out blocks, preserving source, fold, model, and split provenance. Each fold uses only earlier training history.
- [ ] Show actual model and weekly-baseline results even when evaluation fails. Do not lower limits, select favorable products, fabricate observation progress, redate history, or approve failed candidates.
- [ ] Distinguish historical backtests from prospective observation and current operational Forecast Generation. Explain real approval blockers and unavailable operational forecasts.
- [ ] Use only the existing explicit demo boundary for historical comparisons and quantities; show original dates and Historical demo / unapproved identification.

body:
# Align forecasting settings and demonstrate the pipeline with isolated M5 data

## Problem Statement

The Super Administrator cannot reliably understand or control Demand Forecasting because Data Readiness and ML Operation describe different policies. Data Readiness uses a fixed Training Eligibility policy, while ML Operation exposes minimum/preferred history, history-window, forecast-horizon, retraining-frequency, sales-record, accuracy, percentile, and Random Forest controls that do not govern the current pipeline. A successful save can therefore imply a behavior change that never occurs.

The user also wants to see the real pipeline working with M5 data before relying on it: history, eligibility, background training, evaluation, observation, model review, forecasts, and replenishment guidance. The demo must explain these stages without contaminating the operational Store or claiming that external-data performance establishes Store accuracy.

The latest instruction requests a specification before implementing the demo. Creating and publishing this spec does not start database provisioning or application implementation.

## Solution

Make the existing forecasting pages describe one shared policy, expose only settings consumed by the current pipeline, and let the Super Administrator choose a weekly Model Retraining day and time. Present schedule controls and times in AM/PM, explicitly in Philippine time. Explain the differences between Training Eligibility, candidate qualification, observation, approval, and daily Forecast Generation.

Prepare a separate local M5 Demo using the existing importer, shared Random Forest worker, and historical comparison screens. Use 50 reproducibly selected food products from M5 store CA_1, retaining their original dates and anonymous product identities. Provide a browser walkthrough that shows actual results and blocked transitions when a candidate fails; do not manufacture a successful approval or bypass quality gates.

## User Stories

1. As a Super Administrator, I want Data Readiness and ML Operation to show the same Training Eligibility policy, so that I can trust their explanations.
2. As a forecast viewer, I want progress displayed as usable days collected out of required days, so that 120 of 140 days is not mistaken for a 120-day requirement.
3. As a forecast viewer, I want to understand which days count as usable, so that missing records and stockouts are not mistaken for observed zero demand.
4. As a Super Administrator, I want the current 140-usable-day requirement shown read-only, so that an ineffective history setting cannot suggest that I weakened eligibility.
5. As a forecast viewer, I want recent-input and historical evaluation blockers explained, so that reaching 140 days does not imply automatic eligibility.
6. As a Super Administrator, I want disconnected minimum, preferred, nonzero-sales-day, and maximum-history controls removed, so that every available control has a real effect.
7. As an Inventory Manager, I want fixed 7-, 14-, and 28-day Forecast Horizons, so that forecast totals remain consistent across pages.
8. As a Super Administrator, I want to choose the weekly training weekday, so that background work suits the Store's operating pattern.
9. As a Super Administrator, I want to choose the weekly training time in AM/PM, so that I can configure it without converting a 24-hour clock.
10. As a Super Administrator, I want the time range and timezone explained in a tooltip, so that noon, midnight, and the selected hour are unambiguous.
11. As a Super Administrator, I want Sunday at 1:00 AM as the default weekly schedule, so that the existing default remains recognizable.
12. As a Super Administrator, I want saved schedule changes to control the actual scheduler, so that the form and background behavior agree.
13. As a Super Administrator, I want initial automatic training at the next selected training time after eligibility is detected, so that the first model need not wait for the weekly weekday.
14. As a Super Administrator, I want missed training to catch up when the PC starts, so that downtime does not postpone model work for another week.
15. As a Super Administrator, I want catch-up to require eligible new history and prevent duplicate jobs, so that startup does not create repeated training runs.
16. As a Super Administrator, I want manual training to remain available, so that I can deliberately request a run when needed.
17. As a Store operator, I want daily Forecast Generation explained separately from Model Retraining, so that I know predictions can update without rebuilding the model daily.
18. As a Super Administrator, I want the disconnected interval and new-sales-record controls removed, so that they cannot imply competing automatic triggers.
19. As a Super Administrator, I want separate working WAPE limits for the three Forecast Horizons, so that configured acceptance criteria match evaluation.
20. As a model reviewer, I want WAPE described as error with lower values better, so that it is not presented as an accuracy guarantee.
21. As a model reviewer, I want candidates compared against repeating last week's sales, so that a complex model must justify its use.
22. As a forecast viewer, I want unsupported percentile controls removed, so that a point forecast is not presented as a measured uncertainty interval.
23. As a Super Administrator, I want the actual Random Forest recipe displayed read-only, so that the page explains what training really uses.
24. As a model reviewer, I want a completed training run distinguished from a qualified candidate, so that successful execution is not confused with passing evaluation.
25. As a local Administrator, I want the required observation evidence and approval gates retained, so that an automatic training run cannot silently replace the operational model.
26. As a local Administrator, I want a failed or rejected candidate to leave the approved model unchanged, so that routine forecasts remain controlled.
27. As a user learning the system, I want a separately identified M5 Demo, so that external Walmart observations are never mistaken for this Store's sales.
28. As a Super Administrator, I want the M5 Demo in a separate database with isolated model identity and sessions, so that experimentation cannot modify operational records or approvals.
29. As a user learning the system, I want original M5 dates and product codes retained, so that the demonstration does not fabricate current Store history.
30. As a user learning the system, I want 50 CA_1 food products with sufficient historical coverage, so that I can inspect several realistic sales patterns through one shared pipeline.
31. As a Super Administrator, I want source provenance and imported counts recorded, so that the prepared dataset can be checked and reproduced.
32. As a user learning the system, I want to watch an actual queued training job complete, so that the demonstration proves background processing rather than displaying a mock result.
33. As a model reviewer, I want real model and baseline results shown even when they fail, so that the demonstration remains honest.
34. As a user learning the system, I want historical predicted-versus-actual comparisons, so that I can see where the model overpredicts or underpredicts.
35. As an Inventory Manager, I want historical demo quantities clearly separated from approved operational guidance, so that I do not use an unapproved experiment as a purchasing instruction.
36. As an Inventory Manager, I want expected sales separated from suggested purchase quantities, so that existing stock and stock rules remain understandable.
37. As an Inventory Manager, I want unavailable or unapproved forecasts to fall back to explained stock rules, so that replenishment remains usable without invented forecast coverage.
38. As a user learning the system, I want links between history, training, review, forecast, analytics, exceptions, and replenishment pages, so that I can follow the pipeline in order.
39. As a Super Administrator, I want local restart instructions and demo-only login details, so that I can reopen the prepared demonstration later.
40. As a Store owner, I want the operational database and configuration preserved, so that preparing the demonstration cannot replace real sales, stock, users, or model approvals.
41. As a keyboard or mobile user, I want accessible time controls and explanatory tooltips, so that I can use the same scheduling workflow without a mouse or large display.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing asynchronous architecture: PHP checks authorization and queues jobs, the Python CLI worker performs training and inference, and pages read persisted results. Retain one shared global Random Forest and fixed 7/14/28-day Forecast Horizons.
- Keep Training Eligibility read-only: at least 140 accumulated usable days per Product, a supported recent 28-calendar-day input window, and three supported chronological 28-day evaluation periods backed by earlier training history. Supported genuine-zero observations count; closures, unknown observations, and Stockout Days do not add usable days. Supported closures need not themselves invalidate an otherwise supported input/evaluation window.
- Reuse StoreTrainingEligibilityService and the shared history reader as the source of eligibility decisions. Remove legacy explanations that still let disconnected settings change the apparent rule. Training Eligibility is distinct from the existing Forecast Readiness evidence bands; this work does not redesign those bands.
- Update Data Readiness and ML Operation to display the shared policy and actionable blockers. Keep the accumulated usable-day count separate from elapsed calendar span and days with sales.
- Remove writable controls for minimum/preferred/nonzero-sales-day history, maximum training history, and arbitrary forecast horizon. Do not introduce a replacement configurable eligibility policy or a new history-truncation rule.
- Reuse ForecastingSchedulerService and the existing operational schedule settings. The Super Administrator can edit the weekly training weekday and time. Store only one authoritative effective schedule through the existing settings mechanism; preserve existing explicitly selected schedules rather than resetting them to defaults.
- Present the training-time control and displayed schedule times in 12-hour AM/PM, with minute precision and explicit Asia/Manila timezone. The selectable range is 12:00 AM through 11:59 PM. Do not depend on the browser's locale to guarantee AM/PM presentation. Internal schedule storage may retain the existing 24-hour representation.
- Use this time-control tooltip: "Select a time from 12:00 AM to 11:59 PM, Philippine time (Asia/Manila). Prefer a time after Store close. Missed training runs catch up when the PC starts." Permit the full stated range; after-close timing is guidance rather than a newly invented Store-hours restriction.
- Keep Sunday at 1:00 AM as the weekly default. A regular run becomes due on the selected weekday at the selected time and starts on the first available scheduler check, subject to worker availability and eligibility.
- Initial automatic training becomes due at the next occurrence of the selected training time after eligibility is detected, regardless of weekday. For example, eligible history detected Monday at 10:00 AM with a 1:00 AM selection schedules initial training for Tuesday at 1:00 AM. Do not reinterpret first detection after the selected hour as immediate permission to train during Store operations.
- A missed scheduled run, including a previously due initial run, catches up on the first scheduler check after startup without waiting for the selected time or weekday. Determine whether a run was missed from the effective schedule and run evidence; the existing fixed seven-day-age shortcut is insufficient for this contract. A training opportunity that was never due is not a missed run.
- Keep existing prerequisites, active-job deduplication, evidence-cutoff tracking, and retry protections. Catch-up requires eligible new history for Store training and must not fabricate missed historical runs or enqueue one job per missed week. Preserve the existing explicit demo treatment of frozen external history.
- Preserve manual Super Administrator training. Editing schedule settings does not itself train a model or approve a candidate. Keep daily Forecast Generation separate, with its existing 1:00 AM default and existing authorized manual requests; do not add a new daily-schedule editor in this scope.
- Replace the disconnected generic WAPE field with the three actual per-horizon limits consumed by candidate evaluation. Display percentages in the UI and convert consistently to the existing stored error fractions. Validate finite supported values at the write boundary and reuse the existing governance interface. Retain missing-evidence blocking and the strict requirement to beat the seasonal baseline.
- Remove unused lower/upper percentile controls. Current forecasts are point quantities; this work does not create prediction intervals or implied confidence guarantees.
- Replace editable Random Forest controls with the effective fixed recipe from the shared pipeline. The current recipe uses 15 trees, maximum depth 8, and random seed 42. Remove the claim that saving disconnected parameters will affect the next run.
- Preserve candidate lifecycle boundaries and the local approval ownership established by ADR-0022: training completion alone is insufficient; chronological quality checks, required observation evidence, compatible Store artifacts, and explicit local Administrator approval remain required for operational activation. Demo review never activates a Store model.
- Prepare a fresh, clearly named local demo database rather than replacing an existing database. Use isolated model identity, sessions, recovery state, and loopback-only application access. Leave the operational Store environment and ordinary connection configuration unchanged. Reuse the existing demo setup/start tools and importer; introduce no parallel forecasting engine.
- Use the existing deterministic M5 CA_1 FOODS sample of 50 products: two initial training years followed by three chronological 28-day comparison blocks. Preserve original source dates and anonymous identities. Obtain the pinned source used by the existing experiment, record provenance, and validate declared counts, dates, quantities, and product coverage before import.
- Import daily forecasting observations rather than inventing customer receipts, cashier sales, deliveries, or stock movements. Mark opening stock and replenishment parameters as illustrative demo settings, and prices/costs as placeholders rather than M5 facts.
- Run an actual isolated candidate-training job using the shared worker. Reuse the historical M5 experiment and comparison importer for saved held-out predictions, retaining their fold/model provenance. Historical backtest comparisons are distinct from prospective observation and current operational Forecast Generation.
- Do not lower quality limits, select only favorable products, fabricate observation progress, approve a failed candidate, or redate the source to make the walkthrough appear successful. If evaluation blocks approval, show the failed result and explain why operational forecasting is unavailable. Historical preview remains available through the existing explicit demo boundary.
- Cover these page responsibilities: Forecast Data Import supplies optional history; Data Readiness explains eligibility; ML Operation manages technical settings and training; Model Review & Approval handles observation and local approval; Demand Forecast displays available forecasts; Forecast Analytics compares results; Forecast Exceptions explains unavailable output; Replenishment Recommendations and Product Investigation explain stock and buying guidance; the historical comparison page presents the M5 backtest. Existing POS, Store Calendar, and receiving workflows remain data producers/consumers rather than new features.
- Keep Replenishment Recommendations advisory. Historical demo output must carry its original dates and unapproved status. Missing, stale, incomplete, or unapproved operational forecasts retain explained stock-rule fallback. Viewing output never places orders or updates stock.
- Use the existing settings schema where sufficient. Add only the minimum persistent due-state needed if existing run evidence cannot distinguish initial scheduling from a missed run. No broad configuration framework, model-tuning system, or new public API is required.
- Retain backend capability checks, local-only lifecycle restrictions, CSRF protection, input validation, and existing audit attribution. Preserve user working changes. Provide restart instructions, isolated local URL, demo-only account details, and a truthful run report when implementation is complete.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed the test boundaries: the existing browser workflow from settings through readiness, training/review, forecasts, and replenishment, plus deterministic scheduler checks with a controlled clock. Prefer these two high-level boundaries over adding new layers or mirroring implementation details.
- A good browser test saves a visible setting and verifies its observable effect, compares the eligibility rule across both pages, follows a real isolated job through its states, and checks that approval and purchasing guidance reflect actual evidence. Assertions about copied source strings alone do not establish working behavior.
- Extend existing forecasting workflow, public-sales demo, and M5 browser checks for AM/PM controls, timezone/range help, accessible keyboard use, mobile layout, read-only model recipe, removed ineffective inputs, and settings persistence. Verify midnight and noon conversion and that unauthorized saves are rejected.
- Extend scheduler service tests using controlled dates/times: just before/at/after the weekly time; nonweekly initial scheduling; initial eligibility detected after the selected time; restart before and after a due run; a missed run less than seven days old; multiple missed weeks producing one catch-up; no eligible new history; a queued/running job; and changed explicit schedules. These tests must assert jobs and cutoffs, not just formatted time strings.
- Reuse Training Eligibility tests for 139 versus 140 usable days, genuine-zero observations, closures/stockouts/missing evidence, and recent-input/evaluation blockers. Reuse existing governance/activation contracts to verify that changing displayed settings cannot bypass qualification, observation, or local approval.
- Reuse the existing public-sales importer and M5 experiment checks to verify source identity, complete product/date coverage, whole nonnegative quantities, chronological split boundaries, repeat-import refusal, and matching preview provenance. Run a real prepared import and shared-worker job in the isolated demo before reporting completion.
- Verify saved historical prediction totals against the displayed product comparisons and distinguish them from approved operational forecasts. A failed candidate is an acceptable demo result; a false approval or fabricated result is a failure.
- Snapshot relevant demo state before read-only browser review and verify no changes to sales, stock, imported history, jobs, or approvals. Confirm preparation targeted only the new demo and did not alter the operational environment configuration or Store database.
- Run syntax and focused regression checks for touched components, then document which workflow stages were actually exercised and which were blocked by real evidence. Do not claim Windows startup automation was verified unless its installed task and execution were actually checked.

## Out of Scope

- Provisioning the demo database, changing application code, or activating any model as part of this specification-only turn.
- Production deployment, remote hosting, changing the operational Store database, or importing public M5 data into Store Forecast Data Import.
- Model optimization, new algorithms, new price/promotion features, new uncertainty estimators, arbitrary horizons, editable eligibility thresholds, or an additional history-window policy.
- Replacing existing Forecast Readiness bands or claiming 140 days guarantees forecast quality.
- Immediate retraining based on sales-record counts, a second interval-based scheduling policy, automatic candidate approval, or bypassing observation requirements.
- A new daily Forecast Generation schedule editor, public hosting for the local demo, calendar redesign, and unrelated inventory/receiving changes.
- Invented M5 product names, current-date simulation, synthetic receipts, historical stockout reconstruction, or claims that Walmart sales prove unconstrained demand or local Store accuracy.
- Automatic purchasing, purchase orders, stock mutations from forecasts, and forcing a successful end-to-end activation when real candidate results do not qualify.

## Further Notes

- Agreed on 2026-11-03 in Asia/Manila; the test boundaries were explicitly confirmed during specification preparation.
- The user explicitly chose immediate startup catch-up over waiting until the next selected training time. Initial training still waits for its first selected time unless that scheduled opportunity was subsequently missed.
- This specification consolidates the approved settings discussion and the subsequent M5 demo request. It follows ADR-0005 for the shared asynchronous pipeline and ADR-0022 for local Administrator approval; it does not reinstate obsolete Super Administrator-only operational approval.
- Existing repository guides describe a prior M5 demonstration whose candidate failed its original quality gates. Those historical results and old host paths are background information, not proof that a demo database or worker is running on this machine now. Recheck the actual environment during implementation.
- Current exploratory checks found reusable scripts and installed Python data/ML dependencies. No new demo database was created, no dataset download was started, and no worker/server was launched before the user requested this spec.
- M5 source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/skforecast/m5_daily . The existing experiment pins a source revision; retain that provenance and source attribution in the prepared demonstration.
title: Align forecasting settings and demonstrate the pipeline with isolated M5 data

# Consistent notification counts and stock-alert recovery

## Problem Statement

Staff cannot tell whether Notifications represent unseen updates or unresolved stock conditions. The Inventory Manager screenshot shows Unread 0 while the bell still shows 10. Marking a low-stock Notification read does not reliably produce matching counts, and the user reports stale alerts remaining after replenishment restores safe stock.

The Administrator notification center labels stock oversight as Action needed even though routine replenishment belongs to the Inventory Manager. The Administrator screenshot shows 62 such conditions alongside a bell count of 2, implying personal work that the active Workspace cannot perform.

## Solution

Make the bell and the unfiltered Unread total agree for the active Workspace. Reading acknowledges an update and immediately clears its unread contribution; it does not alter inventory or resolve the underlying condition. An unchanged condition must not restore unread status.

Automatically resolve stock alerts when current stock no longer meets their trigger. Remove resolved alerts from Unread, active reminders, and bell counts, while retaining history in All with a Resolved label. Stock Overview and Replenishment Recommendations remain the places to track unresolved stock work.

Keep Administrator stockout and overdue-stock oversight Notifications, but exclude those inventory oversight conditions from Action needed. Reserve that section for work the active role can perform. Preserve existing role authority and routing.

## User Stories

1. As an Inventory Manager, I want the bell and unfiltered Unread total to agree, so that I can trust how many updates need reading.
2. As a staff member, I want marking one Notification read to update both counts immediately, so that acknowledgement has a clear result.
3. As a staff member, I want bulk read actions to update both counts consistently, so that clearing my inbox does not leave a stale badge.
4. As a staff member, I want the bell badge hidden at zero, so that it does not imply unseen work.
5. As a staff member, I want category filters to retain their established scope, so that a filtered count does not silently redefine the Workspace-wide bell.
6. As an Inventory Manager, I want a read low-stock Notification to stay read while the condition is unchanged, so that repeated checks do not demand acknowledgement again.
7. As an Inventory Manager, I want reading an alert to leave stock unchanged, so that acknowledging an update cannot falsify inventory.
8. As an Inventory Manager, I want successful Stock Receiving that restores safe stock to clear the active low-stock alert, so that replenished products do not remain flagged.
9. As an Inventory Manager, I want replenishment above safe stock to clear the same alert, so that excess replenishment does not leave stale warnings.
10. As an Inventory Manager, I want partial replenishment that remains low stock to retain the underlying warning, so that insufficient replenishment is not mistaken for recovery.
11. As a staff member, I want recovered stock alerts removed from Unread even if I never read them, so that obsolete warnings do not inflate the bell.
12. As a staff member, I want recovered stock alerts removed from active reminders, so that those reminders describe current conditions.
13. As a staff member, I want resolved stock Notifications retained in All with a Resolved label, so that useful history survives.
14. As an Inventory Manager, I want low stock that becomes zero stock to generate a new escalation update, so that a meaningful worsening receives attention.
15. As an Inventory Manager, I want stock that recovers and later becomes low again to generate a fresh Notification, so that recurrence is visible.
16. As an Inventory Manager, I want repeated recovery or detection checks to avoid duplicate Notifications, so that routine processing does not create noise.
17. As an Administrator, I want stockout oversight Notifications without an Action needed assignment, so that visibility does not imply replenishment authority.
18. As an Administrator, I want overdue inventory oversight kept outside Action needed, so that responsibility remains with the Inventory Manager.
19. As an Administrator, I want genuinely actionable reviews retained in Action needed, so that I can find work my role can perform.
20. As a multi-role staff member, I want counts and read actions isolated to the active Workspace, so that acknowledging inventory updates does not clear another role's inbox.
21. As a staff member, I want another user's read state protected, so that my actions cannot change their inbox.
22. As a staff member, I want existing active stock alerts reconciled against current stock, so that the fix also clears stale warnings already present.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing Notification service, Attention condition lifecycle, Workspace scoping, read actions, bell, and notification list. Diagnose the count mismatch across their consumers before changing shared behavior; the screenshot establishes a symptom, not its technical cause.
- Keep unread acknowledgement separate from condition resolution. No new acknowledgement workflow or manual stock-resolution action is required.
- Bell counts represent eligible unread Notifications in the active Workspace, never the number of unresolved conditions. The unfiltered Unread total uses the same eligibility rules. Category-specific counts may differ intentionally.
- Update the visible bell and list state after successful individual or bulk read actions without requiring a manual page reload. Preserve category-scoped bulk actions.
- Retain established stock thresholds. Current low-stock eligibility is quantity on hand at or below Reorder Level; safe stock for this alert means strictly above Reorder Level. Equality still qualifies as low stock. Do not reinterpret Safety Stock as a new trigger or change replenishment calculations.
- Evaluate each condition independently: replenishing from zero to a positive quantity clears the Administrator stockout condition, while the Inventory Manager low-stock condition remains if the quantity is still at or below Reorder Level.
- Successful Stock Receiving must make recovery visible on the next notification-center/bell render without waiting for the daily scheduler. Cover other existing stock-changing paths through the smallest shared reconciliation mechanism appropriate to the current architecture.
- Recovery removes associated stale stock updates from unread eligibility and active reminders, and cancels pending obsolete condition email through the existing lifecycle. Retain historical Notifications with a Resolved label; do not delete history or operational records.
- History resolution must distinguish a recovered occurrence from a later recurrence. A fresh occurrence must not make older resolved entries appear active again.
- Do not recreate unread Notifications for unchanged active conditions. Preserve escalation from low stock to out of stock and fresh delivery after recovery followed by recurrence.
- Exclude Administrator inventory oversight from Action needed while retaining its notification history and existing stockout/overdue-stock recipient rules. Other actionable Administrator reviews remain. Notification eligibility never grants inventory authority.
- Reconcile already-existing stock Notifications safely and repeatably against current conditions; do not limit the fix to alerts created after deployment.
- Preserve account and Workspace isolation, role-removal visibility, preferences, CSRF protection, escaped content, and accessible controls. Use existing state/storage where sufficient; this specification does not mandate a new schema.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed extending existing notification browser coverage and stock-alert service contracts. Prefer these established seams over new test interfaces.
- Test observable behavior: delivered updates, visible rows and labels, bell/list counts, permitted actions, and recurrence. Avoid tests that merely reproduce private SQL or implementation structure.
- Extend the notification list and Administrator stock-notification browser fixtures to cover individual and bulk reads, same-page bell refresh, zero-badge removal, filtered counts, active Workspace isolation, and account isolation.
- Verify Administrator stock oversight remains in notification history but is absent from Action needed; preserve a genuinely actionable Administrator review as a control.
- Extend role-notification and Attention lifecycle contracts for unchanged reruns, read-state preservation, escalation, recovery, repeated recovery, and recurrence.
- Cover stock quantities below, exactly at, and above Reorder Level; partial replenishment from zero; and replenishment to safe stock or above it.
- Exercise successful Stock Receiving through existing workflow fixtures, followed by notification rendering before any scheduled run. Assert removal from active reminders, Unread, and bell counts, plus retained Resolved history.
- Cover recovery of an unread alert, recovery of a read alert, and existing stale alerts. Confirm recurrence creates one new unread update without reactivating old history.
- Use disposable database fixtures and the existing injectable clock. Do not run destructive fixture cleanup against the configured Store database.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing the feature as part of publishing this specification.
- Changing role permissions, stock thresholds, Safety Stock calculations, or replenishment policy.
- Removing Administrator oversight delivery or adding inventory execution authority to that Workspace.
- New push/SMS channels, delivery infrastructure, manual dismissal workflows, or speculative reminder settings.
- Broad dashboard or notification-page redesign, retirement of all Action needed sections, or unrelated forecasting changes.
- Deleting notification history or modifying sales, stock, or Stock Issue records to hide warnings.

## Further Notes

- Product behavior and the existing test approach were confirmed in discussion on 2026-11-03.
- Screenshots establish a bell/list discrepancy and confusing Administrator action labeling. Stale alerts following replenishment are user-reported. Runtime root causes remain to be verified during implementation.
- This specification refines the earlier role-based notification specification; it preserves its responsibility split and replaces the confusing presentation of inventory oversight and stale stock conditions.
- No real-time cross-tab delivery is required. Counts must be correct after the user's successful read action and on the next normal render after stock recovery.
title: Fix notification unread counts, stock recovery, and Administrator action labeling
