body:
## Problem Statement

The Store Administrator needs to understand and use Demand Forecasting without machine-learning expertise. Existing forecasting pages expose readiness, candidate review, forecasts, and exceptions, but technical wording and inconsistent Ready or Active labels make it difficult to determine whether forecasts can guide buying today, which Products are covered, and who must act next.

The immediate priority is concrete evidence that the feature functions from Store history through background execution, approval, saved forecasts, display, Replenishment Recommendations, and recovery. Existing test reports include synthetic data, simulated installation assertions, and directly inserted failure notices. These are useful checks but do not prove actual worker failure notification delivery, unattended Windows/XAMPP operation, or useful predictions on genuine Store sales.

Final deployment is localhost on Windows using XAMPP services. The PC may be powered off overnight; routine operation cannot depend on a developer, an open browser, an application login, or manual XAMPP startup. A successful workflow demonstration must be distinguishable from evidence of prediction usefulness.

## Solution

Make Demand Forecast the simple, action-focused starting point for the Administrator. Lead with three questions: Can we use forecasting today? What needs my action? Is it helping? Reuse the existing detailed pages for investigation, informed model approval, and recovery.

Show current Product coverage explicitly, name the role responsible for each action, and explain automatic recovery without asking staff to intervene unnecessarily. Keep technical metrics available beneath understandable explanations. Approval remains an informed local Administrator decision after fixed automated checks pass.

Deliver a dated, traceable operational evidence package demonstrating the actual pipeline and target Windows/XAMPP installation. Separately display prediction evidence from genuine completed Store outcomes, or Still collecting evidence when unavailable. Label test and demo evidence honestly. Forecasts and buying suggestions remain advisory.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want one forecasting starting page, so that I know where to begin without visiting every forecasting page.
2. As an Administrator, I want to see whether forecasts can guide buying today, so that I do not confuse historical results with current guidance.
3. As an Administrator, I want counts of Products using forecasts and Products using stock rules, so that partial availability is visible.
4. As an Administrator, I want to inspect the Products behind each coverage count, so that I can understand exclusions.
5. As an Administrator, I want each excluded Product to have a clear reason, so that I know whether evidence, approval, freshness, or recovery is needed.
6. As an Administrator, I want coverage totals independent of a Product search, so that searching does not misrepresent Store-wide readiness.
7. As an Administrator, I want the date covered by the latest usable results, so that I understand how recent the guidance is.
8. As an Administrator, I want the latest update attempt distinguished from usable saved results, so that one failed attempt does not misrepresent existing valid guidance.
9. As an Administrator, I want issues prioritized by their effect on current guidance, so that the most important work is easy to find.
10. As an Administrator, I want every issue to explain its effect and next step, so that I can act without interpreting technical errors.
11. As an Administrator, I want each action to name its responsible role, so that work goes to the correct person.
12. As an Administrator, I want automatic retries identified as requiring no action, so that I do not create duplicate work.
13. As an Administrator, I want exhausted recovery to explain when technical support is needed, so that I know when local action is insufficient.
14. As an Administrator, I want a clear no-action state, so that a healthy dashboard does not manufacture tasks.
15. As an Administrator, I want a model-review action to open the detailed review before approval, so that activation is an informed decision.
16. As an Administrator, I want the proposed model described in ordinary Store language, so that I understand what I am approving.
17. As an Administrator, I want covered and excluded Products listed before approval, so that I understand its scope.
18. As an Administrator, I want comparisons explained in units sold for a stated period, so that error measures have practical meaning.
19. As an Administrator, I want observation progress and remaining blockers explained, so that I know why approval is unavailable.
20. As an Administrator, I want to know what approval changes and what remains advisory, so that I do not mistake activation for a purchase or stock adjustment.
21. As an Administrator, I want to inspect supporting technical metrics when needed, so that explanations remain auditable without dominating the page.
22. As an Administrator, I want unqualified candidates blocked from approval, so that understandable UI does not weaken safeguards.
23. As an Administrator, I want to approve a qualified Store candidate locally without routine developer access, so that Store operation is self-sufficient.
24. As an Administrator, I want to reject a candidate without losing the approved model, so that review does not disrupt working guidance.
25. As an Administrator, I want to pause and resume forecast-backed guidance with clear consequences, so that I can manage operational concerns safely.
26. As an Administrator, I want compatible previous-model recovery explained and recorded, so that rollback is deliberate and attributable.
27. As an Administrator, I want a short performance summary, so that I can understand whether evidence supports continued use.
28. As an Administrator, I want Still collecting evidence when genuine Store outcomes are insufficient, so that missing evidence is not presented as success.
29. As an Administrator, I want overestimation and underestimation shown separately, so that opposite errors do not cancel into a reassuring average.
30. As an Administrator, I want performance tied to the evaluated model, Products, dates, and Forecast Horizon, so that unrelated results are not mixed.
31. As an Administrator, I want forecasts compared with the existing simple weekly comparison, so that complexity alone is not treated as improvement.
32. As an Administrator, I want stockout periods marked as incomplete demand evidence, so that lower recorded sales are not incorrectly treated as proven overestimation.
33. As an Administrator, I want recorded stockouts and expiry losses distinguished from forecast error, so that business outcomes are not confused with prediction metrics.
34. As an Administrator, I want demo and synthetic results clearly labelled, so that they cannot be mistaken for genuine Store performance.
35. As an Inventory Manager, I want to see whether each buying suggestion uses forecasts or stock rules, so that I understand its basis.
36. As an Inventory Manager, I want expected sales distinguished from suggested purchase quantities, so that I do not buy the forecast quantity blindly.
37. As an Inventory Manager, I want the same usability explanation available to me, so that using forecasts does not require generation or approval permission.
38. As an Inventory Manager, I want actionable stock-evidence issues linked to existing inventory work, so that I can correct records through the proper workflow.
39. As an Inventory Manager, I want stock receiving and counting to continue during forecasting work or failure, so that the model does not block Store activity.
40. As a Cashier, I want sales and refunds to continue during forecasting work or failure, so that customers can still be served.
41. As a Super Administrator, I want technical settings and diagnostics kept in the technical Workspace, so that operational users are not asked to manage algorithms or service internals.
42. As a Store owner, I want required XAMPP services and forecasting scheduling to start with Windows, so that staff need not launch them manually.
43. As a Store owner, I want background work to run without an interactive Windows sign-in, browser, or RetailMind login, so that routine execution is unattended.
44. As a Store owner, I want missed work recovered after the PC starts, so that powering off overnight does not permanently stop forecasting.
45. As a Store owner, I want restart and database-startup delays tested on the target installation, so that service configuration is demonstrated rather than assumed.
46. As a Store owner, I want identified history traced through an actual worker run to saved forecasts, so that queueing alone is not called success.
47. As a Store owner, I want displayed quantities checked against persisted output, so that the dashboard is proven to show the worker's results correctly.
48. As a Store owner, I want a real failure to trigger retries, notice, fallback, and recovery in an isolated acceptance copy, so that failure handling is demonstrated end to end.
49. As a Store owner, I want every acceptance scenario marked Passed, Failed, or Not tested with dated evidence, so that completion claims are reviewable.
50. As a Store owner, I want operational acceptance reported separately from prediction usefulness, so that the feature can be demonstrated before sufficient live outcomes accumulate.
51. As a keyboard or assistive-technology user, I want labelled controls, clear focus, and understandable status text, so that I can complete forecasting tasks accessibly.
52. As an Administrator using a narrow screen, I want actions and explanations to remain readable and usable, so that the dashboard does not depend on a wide monitor.

## Implementation Decisions

### Existing architecture and delivery boundary

- This is a follow-up to completed forecasting work, not a replacement forecasting engine. Reuse DemandForecastService, DemandHistoryService, StoreTrainingEligibilityService, CandidateEvaluationService, StoreModelGovernanceService, StoreActivationService, ForecastingSchedulerService, ReplenishmentQueueService, the existing job service, and role capability policy.
- Preserve the single asynchronous Random Forest pipeline, persisted results, supported 7/14/28-day Forecast Horizons, chronological qualification checks, approved-model identity, demo isolation, and Protected Audit Records. Follow ADR-0005 as modified by ADR-0022.
- Reuse Demand Forecast as the Administrator's forecasting landing surface and retain Data Readiness, Model Review & Approval, Forecast Exceptions, and Replenishment Recommendations as linked destinations. Avoid a parallel dashboard with independently computed status.
- Reconcile current source with prior completed work before editing; earlier documents contain stale implementation-status statements. No schema migration is presumed. Add persistence only if existing dated evidence cannot represent a required outcome, and document the necessity.
- Keep the user's current task limited to specification and publication. This issue describes subsequent implementation and verification; publication is not evidence that either has occurred.

### Dashboard structure and status contract

- First show today's forecast usability and full eligible Store Product coverage, then actions needing attention, then a brief performance summary. Define the Product denominator explicitly using the existing active replenishment Product scope. Compute coverage before optional search/filtering; filtered results must be labelled separately.
- Use one shared operational eligibility decision for dashboard counts, per-Product status, forecast display explanations, exceptions, and buying guidance. Reuse the replenishment eligibility boundary; do not reproduce a weaker freshness-only check in presentation code.
- Current guidance requires complete successful operational output, the approved compatible Store model, the accepted completed Philippine-day origin, supported Product evidence, and no suspension or observation-only restriction. Unavailable Products use existing stock rules and retain unknown expected sales rather than fabricated zeros. Explain products with no positive buy suggestion without implying stock rules always recommend a purchase.
- Distinguish current usability, latest attempt, and background activity. A pending job is not a completed forecast; a failed latest attempt does not invalidate still-eligible earlier output. Old output may remain dated history but must not be labelled usable for buying.
- Handle empty Store, insufficient history, no approved model, candidate observation, partial coverage, current coverage, stale or incomplete output, failed update, automatic retry, paused guidance, and recovery. Never label guidance Active solely because it is not paused.
- Example coverage wording is Forecasts available for 18 of 25 products; 7 use stock rules. Example retry wording is Forecast update failed. Buying suggestions are using stock rules. Automatic retry scheduled; no action needed. Render only conditions supported by actual state; these examples are not Store results.
- Each issue includes a plain-language condition, practical effect, responsible role or automatic action, and a working link to the existing next step. Put conditions affecting current guidance first, followed by available review actions and informational progress. Do not create speculative or duplicate warnings.
- Keep Store Calendar and Promotions in existing operational navigation with contextual links. Preserve technical forecasting pages for the Super Administrator. Use the app's existing tokens, components, theme support, accessible patterns, and responsive layout; no new UI framework or chart dependency is needed. Apply relevant installed design skills during implementation and verify rendered desktop/narrow-screen behavior.

### Review, roles, and actions

- The review action navigates to a business-first approval summary: Products covered/excluded, model comparison with units and periods, observation progress, passed checks and blockers, limitations, and the effect of activation. Put raw MAE, RMSE, WAPE, model identifiers, folds, and diagnostics in supporting details with explanations. WAPE is error, not an accuracy percentage.
- Preserve fixed automated gates and at least 28 usable completed prospective observation target dates. Preparing a candidate does not replace the approved model. Historical backtests do not substitute for prospective observation; synthetic elapsed days never authorize actual Store activation.
- Local Administrator approval, rejection, suspension/resumption, and compatible rollback use existing authenticated, CSRF-protected, audited actions. Revalidate eligibility on mutation. Do not add dashboard one-click activation or permit remote mutation.
- The Administrator owns operational review, calendar maintenance, approval, and exceptions. The Super Administrator owns imports, technical configuration, manual training, and maintenance. The Inventory Manager owns inventory execution and buying decisions; the Cashier records sales/refunds without forecasting management rights. Preserve active Workspace capability enforcement even for users assigned multiple roles.
- Provide read-only usability explanations to the Inventory Manager without granting generation or approval capability. Dashboard links never substitute for backend authorization.
- Forecast Quantity remains expected recorded sales in Base Units; Replenishment Recommendations account for stock and existing replenishment rules. Neither places an order nor changes inventory. Only existing operational workflows such as Stock Receiving change stock.

### Honest evidence and performance

- Maintain separate operational evidence and prediction-performance evidence. A passing job, a history-length readiness category, a screenshot, or a public-data benchmark is not measured Store prediction usefulness.
- Reuse candidate/forecast provenance and outcome evaluation. Show model identity, Product coverage, supported Forecast Horizon, evaluation dates, and usable comparison count. Compare dated forecasts made before the outcomes with subsequent genuine Store observations and the existing weekly comparison on matching eligible periods.
- Until existing evaluation prerequisites and genuinely usable outcomes support a claim, show Still collecting evidence with actual progress and reasons. Do not invent an accuracy target, replace existing gates, or introduce a new numeric sufficiency threshold. When performance belongs to a candidate or previous model, label that association rather than implying it describes the current approved model.
- Summarize overestimated and underestimated units separately at stated Product/horizon boundaries. Do not cancel signed errors into an accuracy claim or multiply overlapping forecast windows into apparently independent evidence. Missing or incomparable data stays unavailable.
- Stockouts, including positive sales before a sellout, leave unmet demand unknown. Preserve recorded sales but do not treat incomplete availability as proof of complete demand. Closures, unknown history, and imported evidence retain their established distinctions.
- Keep recorded stockouts and expiry losses separate from forecast errors. Reuse available verified operational evidence for these outcomes; show unavailable when absent. Do not claim forecasting caused fewer shortages or less waste without a valid comparison. Exact business tolerances remain deferred; existing qualification checks remain in force.
- Collected prices and promotion evidence do not establish active model inputs or improvement. Current model behavior must be described truthfully; new input experiments are not part of this issue.

### Windows/XAMPP acceptance

- Use the actual target Windows localhost/XAMPP configuration. Record installed PHP/Python executable selection, database configuration, service account/startup behavior, scheduler configuration, application revision, and model provenance without exposing credentials.
- Preserve accepted daily Forecast Generation at 01:00 and Sunday candidate training at 01:00, Asia/Manila. Verify effective settings and correct conflicting defaults without silently overriding an explicitly selected operational schedule. Verify latest-completed-day cutoff, current-only catch-up, deduplication, and the three-total-attempt policy.
- Verify automatic local service startup and job execution without interactive Windows sign-in, browser, application login, or manual XAMPP launch. The system cannot run while powered off; it must resume useful work after startup.
- Verify closure-aware accumulated history and observation continuity against the worker, including any stricter consecutive-observed-date generation checks. Fix contradictory prerequisites in shared logic rather than merely changing page labels. Keep 140 accumulated usable training records and existing chronological coverage requirements.
- Exercise destructive resets and failure injection only in isolated acceptance data/artifacts on the target software stack. Do not corrupt genuine Store history or promote synthetic candidates into production. Distinguish isolated target-stack demonstrations from genuine Store readiness.

## Testing Decisions

- The user approved the highest existing end-to-end boundary: identified Store history through the real queue and worker, persisted model/forecast output, authenticated pages, and Replenishment Recommendations. Prefer this boundary rather than adding parallel private test interfaces. Use focused existing service contracts only for failures or authorization cases that are impractical to exercise at that boundary.
- Prior art includes the Store forecasting operational workflow suite, Demand Forecast workflow browser fixtures, forecast decision/browser checks, forecast navigation and notices checks, scheduler/runner installation checks, and Store activation/recovery contracts. Extend or correct their behavioral assertions; source-string matching and simulated configuration assertions cannot establish installation acceptance.
- Test externally observable behavior: permitted/blocked actions, saved output, displayed quantities and explanations, usable coverage, fallback, actual notices, and recovery. Do not assert private methods, SQL spelling, chart internals, or model tree layout.
- Exercise the history reader, training eligibility, candidate evaluation, governance/activation, real worker persistence, replenishment eligibility, role authorization, and dashboard together. Seed minimum isolated history where necessary, then execute the actual pipeline rather than inserting a successful job or forecast as proof of completion.
- Demonstrate blocked unqualified approval and qualified local approval. Synthetic qualification/observation may support isolated workflow tests only and must be labelled; document genuine production qualification separately.
- Assert search-independent coverage, full/partial/no coverage, expired and incomplete forecasts, model replacement, observation-only results, pause/resume, compatible rollback, failed update with valid earlier output, and mismatched Product evidence. The dashboard and buying guidance must agree on the same Product/date/model.
- Inject an actual worker failure and observe retries, final job state, generated notification, stock-rule fallback, then successful recovery. Directly inserting the expected notification is not evidence that the failure path delivers it.
- Verify negative authorization paths for Cashier, Inventory Manager, remote access, and wrong active Workspace. Exercise successful local Administrator controls and prove read-only explanations do not require mutation permissions.
- Browser verification covers working action destinations, explicit approval review, keyboard navigation, labelled controls, visible focus, text-based statuses, existing light/dark themes, narrow-screen layout, empty/error/loading states, and no false success after queueing. Capture screenshots as supporting visual evidence alongside behavior assertions.
- On the target Windows/XAMPP installation, perform an actual restart without interactive sign-in and inspect independent service/job evidence afterward. Demonstrate database startup delay, missed daily/weekly catch-up, duplicate prevention, actual full worker completion, and continued sales/refund/receiving/count operations during forecasting activity. A simulated SYSTEM account setting is not an unattended boot test.
- Produce an acceptance matrix containing scenario, environment/revision, data provenance, expected result, observed result, Philippine timestamp, supporting run/model/forecast references and artifacts, and Passed/Failed/Not tested. Capture only evidence actually observed; record unavailable prerequisites or manual steps honestly.

| Acceptance scenario | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| History to candidate | Identified isolated source history, actual completed training/evaluation, saved compatible candidate |
| Qualification to approval | Blocked unqualified attempt, labelled observation evidence, authorized approval and audit attribution |
| Approval to forecasts | Actual worker execution and complete persisted 7/14/28-day output |
| Forecasts to dashboard | Displayed dates, quantities, model identity and coverage agree with saved output |
| Forecasts to buying guidance | Eligible Products use forecasts; excluded Products show truthful stock-rule basis |
| Failure to recovery | Injected failure, bounded attempts, generated notice, fallback and successful recovery |
| Windows/XAMPP startup | Actual unattended startup and catch-up supported by dated service/job evidence |
| Store non-disruption | Successful routine Store operations during forecasting work/failure |

- Separate the operational completion verdict from prediction usefulness. Do not declare target-installation acceptance complete while a mandatory operational scenario is Failed or Not tested. Insufficient genuine Store outcomes may leave prediction usefulness Still collecting evidence without preventing an honestly labelled isolated functional demonstration.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing the application or changing Windows services during specification/publication.
- A second forecasting engine, replacement model architecture, cloud deployment, multi-Store support, or a new dashboard framework.
- Automatic model activation, ordering, inventory adjustment, relaxed qualification, combined Workspace powers, or routine developer approval for qualified local activation.
- New price/promotion/stockout feature experiments, invented lost-demand quantities, new accuracy promises, or revised error thresholds without evidence.
- New causal business-benefit claims, a general expiry/stockout analytics subsystem, or waiting for months of outcomes before demonstrating isolated functional behavior.
- Destructive testing on genuine Store records, production use of synthetic observation evidence, or presenting demo performance as genuine Store performance.

## Further Notes

- Decisions synthesized on November 2, 2026, Asia/Manila. The user explicitly requested discussion followed by a specification and deferred implementation.
- This follows [the hands-off forecasting specification, issue #359](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/359). Related completed work includes [navigation #371](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/371), [unattended startup #363](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/363), [scheduler recovery #361](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/361), [candidate observation #367](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/367), [current purchasing guidance #369](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/369), [forecasting notices #382](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/382), and [Store Calendar #386](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/386). Their completion is prior art, not proof of target-installation acceptance.
- Static inspection found inconsistent current-forecast labels, an Active label derived solely from suspension, technical-first approval wording, a generation-window check needing closure-aware comparison, and a 23:00 daily default conflicting with accepted policy. Recheck these against the implementation revision before modifying them.
- No new runtime tests, unattended reboot, target deployment acceptance, or genuine Store performance measurement were performed while producing this spec. Existing reports must not be promoted to stronger claims without examining the underlying evidence.
title: Spec: Action-focused forecasting dashboard and Windows/XAMPP operational evidence

## What to build

An Inventory Manager can choose First useful tasks and follow walkthroughs on the existing replenishment needs, Product setup, and Stock Receiving pages. Staff learn the real stock workflows while all operational decisions and saves remain explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Help and the optional overview offer First useful tasks with replenishment needs, Product setup, and Stock Receiving topics. Other Inventory Manager Help capabilities remain available.
- [ ] Replenishment guidance explains buying suggestions, their basis and reasons, and their advisory nature. It never purchases goods or changes stock automatically.
- [ ] Product guidance uses the existing Product procedure and actual controls, including relevant Product details, counted opening stock, package sizes, and stock rules. It creates no practice or duplicate Products.
- [ ] Stock Receiving guidance uses the existing workflow to explain recording goods that actually arrived. Actual receipt saves remain explicit, and receiving is not described as customer demand history.
- [ ] All three topics provide the shared checklist, step counts, Back, Next, Exit, optional Learn more, continuation after navigation and login, replay, and Guidance finished.
- [ ] A multi-role account switching between Administrator and Inventory Manager sees only the active Workspace's topics and personal progress context. Accounts remain isolated; inaccessible destinations and forged or invalid-CSRF progress submissions are rejected independently of guidance visibility.
- [ ] Explanation-only navigation, Next, exit, replay, and completion do not create Products, receive stock, change stock, or confirm shared setup. Existing workflow saves, validation, and error feedback remain authoritative.
- [ ] All three topics remain usable with keyboard navigation, reduced motion, narrow screens, and supported themes.

## Verification boundary

Extend existing authenticated browser-to-HTTP acceptance workflows using disposable databases and existing onboarding, Help, Workspace switching, workflow, and theme fixtures. Test observable behavior and persisted outcomes, including unchanged operational records and setup confirmations during explanation-only navigation. Cover keyboard/focus, target usability, narrow screens, supported themes, and reduced motion; supplement behavior checks with rendered visual inspection where needed. Use existing workflow tests for explicit operational saves and validation; do not add a walkthrough test framework.

Follow ADR-0001 and ADR-0009: the active Workspace determines authority, linked pages retain their independent authorization, and guidance grants no additional capability. Reuse existing components, tokens, navigation, authentication, CSRF protections, and error feedback. No rebuilt operational forms, public API, analytics platform, or tutorial framework dependency.

body:
# Interactive Workspace onboarding

Status: scope and testing boundary confirmed for issue publication. Specification only; application implementation is not authorized by this task.

## Problem Statement

Administrator and Inventory Manager staff can find role-specific explanations in Help, but still need to connect those explanations to the controls used for real work. A tour of every feature would interrupt Store operations and overwhelm new staff.

A newly created Administrator needs personal orientation even when other staff have already completed shared Store setup. Current guidance suppression follows shared setup completion, so it can hide the invitation that this person needs. Staff also need to distinguish learning progress from operational records and shared setup confirmations.

## Solution

Extend existing Help and the optional first-visit overview with optional, task-focused walkthroughs on the existing workflow pages. Staff choose a topic, see one short explanation and highlighted control at a time, and use Back, Next, or Exit. They can continue later or replay through Help.

Provide Administrator paths for Get oriented and Daily oversight, and an Inventory Manager path for First useful tasks. Invite a new Administrator after Mandatory Password Change, independently of shared Store setup completion. Start guidance and Not now leave work unblocked, and automatic invitations do not repeat after a choice.

Walkthroughs accompany genuine work. Staff explicitly save or confirm every operational action. Existing configuration can be reviewed without creating duplicates. Personal completion reads Guidance finished and never confirms Store setup or claims an operational task was completed.

## User Stories

1. As a new Administrator, I want an invitation after Mandatory Password Change, so that I can learn my responsibilities once my account is ready.
2. As a new Administrator, I want an invitation even when shared Store setup is complete, so that another person's setup work does not hide my orientation.
3. As an Administrator, I want Start guidance on the invitation, so that I can begin orientation when ready.
4. As an Administrator, I want Not now on the invitation, so that I can start Store work immediately.
5. As a returning staff member, I want my invitation choice remembered, so that guidance does not repeatedly launch automatically.
6. As a staff member, I want to choose a task through Help, so that I can learn what I need at the time.
7. As a staff member, I want walkthrough access from the optional first-visit overview, so that I can move from orientation to a useful task.
8. As an Administrator, I want a Get oriented path, so that I can review the Store's operational configuration.
9. As an Administrator, I want Store Settings guidance, so that I can understand the settings within my authority.
10. As an Administrator, I want Register guidance, so that I can review or create named till records and receipt-width settings.
11. As an Administrator, I want Fiscal Period guidance, so that I can find and understand the existing period workflow.
12. As an Administrator, I want staff account guidance, so that I can create accounts using existing permitted procedures.
13. As an Administrator, I want Store calendar guidance, so that I can review trading days and closures.
14. As an Administrator, I want a Daily oversight path, so that I can learn the recurring review work for my Workspace.
15. As an Administrator, I want Needs Attention guidance, so that I can find operational exceptions requiring review.
16. As an Administrator, I want Store Reports guidance, so that I can inspect Store performance through existing reports.
17. As an Inventory Manager, I want a First useful tasks path, so that I can begin the core stock workflows.
18. As an Inventory Manager, I want replenishment guidance, so that I can review buying suggestions and their reasons.
19. As an Inventory Manager, I want Product setup guidance, so that I can use the existing Product procedure.
20. As an Inventory Manager, I want Stock Receiving guidance, so that I can record goods that actually arrived.
21. As a staff member with multiple roles, I want guidance to follow my active Workspace, so that suggested actions match my current authority.
22. As a staff member, I want guidance on the actual workflow page, so that I can connect explanations to real controls.
23. As a staff member, I want one action and one short explanation per step, so that I can focus on the next useful interaction.
24. As a staff member, I want optional Learn more, so that extra detail is available without overwhelming each step.
25. As a staff member, I want a spotlight around the current control, so that I can locate the relevant interaction.
26. As a staff member, I want gentle transitions and one attention pulse per appearing step, so that guidance draws attention without ongoing distraction.
27. As a staff member who prefers reduced motion, I want immediate static cues, so that I can follow the same instructions comfortably.
28. As a staff member, I want Back and Next, so that I can control the pace and revisit an explanation.
29. As a staff member, I want Exit at any step, so that guidance never traps me or blocks Store work.
30. As a staff member, I want step counts and a topic checklist, so that I can understand my learning progress.
31. As a returning staff member, I want Continue where you left off, so that I can resume after leaving a walkthrough.
32. As a staff member, I want replay through Help, so that I can refresh a previously learned task.
33. As a staff member, I want progress personal to my account and active Workspace, so that another person or role does not complete my learning.
34. As an Administrator, I want to review existing accounts, Registers, Fiscal Periods, and Store Settings, so that learning does not require duplicate setup.
35. As a staff member, I want every operational save and confirmation to remain my explicit action, so that guidance cannot create unintended records.
36. As a staff member, I want guidance to avoid practice records, so that Store data continues to represent real operations.
37. As a staff member, I want Guidance finished to acknowledge learning, so that completion does not imply that Store setup or operational work is complete.
38. As a staff member, I want other capabilities to remain available through Help, so that the first-release paths do not limit the rest of my Workspace.
39. As a keyboard user, I want reachable controls and predictable focus, so that I can operate and exit walkthroughs without a pointer.
40. As a staff member using a narrow screen or supported theme, I want readable guidance and visible highlighted controls, so that I can follow a task in my normal working conditions.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the authenticated Workspace shell, existing Help workflow catalogue, overview entry points, and existing permitted workflow pages. Reuse current design tokens, components, navigation, error feedback, and guidance conventions. Do not rebuild operational forms.
- Deliver exactly three first-release paths: Administrator Get oriented (Store Settings, Registers, Fiscal Periods, staff accounts, Store calendar); Administrator Daily oversight (Needs Attention, Store Reports); Inventory Manager First useful tasks (replenishment needs, Product setup, Stock Receiving). Other capabilities retain their Help access.
- Offer a new Administrator a nonblocking invitation after Mandatory Password Change and entry into the Administrator Workspace. Shared Store setup completion must not suppress this personal invitation. Start guidance begins the selected path; Not now dismisses it without repeated automatic launches. This explicitly revises the earlier shared-setup-based reminder policy for new Administrators.
- Keep personal invitation, walkthrough progress, and shared Store setup confirmations distinct. Reuse the existing account-and-Workspace guidance persistence boundary and extend it only as needed for continuation and topic progress. Preserve existing saved choices without silently re-enrolling existing users in an automatic tour.
- Persist personal progress across workflow navigation and later visits. Help offers Continue where you left off and replay. Switching Workspace changes the available topics and personal progress context; switching accounts must not expose another person's progress.
- Keep current overview completion distinct from completion of the new walkthrough topics. Finishing an overview alone must not imply completion of interactive guidance. Exact storage representation and migration mechanics remain implementation choices.
- Each step describes one action in concise language, highlights the relevant control, and may offer Learn more. Back, Next, and Exit remain under staff control. Navigation through explanations is not evidence that an operational save or setup confirmation occurred.
- Use gentle transitions, a spotlight, and one attention pulse when a step appears. Avoid looping animation. Honor reduced-motion preferences with immediate static cues and provide a brief completion checkmark with Guidance finished.
- Keep instructions and target controls usable on supported narrow screens and in supported light/dark themes. Provide keyboard access, visible focus, accessible step/status text, and predictable focus on entry and exit. Highlighting must not prevent the intended control interaction.
- Review existing configuration instead of requiring duplicate accounts, Registers, Fiscal Periods, or settings. Any changes remain optional, explicit, and subject to the existing workflow's validation and authorization.
- Guidance never submits operational forms, confirms shared setup, generates practice records, changes stock, or performs staff lifecycle actions automatically. Replenishment remains advisory and Stock Receiving records actual arrivals through the existing workflow.
- Enforce active Workspace permissions for every linked page and progress mutation using existing authentication and CSRF protections. Derive account and Workspace identity from the authenticated context. Walkthroughs grant no additional capability, consistent with ADR-0001 and ADR-0009.
- Register guidance covers named till records and receipt-width settings. Store Settings guidance stays within Administrator authority. Do not imply printer-driver installation, hardware setup, or access to Platform Settings.
- Account for the existing guidance data's participation in account lifecycle cleanup and backup identity reconciliation if persistence changes. Preserve those boundaries using current conventions rather than creating a second preferences system.
- No new public API, tutorial framework dependency, analytics system, or architecture decision is required by this specification. Select the smallest implementation that supports the agreed interactions.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed the primary seam: authenticated browser-to-HTTP acceptance workflows with disposable databases, extending the existing Workspace onboarding and Administrator workflow guidance browser harnesses. Use existing Help, Workspace switching, theme fixtures, and workflow coverage as prior art rather than adding a walkthrough test framework.
- Test externally observable behavior and persisted outcomes, not private helpers, exact DOM structure, animation implementation, or table layout. Cover the authenticated shell, Help, progress handling, invitation eligibility, and the existing operational destinations through this shared boundary.
- Create a new Administrator, exercise Mandatory Password Change, and verify the invitation is offered afterward with shared Store setup both incomplete and complete. It must not bypass the password requirement or block ordinary work.
- Exercise Start guidance and Not now, then navigate, refresh, and log in again. Choices must persist without repeated automatic launches; Help must remain available. Existing skipped, deferred, and completed overview choices must not be silently reset.
- Cover all three paths and their listed topics. Verify each destination is permitted in the active Workspace, including a multi-role account switching between Administrator and Inventory Manager, and ensure other accounts' progress remains separate.
- Exercise Back, Next, Exit, topic checklists, step counts, continuation after navigation and later login, replay, and Guidance finished. Overview completion and topic progress must remain distinguishable. Replay must not restart automatic invitations or change shared Store setup.
- With existing configuration, finish review guidance without creating duplicate records. Compare operational records and setup confirmations before and after explanation-only navigation, exit, replay, and completion; they must remain unchanged.
- Where staff choose genuine operational work, use existing workflow tests to verify explicit save/confirmation, validation, and errors remain authoritative. Next must never submit a form, create a Product, receive stock, create staff, or confirm setup.
- Reject invalid-CSRF and forged account/Workspace progress submissions without changing anyone's progress or operational data. Verify inaccessible workflow destinations remain inaccessible independently of guidance visibility.
- Verify keyboard navigation, focus entry/exit, reachable controls, spotlight target usability, narrow-screen layout, supported themes, reduced-motion static cues, and the absence of looping distraction. Use existing rendered browser inspection patterns; supplement automated behavior checks with visual inspection where needed.
- Run implementation checks only against isolated test data. This planning task does not run application tests or claim walkthrough behavior is implemented.

## Out of Scope

- Application implementation, deployment, live Store changes, or operational fixture creation during specification work.
- Mandatory training, quizzes, an every-feature tour, repeated automatic launches, or new setup requirements.
- Cashier or Super Administrator onboarding and changes to role authority.
- New or rebuilt Product, receiving, account, Register, Fiscal Period, Store Settings, Store calendar, reporting, or attention workflows.
- Automatic form submission, practice records, duplicate setup, automatic purchasing, and changes to shared setup confirmation rules.
- Printer-driver or hardware installation, Platform Settings guidance, forecasting model or replenishment calculation redesign, and operational alert suppression.
- A new analytics platform, general tutorial authoring product, or speculative configuration options.

## Further Notes

- Synthesized from the consolidated interactive Workspace onboarding discussion dated 2026-11-02, Asia/Manila, and the accepted role-onboarding specification. The discussion records accepted interaction and motion choices; this spec preserves them without another product interview.
- This feature extends earlier onboarding guidance. It changes the new Administrator invitation policy independently of shared Store setup completion while retaining personal guidance/shared setup separation and existing operational procedures.
- Inspection found existing role-specific Help explanations, persisted account-and-Workspace overview choices, and browser coverage. Those are reuse opportunities, not evidence that interactive walkthroughs or the revised invitation policy already exist.
- Publication with ready-for-agent organizes future implementation; it does not authorize application changes during this task. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes.
title: Interactive Workspace onboarding

## What to build

Inventory Managers receive goods and separately linked Replacement Stock with consistent unit conversion, new Stock Batches and atomic inventory/movement updates.

Architecture-deepening refactor: preserve current user workflows, validation, authorization, error handling and stored evidence. Follow accepted domain decisions, including ADR-0001, ADR-0005, ADR-0006, ADR-0013 and ADR-0022. Paper-width rules come from ADR-0006; ADR-0018 is tablet printer infrastructure and does not add printer work here. No schema changes, new frameworks/dependencies, UI restyling, training-algorithm changes or multi-store abstractions. Test with isolated fixtures, never live Store records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Delegate accepted-stock credits and new Stock Batch creation to Batch Inventory Ledger while preserving existing receiving validation, authorization and direct-receiving workflow.
- [ ] Convert Receiving Units using existing Units per Package into Base Units; retain sealed/loose form accounting, batch costs, expiration, receiving provenance and optional supplier/receipt details.
- [ ] Preserve excluded damaged quantities, partial/later Replacement Stock links and receiving history; new arrivals must not overwrite historical batches.
- [ ] Apply open Fiscal Period checks, ledger locking, movement evidence and stock-on-hand/batch-total equality within the existing receiving transaction.
- [ ] Multi-line receiving either commits all receiving records, batches, totals and movements or rolls back all of them; remove duplicated receiving mutations after callers migrate.
- [ ] Verify unit conversion, pack forms, damaged-stock exclusion, replacement links, locked periods and multi-line failure; run cross-workflow checks spanning receiving, Stock Issues, physical counts and Supplier Pullouts.
- [ ] Run the existing regression boundary for affected receipt, governance, financial, attention and inventory workflows after integration. Preserve compatibility with sales, Cash Refunds, Opening Batches and other stock writers without expanding their migration into this ticket.
title: Route Stock Receiving through ledger

title: Introduce Batch Inventory Ledger through Stock Issue approval

body:
# Remove the spurious Stock Issue Oversight access warning

## Problem Statement

An Administrator sees the unwanted message "Stock issue oversight is limited to Administrators, Inventory Managers, and Cashiers viewing their own reports." while using Stock Issue Oversight. This makes an intended Administrator responsibility appear forbidden and interrupts access to Store loss history.

The user confirmed that Administrators should retain read-only Stock Issue Oversight and requested removal of this specific warning.

## Solution

Allow an authorized Administrator to open and use Stock Issue Oversight without the quoted warning. Identify and correct the actual source of the warning rather than suppressing all authorization errors. Preserve the existing read-only responsibility and role boundaries.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want to open Stock Issue Oversight without an incorrect access warning, so that I can monitor Store losses confidently.
2. As an Administrator, I want direct navigation to work, so that bookmarked oversight links remain useful.
3. As an Administrator, I want sidebar navigation to work without the warning, so that routine monitoring is uninterrupted.
4. As an Administrator, I want to filter Stock Issue reports without the warning, so that I can investigate relevant history.
5. As an Administrator, I want to open report details without the warning, so that I can inspect actors, decisions, and linked corrections.
6. As a person using the Administrator Workspace through an additional assigned role, I want my active Workspace recognized, so that my permitted oversight works consistently.
7. As an Administrator, I want oversight to remain read-only, so that inventory decisions stay with the Inventory Manager.
8. As an Inventory Manager, I want existing report review and inventory decisions preserved, so that removing the warning does not disrupt my work.
9. As a Cashier, I want access to remain limited to my own Stock Issue reports, so that other staff reports remain protected.
10. As a Store operator, I want unauthorized access to remain denied, so that warning cleanup does not expand privileges.
11. As an Administrator, I want genuine loading failures and missing-report errors to remain visible, so that I can distinguish failures from an empty report list.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the Stock Issue service, Administrator oversight page, and existing Workspace authorization mechanisms.
- Trace the quoted exception through report listing, detail loading, active Workspace resolution, and navigation feedback before choosing the smallest complete fix.
- Current service inspection shows listing and detail authorization use a viewer role resolved from the account. Investigate its consistency with the active Workspace, especially for additional role assignments; this is a lead, not a confirmed cause.
- The existing browser alert test explicitly injects this message through an error query parameter. That test demonstrates feedback presentation, not that normal Administrator navigation reproduces the bug. Do not treat synthetic URL feedback as proof of a production authorization failure.
- Ensure authorized navigation does not generate or carry stale copies of this warning. Preserve unrelated query feedback and genuine error handling.
- Preserve ADR-0001 Store operational authority and ADR-0009 active Workspace boundaries. Assigned roles do not combine permissions.
- Preserve Administrator mutation denial, Inventory Manager decision authority, Cashier own-report scoping, immutable decisions, and linked correction history.
- No schema changes, new permissions, dependencies, or interface redesign are required.

## Testing Decisions

- Use the existing Stock Issue browser coverage as the primary external-behavior seam. The user confirmed this approach before publication.
- Verify successful report loading and absence of the quoted warning through direct and sidebar navigation, including filter and detail access.
- Cover an ordinary Administrator and an account with additional Administrator access operating in the Administrator Workspace, using isolated synthetic fixtures.
- Prefer visible report content and accessible page feedback assertions over source-text assertions or private-method tests.
- Extend or reuse existing Stock Issue oversight and Workspace authorization contracts to verify unauthorized access remains denied, Cashiers cannot view another Cashier's reports, and Administrators cannot mutate reports.
- Preserve coverage for genuine missing-report and loading errors. If the generic alert test still needs synthetic feedback, use a neutral message independent of this authorization regression.
- Prior art includes the existing Stock Issue alert browser test, oversight authorization contract, and Administrator mobile navigation coverage. Add no new testing seam unless existing coverage cannot reproduce the failure.

## Out of Scope

Removing Stock Issue Oversight, granting Administrator inventory mutation rights, granting Super Administrator Store operational authority, changing approval workflows, hiding all warnings, redesigning the page, altering notification thresholds, or changing historical Stock Issue data.

## Further Notes

The exact unwanted text is an authorization exception, not a standing informational banner. Establish a reproducer before implementation and document whether the trigger was role resolution, stale navigation feedback, or another confirmed cause. This spec requests correct authorized behavior, not deletion of the underlying security check.
title: Remove spurious Stock Issue Oversight warning for authorized Administrators

## Parent

#359

## What to build

Let staff maintain a regular Store opening schedule while completed Product sales automatically establish genuine special openings. Preserve dated, origin-known evidence without treating Store opening as proof of Product availability.

Reuse the existing calendar, history/export and authenticated workflow boundaries. Keep tests isolated from live Store records and preserve existing records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Let the local Administrator configure regular open/closed weekdays with effective dates and date-specific exceptions; exceptions override the weekly schedule.
- [ ] Preserve schedule and exception revisions, recorded timestamps, actor and source so later edits do not rewrite historical evidence or calendar inputs known at an earlier forecast origin.
- [ ] A completed Product sale automatically establishes Open on its Philippine business date, overriding both weekly and date-specific closure without confirmation. Show the sale provenance and preserve earlier calendar records.
- [ ] Support special and half-day weekend openings without requiring manual opening-hours entry. Open establishes that trading occurred, not a complete trading day or complete Product availability.
- [ ] Keep Product availability independent: one Product's sale cannot certify another Product's zero sales, and positive sales cannot erase stockout evidence. A scheduled open day alone certifies neither complete sales nor availability.
- [ ] Refunds, GCash services and unfinished transactions do not establish automatic opening; absent sales or PC downtime do not establish closure.
- [ ] Use the same cutoff-aware resolved calendar evidence in Store Calendar displays, demand-history/export consumers and forecasting. Retain unknown evidence rather than fabricating observations.
- [ ] Verify authenticated weekly-schedule and exception edits, weekday closure, completed weekend sale overriding closure, half-day trading, earlier cutoffs before the sale, later schedule changes and independent Product classifications through persisted and rendered behavior.
- [ ] Reuse Store Calendar and existing business workflows; preserve role/Workspace authorization, CSRF protection, accessibility and financial records. Keep calendar management in Store operations with contextual forecasting links.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Support weekly Store Calendar and sales-based opening evidence

# Delegate Store & receipts to the Administrator

Confirmed scope and testing approach, 2026-11-02 Philippine time.

## Problem Statement

The Administrator is responsible for Store operations but must currently depend on the Super Administrator to maintain Store identity and customer receipt settings. The Store & receipts section is grouped into Platform Settings with unrelated technical controls. This makes routine Store setup depend on platform-governance intervention.

## Solution

Move the complete Store & receipts function into Administrator Store Settings. The Administrator can view and save all nine existing fields without per-field Super Administrator approval. Keep existing operational attention thresholds available alongside this section. Separate platform functions remain under Super Administrator authority.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want Store & receipts in Store Settings, so that I can maintain the Store without platform-governance intervention.
2. As an Administrator, I want to update the Store name, so that future customer receipts identify the Store correctly.
3. As an Administrator, I want to update the TIN / Business identifier, so that I can maintain the Store's recorded business identification.
4. As an Administrator, I want to update the Store email, so that the recorded contact details remain current.
5. As an Administrator, I want to update the Contact number, so that customers receive current contact information.
6. As an Administrator, I want to update the Store address, so that future receipts show the current address.
7. As an Administrator, I want to update the Currency symbol, so that I can control the existing monetary display setting.
8. As an Administrator, I want access to the existing Timezone field, so that the complete Store & receipts function is available in my Workspace.
9. As an Administrator, I want to update the Expiry alert lead time, so that I can maintain the existing Store-wide expiry-warning setting.
10. As an Administrator, I want to update the Receipt footer, so that future receipts carry the Store's chosen message.
11. As an Administrator, I want all nine fields available without separate technical approval, so that delegated authority stays simple.
12. As an Administrator, I want current saved values displayed when I open Store Settings, so that I can review and amend the existing configuration.
13. As an Administrator, I want clear validation and save feedback, so that I know whether my changes were accepted.
14. As an Administrator, I want to save receipt settings independently of attention thresholds, so that one form does not overwrite another form's settings.
15. As an Administrator, I want existing operational threshold controls retained, so that delegation does not remove my current Store Settings functions.
16. As a Store operator, I want successful settings changes attributable to the acting user, so that Store configuration changes remain traceable.
17. As a customer, I want newly completed receipts to preserve the applicable Store details, so that later configuration changes do not rewrite my receipt.
18. As an Administrator, I want historical reprints to retain their existing preservation behavior and legacy notices, so that delegation does not undermine receipt history.
19. As a Super Administrator, I want dormancy policy, email testing, and other platform controls to retain their authorization, so that Store delegation does not grant technical governance.
20. As a multi-role user, I want Store settings changes to require the Administrator Workspace, so that assigned roles do not combine authority.
21. As a Store operator, I want unauthorized or forged requests rejected without settings changes, so that the permission boundary holds beyond the visible interface.

## Implementation Decisions

- The Administrator owns the entire existing Store & receipts section: Store name, TIN / Business identifier, Store email, Contact number, Store address, Currency symbol, Timezone, Expiry alert lead time, and Receipt footer.
- Move the section and its mutation responsibility from Platform Settings into Administrator Store Settings. Remove the former Super Administrator editing path for these fields rather than retaining duplicate forms. Under ADR-0001 and the Workspace model, a user with assigned Administrator access switches into that Workspace for Store mutations.
- Preserve the separate platform-governance gate. Do not grant the Administrator the general platform-governance capability. Dormancy policy, test-email dispatch, platform attention thresholds, safety limits, and other technical controls retain their existing authority.
- Audit both the current frontend handler and the legacy system-settings handler so neither retains an unintended Store-settings write path. Preserve unrelated platform actions in both entry points where applicable.
- Reuse the existing Store settings persistence and activity logging mechanisms. Retain existing keys and values; no schema migration, new role, approval workflow, or per-field permission system is required.
- Keep Store & receipts and attention thresholds independently dispatched and explicitly allowlisted. A submission for one section must not clear missing fields from the other section or write arbitrary Store or platform settings.
- Preserve authentication, active-Workspace checks, applicable remote-access and Store write restrictions, CSRF verification, server-side validation, output escaping, and safe failure handling. Retain required Store name, valid optional Store email, and valid optional IANA timezone checks; reuse existing field-specific validation where present.
- Preserve expiry-warning behavior and the existing serialized lead-time format. This work delegates the existing control rather than introducing a new warning policy or redesigning Product-level overrides.
- Record successful Store & receipts saves with the acting user's identity through existing activity logging. Do not report successful saves when persistence fails.
- Preserve modern Sale Receipt, Refund Receipt, and GCash Service Receipt snapshots. Changes apply to subsequently captured details; existing legacy reconstruction behavior and notices remain intact under ADR-0006.
- Preserve the Currency symbol field's current display-only behavior: changing it does not convert amounts or create multi-currency accounting.
- Preserve the Timezone field's current behavior: saving it does not change the runtime timezone, which currently comes from APP_TIMEZONE. Activating runtime timezone switching is outside this delegation.
- Update page descriptions and navigation references affected by the moved section, using existing accessible form and feedback patterns. Do not redesign unrelated settings screens.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed the test approach: exercise authenticated settings-page save requests, verify Workspace and platform authorization boundaries, and reuse existing receipt-history tests.
- Prefer one request-level integration flow through Administrator Store Settings using existing authenticated browser/request fixtures. Assert observable access, persisted values, validation feedback, and audit attribution rather than internal function structure or exact markup.
- Verify that an Administrator can load and save all nine fields, reload them, and save attention thresholds separately without cross-form data loss.
- Verify rejection without mutation for invalid required/name, email, and timezone inputs, missing/invalid CSRF tokens, unauthorized Workspaces, and forged submissions attempting platform actions or extra setting keys. Include the existing remote read-only boundary where the fixture supports it.
- Verify that Super Administrator platform actions remain available under their existing policy while Store & receipts writes require the Administrator Workspace, including any reachable legacy settings entry point.
- Reuse existing authenticated browser coverage for role-specific settings access and responsive settings pages; extend only the assertions affected by relocation.
- Reuse existing receipt attribution and sale, refund, and GCash integration coverage to verify transaction-time snapshots survive later settings edits. Preserve legacy receipt notices without inventing historical data.
- Reuse existing dormancy-policy authorization and Administrator alert contracts as regression coverage for the separated platform actions and retained attention thresholds. Do not add a parallel testing framework.

## Out of Scope

- Application implementation as part of writing or publishing this specification.
- Giving the Administrator general Platform Settings access, technical governance, dormancy-policy authority, or email-test authority.
- Per-field approval, a new permission editor, temporary delegation, new roles, or arbitrary privilege assignment.
- Runtime timezone switching, currency conversion, multi-currency accounting, new receipt layouts, or rewriting historical receipts.
- Changing expiry-warning policy, platform safety limits, operational attention-threshold policy, or remote-access policy.
- New schema, speculative abstractions, and unrelated settings redesign.

## Further Notes

The user explicitly chose the complete function for simplicity, superseding the initially proposed split that reserved TIN, Currency symbol, and Timezone for the Super Administrator. The user then confirmed the final scope before requesting this specification.

This follows ADR-0001's separation of Administrator Store operations and Super Administrator technical governance, and ADR-0006's receipt-preservation policy. Timezone's existing lack of runtime effect and Currency symbol's display-only behavior are known limitations retained by this scope.
title: Delegate the full Store & receipts function to Administrator Store Settings
