body:
# Administrator workflow alignment and accountable corrections

Specification synthesized on 2026-10-27 Philippine time from the confirmed Administrator workflow review through Q59. Test seams confirmed in this specification session. Publication organizes future implementation; this session does not authorize application implementation or live operations.

## Problem Statement

The Administrator needs to understand what requires attention, investigate the exact records, and direct unfinished work to the right person. Current workflows include dead-end alerts, misleading review labels, inconsistent cash thresholds, incomplete GCash follow-up, and unclear consequences for approvals, account changes, reporting, and recovery.

These ambiguities can make a reviewed shortage look recovered, a cancelled exchange look repaid, a closed session look like a settled customer obligation, or an approved correction look executed. Role bypasses and unclear financial measures further weaken accountability. The Store needs clear, consistent workflows that preserve original evidence and distinguish investigation, authorization, responsibility, and actual money or stock movement.

## Solution

Make Store Overview the Administrator's daily starting point for actionable Store-wide attention, with investigation and execution in their dedicated Workspaces. Give reviews explicit explanations and history, keep unsettled obligations visible across handover and closure, and require actual movement evidence before showing repayment or correction as complete.

Align supervisor approval, staff lifecycle, Fiscal Period guidance, GCash controls, refund corrections, reporting, settings, forecasts, and protected restore guidance with the accepted role boundaries. Preserve immutable records, original attribution, existing safeguards, and the single-Store model. Clearly identify unavailable information and the next permitted action.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want Store Overview to summarize Store-wide work requiring attention, so that I know where to start each day.
2. As an Administrator, I want one GCash attention row with separate unresolved-exchange and unreviewed-closing-difference counts, so that I can open the correct review tab.
3. As an Administrator, I want outstanding GCash counts to cover every date and Cashier independently of reporting filters, so that unfinished work cannot disappear behind my selection.
4. As an Administrator, I want the GCash attention row hidden only when both counts are zero and an unavailable state on failure, so that an unsuccessful load cannot imply all clear.
5. As an Administrator, I want GCash funds, fees, and activity kept in GCash Overview, so that Store Overview remains focused and Product sales remain distinct.
6. As an Administrator, I want a cash-variance alert to open its exact Cashier Shift even outside default report dates, so that I investigate the correct event.
7. As an Administrator, I want the Shift's Cashier, Register, dates, expected cash, counted cash, signed difference, and closing notes, so that I understand the shortage or excess.
8. As an Administrator, I want ordinary qualifying cash differences labelled Needs review, so that severity does not imply an unagreed emergency.
9. As an Administrator, I want to save investigation notes without clearing attention, so that work in progress remains visible.
10. As an Administrator, I want Mark reviewed to require an explanation and preserve reviewer identity and time, so that a finished investigation is accountable.
11. As an Administrator, I want to finish a review while explicitly recording money still missing, so that investigation completion does not falsely claim recovery.
12. As an Administrator, I want Reopen review to require a reason and retain previous conclusions, so that new evidence can restore pending attention without erasing history.
13. As an Administrator, I want Shift closure and Dashboard attention to use the same nonzero, inclusive cash threshold, so that the same difference receives the same treatment.
14. As an Administrator, I want threshold changes to affect future closures while preserving existing required reviews, so that changing a setting cannot dismiss unfinished investigations.
15. As an Administrator, I want small cash differences retained in Shift reports, so that differences below the attention threshold remain traceable.
16. As an Administrator, I want normal pending Stock Issues shown as Store status with Waiting for Inventory Manager, so that oversight is not mistaken for an approval task.
17. As an Administrator, I want overdue or high-value Stock Issues labelled Follow up with Inventory Manager, so that meaningful oversight remains visible without transferring inventory authority.
18. As an Administrator, I want size-only discount alerts and obsolete Legacy Reversal alerts removed, so that valid Promotions and retired workflows do not create false work.
19. As an Administrator, I want discounts and historical records preserved in receipts and reporting, so that alert cleanup does not erase evidence.
20. As an Administrator, I want Fiscal Period closure to list unfinished Shifts, GCash reconciliation, and pending Inventory Counts with permitted links, so that each responsible role can clear the actual blockers.
21. As an Administrator, I want closing confirmation to explain that new sales require a covering open period, so that closure consequences are clear.
22. As an Administrator, I want Open next period to suggest the following day as its start and require my chosen end date and confirmation, so that rollover remains deliberate.
23. As an Administrator, I want a properly counted and reconciled GCash session to close with an explicitly carried-forward customer obligation and responsible Cashier, so that custody closure need not falsely settle the exchange.
24. As a responsible Cashier, I want accepted GCash follow-up to survive Shift, session, and Fiscal Period closure, so that obligations remain accessible when I next work.
25. As an Administrator, I want Verify & Clear explained as confirmation of a completed exchange, so that I do not use it to dismiss a failed exchange.
26. As an Administrator, I want failed-exchange handling directed to the responsible Cashier's permitted workflow, so that cancellation stays with its authorized operator.
27. As an Administrator, I want completion evidence to identify who checked cash and wallet and what each found, so that accountable Cashier-supplied checks can support my confirmation.
28. As an Administrator, I want uncertain cash or wallet evidence to leave an exchange pending, so that expected system balances cannot substitute for proof.
29. As an Administrator, I want GCash Closing Difference Review to require both cash and wallet checks and explanations, so that an excess cannot conceal a shortage.
30. As an Administrator, I want the GCash action called Mark reviewed and original closing amounts retained, so that review is not confused with a cash adjustment or repayment.
31. As an Administrator, I want Emergency handover / Stop service exposed in GCash Overview with physical cash and wallet checks and a reason, so that abandoned custody can be handled safely.
32. As an Administrator, I want an eligible replacement Cashier to take custody or new exchanges to stop when no replacement exists, so that service does not continue without responsibility.
33. As an incoming Cashier, I want to see and explicitly accept individual unfinished exchanges, so that I know which follow-up work I accept.
34. As an Administrator, I want unaccepted exchanges labelled Needs a responsible Cashier, so that handover cannot hide unassigned obligations.
35. As a Cashier, I want original recorder and money attribution preserved through handover, so that follow-up responsibility does not assign blame for an earlier shortage.
36. As a responsible Cashier, I want failed exchanges to record actual partial returns and remaining amounts owed, so that cancellation finishes only after required returns are complete and checked.
37. As an authorized operator, I want correction choices to distinguish Fix a recording mistake from Record an actual money movement, so that the record reflects whether money moved now.
38. As an authorized operator, I want correction effects previewed and explained before confirmation, so that corrections are understandable and linked to their originals.
39. As a responsible Cashier, I want later actual returns recorded in my current open GCash session, so that closed-session cash counts remain historical evidence.
40. As an Administrator, I want mistakes discovered after closure corrected by linked records without overwriting entries or closing counts, so that the original evidence remains intact.
41. As a Cashier, I want Product-drawer funding limited to my own open drawer with its Register and amount shown, so that another person's drawer cannot become an implicit source.
42. As a responsible Cashier, I want one funding form to capture source, amount, Administrator approval, and my confirmation of actual receipt, so that approval alone cannot post unreceived funds.
43. As an Administrator, I want Money history to show additions, withdrawals, exchanges, returns, corrections, and their recording and approving people, so that I can trace service funds.
44. As an Administrator, I want recovered GCash shortages linked to the earlier review and today's approved receipt, so that recovered amounts are visible without changing the original shortage.
45. As an Administrator, I want one actual movement linked to every relevant exchange or discrepancy, so that the same cash is never counted twice.
46. As an Administrator, I want Fees charged, Fees returned, and Fees after returns shown separately, so that service fees are not overstated or presented as profit.
47. As an Administrator, I want explicit exchange-linked fee returns dated when actually returned, so that arbitrary corrections do not masquerade as fee returns.
48. As an Administrator, I want completed GCash activity and charged fees dated on completion, so that a later-completed exchange belongs to its actual completion period.
49. As an Administrator, I want unfinished and cancelled history dated by start date with clear labels, so that mixed-status history has an honest date basis.
50. As an Administrator, I want display, filters, sorting, pagination, and exchange CSV to share that date rule, so that exported and visible records agree.
51. As a Cashier requesting supervisor approval, I want the approving Administrator to use Username or Email Address plus password, so that approval follows ordinary Login Identifier rules.
52. As a person assigned Cashier and Administrator access, I want to approve my own eligible action using my Administrator credentials, so that a second person or account is not artificially required.
53. As an Administrator approving on a Cashier screen, I want approval limited to that action with the required reason and attribution, so that it creates neither combined Workspace permissions nor a lasting approval session.
54. As a Store owner, I want technical-account status alone excluded from business supervisor approval, so that operational approvals require eligible Administrator assignment.
55. As a Cashier refunding another Cashier's sale, I want separate receipt-access and exact-amount refund approvals, so that permission to inspect a sale is not payment authority.
56. As a Cashier, I want different eligible Administrators permitted for those two approvals, so that the final approval remains independent without an unnecessary identity-match restriction.
57. As an Administrator, I want to open and approve a Refund Correction Review while preserving the original sale and refund, so that mistakes can be corrected accountably.
58. As a Cashier, I want actual refund money corrections performed through permitted Shift controls, so that review approval cannot fabricate repayment.
59. As an Inventory Manager, I want any required refund stock correction handled separately through my permitted workflow, so that financial approval does not imply stock execution.
60. As an Administrator, I want Reviewed—correction outstanding while money or stock tasks remain and Corrected only after completion, so that investigation and execution have truthful statuses.
61. As a multi-role staff member, I want the active Workspace to govern business actions, so that assigned roles never silently combine permissions.
62. As a Super Administrator, I want Store oversight read-only and operational actions to require the corresponding assigned Workspace, so that technical governance does not become a business bypass.
63. As an Administrator, I want routine staff lifecycle actions in my Workspace under existing protections, so that Store staffing remains operationally managed.
64. As a Super Administrator, I want ordinary-user management limited to creating ordinary Administrators and disabling ordinary accounts with Administrator access, so that technical user management stays narrowly defined.
65. As an Administrator, I want immediate protected disablement even when staff have unfinished cash duties, so that removing access does not wait for operational cleanup.
66. As an Administrator, I want unfinished duties and permitted handover links retained after disablement, so that access revocation never pretends to reconcile cash.
67. As an Administrator, I want role removal to withdraw the Workspace and revoke sessions immediately, so that removed authority cannot persist in an existing session.
68. As an Administrator, I want password reset and Revoke Sessions explained distinctly from disablement and cash closure, so that I understand each action's consequences.
69. As an Administrator closing an abandoned Cashier Shift, I want to cancel its unpaid Held Sales with a reason and original saver/canceller attribution, so that closure can finish without inventing a sale or cash movement.
70. As an Administrator, I want ordinary staff lifecycle history with actor and time in Operational Audit, so that I can investigate staffing changes without seeing passwords or technical-account security records.
71. As an Administrator, I want Promotion copy to distinguish enabled from currently eligible and describe explicit Cashier selection, so that no automatic or highest-discount behavior is promised.
72. As an Administrator, I want Register disabling explained as blocking new Shifts while preserving existing Shifts, so that it is not mistaken for a shutdown action.
73. As an Administrator, I want Calendar Closed/Holiday classifications explained as Store and forecast context, so that they are not mistaken for checkout or Shift-closing controls.
74. As an Administrator, I want every retained Store Setting to explain its actual effect and ineffective controls removed, so that configuration is meaningful.
75. As an Administrator, I want Low Stock and Inventory Value labelled Current stock with ineffective historical controls hidden, so that reports do not imply unavailable historical reconstruction.
76. As an Administrator, I want Expiration reports to disclose their actual Today-based scope, so that selected dates are not falsely presented as applied.
77. As an Administrator, I want Stock Value based on remaining batch quantities and recorded purchase costs, so that a new Product cost does not reprice old stock.
78. As an Administrator, I want Recorded value, Estimated value, and Cost missing quantities separated, so that incomplete costing cannot appear exact or complete.
79. As an Administrator, I want explicitly recorded zero purchase cost distinguished from default zero catalog cost and quantity mismatches flagged, so that unreliable quantities and unknown costs are not concealed.
80. As an Administrator, I want the valuation column labelled Price minus cost per item and earned Gross Profit kept separate, so that a price margin is not presented as realized earnings.
81. As an Inventory Manager, I want permitted inventory and demand reports without staff sales performance, financial refund reports, or Gross Profit, so that report access matches my role.
82. As an Administrator, I want sales-period refunds counted on refund issue/payment date with original-sale links, so that sales and later refunds appear in their actual periods.
83. As a report user, I want Print / Save as PDF to describe browser printing honestly, so that duplicate controls do not imply a separate generator.
84. As an Administrator, I want operational forecasts, readiness, origin, age, and generation status with ready, updating, old, and unavailable states, so that I can judge operational usefulness.
85. As a Super Administrator, I want technical model scores, tests, training, configuration, approval, and rollback kept in technical governance, so that operational reporting does not imply model-maintenance authority.
86. As an Administrator, I want unavailable forecast confidence shown honestly and Product counts to count distinct Products, so that missing evidence and daily rows are not misrepresented.
87. As an Administrator restoring the Store, I want the current protected restore stage and next action, so that waiting for technical approval and verification requirements are understandable.
88. As an authorized Administrator, I want to take over verification and reopening using my own password if the initiator is unavailable, so that recovery can finish without bypassing safeguards.
89. As a remote-monitoring owner, I want the independent read-only remote boundary preserved even when I hold Administrator access, so that local operational permissions do not authorize remote changes.
90. As a staff member, I want failures, permission links, CSV exports, and refresh states handled safely and accessibly, so that unavailable data, raw errors, or stale results cannot mislead me or expose restricted information.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing StoreOperationsDashboardWorkspace, Attention services, CashierShiftService, StoreShiftReportService, GCashTransactionService, CashRefundService, RefundExceptionService, FiscalPeriodGuardService, authorization policy/context, ProtectedAuditRecordService, reporting services, and protected backup/recovery components. Extend current application and request boundaries; do not add a parallel workflow engine, shared test facade, or dependency.
- Reach affected callers, UI, routes, service queries, notifications, cached attention aggregates, filters, exports, settings consumers, fixtures, and schema support. A hidden button is insufficient authorization. Preserve validation, CSRF protection, appropriate authentication-abuse controls, Store write gates, and existing transaction/error handling. Implementation must inspect every affected caller before changing a shared contract.
- Store Overview receives one GCash Needs attention row with distinct unresolved-exchange and unreviewed-closing-difference counts and tab-specific destinations. Its counts are Store-wide across all dates/Cashiers; report filters must not narrow them. Hide only when both are known zero. Preserve honest loading/failure states and refresh after successful actions. GCash balances, fees, and activity stay in GCash Overview and outside Product sales measures.
- Cash variance attention must carry the exact Shift identity into the review destination, independent of default date filters. Show Cashier, Register, open/close dates, expected and counted cash, signed difference, and closing notes. Explain negative as short and positive as extra. Use Needs review for ordinary qualifying differences; no new Critical conditions are defined.
- Apply a shared closure rule: a nonzero difference requires review when its absolute amount equals or exceeds the configured Store limit. Retain smaller differences in reports. PHP 100 is an example, not a selected limit. Persist the threshold and reason applicable at closure so Store/platform limit changes affect future closures without clearing previously required reviews.
- Save investigation notes independently of completion and preserve them alongside the final explanation. Mark reviewed requires a finished investigation, explanation, reviewer, and time; it removes pending attention while retaining original amounts and all history. Explicitly record any remaining shortage. Review is not recovery, debt assignment, a cash adjustment, or permission for wage deduction. Reopen review requires a reason, restores attention, and preserves all earlier notes, reviewers, times, and conclusions. Apply reopening to the cash-review workflows covered by the confirmed decision without inventing a general reopening mechanism for unrelated records.
- Remove size-only Unusual discount attention, related exception/comparison counts, notifications, and obsolete settings/references. Preserve Promotion discounts and manual/legacy discount history in receipts/reports; absent Promotion attribution is not proof of wrongdoing. Remove Legacy Reversal alerts, retired-tab links, and related exception counts without deleting underlying records or recreating reversal UI. No historical migration/review workflow is required for this development cleanup.
- Normal pending Stock Issues belong in Store status with Waiting for Inventory Manager and their count. Retain existing configured overdue/high-value oversight alerts labelled Follow up with Inventory Manager. Administrator oversight stays read-only; the Inventory Manager decides inventory effects. Verify consumers before removing persisted settings, remove ineffective controls rather than manufacturing behavior, and explain each remaining control's actual effect while retaining unrelated validation.
- Reuse the accepted Fiscal Period lifecycle and commit-time safeguards. Present open Shifts, open/unreconciled GCash sessions, and in-period pending Inventory Counts as actionable blockers with role-correct links. Preserve all other prerequisites. Closing confirmation explains that new sales need a covering open period; after closing offer Open next period starting the next day, with an Administrator-selected end date and explicit confirmation. Never roll periods automatically.
- Clarify that GCash custody reconciliation differs from exchange settlement. An unsettled exchange may survive Fiscal Period closure only when physical cash/wallet have been counted and checked, the session otherwise closes properly, and the obligation is explicitly carried forward with a responsible Cashier. Preserve original period/session attribution, pending state, and owed amount. Determine current obligations from linked exchange state rather than freezing an old carryover count as permanent truth. A shortage alone does not establish a person's debt.
- Accepted follow-up responsibility survives Shift/session/period closure without keeping custody open. Preserve snapshot/count-only session closure when money posting is blocked. Later actual money or stock movements still require a valid covering open period and the responsible operator's eligible Shift/session; use the existing controlled amendment of an open period's end date when needed. Do not silently backdate later payments or relax fiscal protection.
- Verify & Clear confirms completed exchange evidence and posts only applicable remaining movements; it is not dismissal. Failed handling remains in the responsible Cashier workflow, reachable by eligible assigned Workspace switching. Administrator cancellation authority is not added. Completion may rely on responsible Cashier checks recording who checked cash/wallet and what each found, with Administrator accountability and existing confirmations. Either uncertain part keeps the exchange pending; expected balances alone are insufficient.
- Rename the GCash discrepancy user action Waive to Mark reviewed while preserving existing accountable approval and audit behavior. Require both cash and wallet differences to be checked and explained before completion. Never offset one against the other. Retain original counts, signed differences, earlier history, and the distinction between reviewed and recovered funds. Internal compatibility decisions must not rewrite old evidence merely to rename the action.
- Expose Administrator Emergency handover / Stop service using existing eligible-Shift custody controls, physical cash count, wallet check, and a required reason. With an eligible replacement, hand over custody; without one, safely stop new exchanges. Neither completes pending exchanges nor removes shortages. Incoming Cashiers explicitly accept individual unfinished exchanges; record acceptance, preserve the original recorder/movements, and expose unaccepted work as Needs a responsible Cashier. Responsible-Cashier follow-up must remain reachable beyond original-recorder/session filters.
- Replace cancellation's assumed automatic offset with actual return tracking. Record partial returns, required remaining cash/wallet/fee obligations as applicable, evidence, approvals, and responsible Cashier; leave failed exchanges pending until all required returns are actually completed and checked. Clicking Cancel is not evidence of movement. Preserve the original exchange and return history and prevent duplicate posting on repeated or competing confirmations.
- Corrections distinguish Fix a recording mistake (no money moved now) from Record an actual money movement. Preview effects, require an explanation, link to the original, and preserve applicable supervisor approval. Neither action initiates a GCash-app transfer. Historical recording corrections preserve original entries and closing counts and must not masquerade as present-day money. Actual later receipts/returns use the responsible Cashier's current open session and effective date; require opening an eligible session if none exists.
- Limit Product-drawer funding to the recording Cashier's own open drawer. Preview its specific Register/drawer and amount before approval. Funding uses one joint form capturing source, amount, eligible Administrator approval, and responsible Cashier confirmation that funds were actually received; post only after all are confirmed. Self-approval/receipt confirmation is allowed for a person assigned both roles. No cross-drawer transfer or pending funding-request subsystem is authorized.
- Add Money history within GCash Overview for additions, withdrawals, exchanges, returns, and corrections, including recording/approving actors and links. Clearly distinguish actual movements from recording corrections. Later recovery of an earlier reviewed shortage is an approved actual receipt in today's open session linked to the earlier review; retain original shortage and show later recovered amounts. A movement linked to both an exchange and discrepancy is counted once with multiple traceable links.
- Show Fees charged, Fees returned, and Fees after returns separately. Returns are explicit exchange-linked records, never inferred from arbitrary cash/wallet corrections. Charge fees on completion date and returns on actual-return date; the selected-period difference may be negative and must not be clamped. These are service-fee measures, not profit after expenses.
- Completed GCash activity and completed history use actual completion date. Unfinished/cancelled history uses start date with clear labels. Apply the effective date consistently to filtering, display, ordering, pagination, and the existing complete filtered exchange CSV. Retain start/completion dates in details where available; do not invent historical cancellation times or classify legacy reference-only review as completed exchange money. Preserve other existing shared/local filter scopes. Label the CSV exchange-only; Money history does not authorize a complete-ledger export.
- Supervisor approval uses the existing Login Identifier rules: Username or Email Address plus password. Require an enabled eligible ordinary Administrator assignment, including additional access, and preserve account/password-state checks, per-action limits, required reasons, audit attribution, and appropriate abuse protections. A dual-role person may approve their own eligible action. Record both Cashier and approving Administrator even when the same person. Super Administrator credentials alone are ineligible. Do not retain passwords between prompts, log in or switch the approver's session, grant general access, or create reusable approval sessions.
- Apply those common supervisor rules to drawer operations, applicable GCash actions, and exceptional refunds. The Cashier still records the operation on the Cashier screen; the credential prompt is a narrow approval exception to active-Workspace separation. Exceptional refunds retain two distinct approvals: access to that receipt, then fresh approval of the displayed selected-item/quantity refund amount. Preserve single-sale/Cashier/Shift binding, expiry, and existing own-sale behavior without supervisor credentials. Different eligible Administrators may approve the two stages; remove the same-approver requirement without weakening final authorization.
- Refund Correction Review preserves the original sale/refund and records the mistake, Administrator review/approval, and explicit required/completed correction steps. The Cashier executes actual money corrections through permitted Shift controls; the Inventory Manager executes separate stock corrections. A finished investigation may say Reviewed—correction outstanding, with remaining tasks visible to responsible roles. Only completed required corrections justify Corrected. Review approval itself moves neither money nor stock.
- Enforce the active Workspace in backend actions, routes, and visible controls. The Super Administrator Workspace provides read-only Store oversight, including GCash; operational mutations require the corresponding role already assigned and active. Technical identity is not an operational bypass. Preserve explicit shared Database Backup capability, protected Administrator restore, and technical model-maintenance authority. Independently preserve ADR-0019's read-only remote restrictions, including remote approvals, backups, and bulk exports.
- Ordinary staff lifecycle remains in the Administrator Workspace with fixed Administrator/Cashier/Inventory Manager assignments and existing protected-identity, self-action, password, and last-active-Administrator rules. Super Administrator ordinary-user authority is limited to creating ordinary Administrator accounts and disabling ordinary accounts with Administrator access; it grants no general Cashier-only/Inventory-Manager-only management, staff profile/password editing, arbitrary role assignment, or inferred re-enable permission. Preserve technical self-account security and Recovery Account boundaries.
- Permit immediate account disablement under existing self/last-Administrator protections despite unfinished cash work; revoke access and expose pending duties with permitted intervention links. Never auto-close/reconcile work. Role removal immediately withdraws its Workspace and revokes sessions while preserving unfinished duties. Explain whole-account/multi-role consequences. Revoke Sessions signs out current sessions and permits later eligible sign-in; password reset, session revocation, disablement, and operational closure remain distinct.
- During Administrator closure of an abandoned Shift, allow cancellation only of that Shift's unfinished unpaid Held Sales with a required reason and saver/canceller attribution. It creates no sale, refund, or cash movement and does not grant general access to operate another Cashier's carts.
- Operational Audit includes ordinary staff lifecycle events, including ordinary Administrators: creation, profile/role changes, enable/disable, and password-reset events, with actor/time and no passwords. Preserve technical-account security restrictions, Protected Audit Record immutability, and the same visibility scope in details, search, and exports. No audit editing/deletion is introduced.
- Promotion labels distinguish enabled from currently eligible. Describe explicit Cashier selection, not automatic or highest-discount selection, without adding edit/delete features. Register disabling blocks new Shifts and does not close/lock an existing one. Calendar Closed/Holiday describes Store/forecast context and does not gate checkout or close Shifts; retain Holiday's closed-trading-day forecasting meaning and use Open when trading on a holiday.
- Label Low Stock and Inventory Value Current stock and hide ineffective historical controls. Expiration reports disclose their actual Today-based scope rather than implying selected dates apply. Do not reconstruct historical inventory. Rename valuation's per-unit Profit column Price minus cost per item and preserve earned Gross Profit as a separate measure.
- Stock Value uses remaining batch quantities and recorded purchase costs, not latest Product cost for all units: ten units at PHP 5 plus ten at PHP 6 have Recorded Stock Value PHP 110. For missing purchase costs only, a usable positive current Product cost may supply an explicitly identified estimate. Show Recorded value, Estimated value, and quantities with Cost missing separately; label combined recorded-plus-estimated totals honestly and never present partial sums as complete exact value. Explicitly recorded zero batch/receiving cost is known zero; default zero catalog cost does not establish free goods. Flag stock-total/batch mismatches instead of estimating over unreliable quantities. Trace costing consumers without changing unrelated Gross Profit costing semantics.
- Inventory Manager reports are limited to inventory-related stock, receiving, expiry, inventory value, and permitted demand information. Exclude Sales by Cashier/staff financial performance, financial refund reports, and Gross Profit, including direct/export access. Preserve permitted receipt lookup for inventory work without extending it to full financial-report access.
- Align sales-report refunds with refund issue/payment date, consistent with Dashboard/Gross Profit. An October sale refunded in November retains October sales and records November refund effects, with the original-sale link. Preserve authoritative Gross Sales, Discounts, Refunds, Net Sales, and Gross Profit definitions; do not silently group normal period refunds by original sale date. Replace duplicate browser-print controls with Print / Save as PDF using the existing browser feature.
- Administrator forecasts expose operational results, readiness, origin/age, and generation status, distinguishing ready, updating, old, and unavailable. Ordinary Store forecast generation follows Administrator operational authority; preserve permitted Inventory Manager demand access. Technical training/testing/comparison scores, configuration, approval, and rollback remain with Super Administrator. Do not add a replacement misleading forecast-versus-sales comparison. Show unavailable confidence as unavailable rather than zero and count distinct Products where labels say Products.
- Protected restore guidance shows durable current stage and next action, including waiting for technical approval, ready to restore, verification needed, and actionable failure/recovery states. Preserve approved encrypted-package/passphrase, destination protection, Identity Reconciliation/Reconciliation Approval, safety-copy, replacement warning, write pause, automated/human verification, and explicit reopening requirements. Another authorized Administrator may take over finishing checks/reopening using their own verified password, with takeover attribution and all prerequisites intact; never reopen automatically or infer bypass authority from account availability.
- Retain accessible labels, keyboard/dialog behavior, existing mobile layouts, formula-safe complete filtered CSV, accurate role-specific links, safe Operator Alerts, and failure-safe data states. Do not expose raw internal errors in Store-facing failures or turn missing data into zero/all clear. Preserve request freshness behavior so stale responses cannot replace newer selections. Detailed diagnostics remain in existing protected logs as applicable.
- Persist only the additional review history, closure-threshold evidence, responsibility acceptance, actual-return/correction links, fee-return attribution, refund task evidence, and recovery takeover evidence needed to satisfy these behaviors, extending existing records where practical. Exact schema and route shapes are implementation choices, not a license for parallel ledgers or destructive historical rewrites. Maintain atomic posting and existing concurrency protections across affected entry points.

## Testing Decisions

- User-confirmed seams: existing workflow/service entry points against disposable databases, HTTP/request checks for permissions and forged requests, and focused browser checks of changed screens. Prefer the highest existing seam that exercises the behavior. Add no shared facade, test framework, production-only test interface, or live Store fixture.
- Good tests exercise externally visible results: returned/rendered data, persisted balances/stock, immutable originals, review/task states, actor/time attribution, notifications, CSV contents, and unchanged state after refusal. Avoid assertions about private helpers, incidental CSS, SQL text, or implementation source strings.
- Prior art includes Administrator Dashboard workspace/route/browser tests; GCash transaction integration, Administrator approval contract, and overview/browser coverage; Cashier Shift reconciliation and Held Sale contracts; Cash Refund contract/concurrency and safe-refund browser tests; audit visibility integration; staff minimum/management and Workspace-switching tests; Gross Profit historical-cost/reporting and inventory export tests; and recovery authentication/restart/reopening integration/browser suites. Reuse their existing disposable fixtures and application boundaries; update obsolete expectations rather than preserve retired behavior for tests.
- Cash review: exercise positive/negative/zero differences and below/equal/above limits, including a zero limit with zero difference, exact-Shift deep links outside dates, independent draft notes, required final explanations, missing-money conclusions, review reopening/history, threshold increases/decreases, and unchanged closing evidence. Required reviews must remain pending after later Store/platform limit changes.
- Attention: exercise global GCash counts outside selected date/Cashier filters, hide-on-known-zero, unavailable and partial-failure states, post-action refresh, normal versus overdue/high-value Stock Issues, correct role destinations, and complete removal of discount/reversal alerts, notification producers, obsolete counts, and settings consumers without lost underlying history.
- GCash custody/follow-up: cover replacement and no-replacement emergency outcomes, eligibility failures, cash/wallet checks, individual acceptance/refusal, unassigned items, original attribution, responsible-Cashier access after session/Shift/period closure, and disappearance of settled obligations from current pending totals without altering historical carryover evidence.
- GCash money: cover partial and complete returns, uncertain completion evidence, independent cash/wallet differences, no automatic cancellation offsets, repeated/concurrent submissions, current-session requirements, absent-session refusal, historical no-movement corrections, approved funding with actual-receipt confirmation, own-drawer restrictions, shortage recovery, and one movement linked to multiple records without double counting. Refused actions must leave money/history unchanged.
- Dates/fees: use exchanges started and completed on different Philippine dates/months, pending/cancelled/legacy records, mixed Cashiers, partial fee returns in later periods, negative Fees after returns, consistent effective-date list/order/pagination/CSV, and retained original dates. Verify all matching export pages, formula-injection protection, and honest exchange-only labels.
- Supervisor/refunds: test Username and Email Address, primary/additional Administrator assignment, allowed self-approval, technical-only rejection, disabled/invalid/password-state accounts, abuse protections, required reasons, and no approver-session mutation or retained password. Cover separate receipt and exact-amount approvals by the same/different eligible Administrators, expiry/binding/amount tampering, and unchanged own-sale behavior. Test Refund Correction Review with money-only, stock-only, and combined tasks, Reviewed—correction outstanding, role-specific execution, actual completion, and preserved originals.
- Roles/staff/audit: call forbidden backend routes directly from every relevant active Workspace and remote context, including users with additional assignments. Exercise narrow Super Administrator create/disable authority, immediate disablement with unfinished duties, self/last-Administrator protections, role-removal revocation, abandoned-Shift Held Sale cancellation scope, and ordinary lifecycle audit visibility across lists/details/search/exports without technical security leakage.
- Fiscal lifecycle: exercise each closure blocker and actionable destination, counted/reconciled sessions carrying unresolved obligations with accepted responsibility, refusal without that responsibility or reconciliation, next-period dates and explicit confirmation, posting-blocked count-only closure, permitted open-end-date amendment, and later movements in a valid new Shift/session/period. Preserve existing commit-time concurrency tests and no partial effects on failure.
- Reports/forecasts/settings: verify recorded batch values with the PHP 110 example, positive estimates, explicit zero versus default zero, missing costs, partial totals, and quantity mismatches; truthful Current stock/Today labels; refund-date monthly totals; Inventory Manager direct/export refusals; browser Print / Save as PDF; accurate setting effects; Calendar/Register/Promotion explanations; distinct Product counts; and unavailable confidence/status without fabricated numbers or technical-tool exposure.
- Recovery: use isolated disposable installations and retained recovery fixtures for stage/next-action guidance, technical approval waiting, invalid/stale approval, failed verification, initiator unavailability, authenticated authorized-Administrator takeover, audit attribution, and explicit reopening. Reopening must remain blocked until all original protection/verification conditions pass; wrong passwords and unauthorized takeover must change nothing.
- Focus browser smoke checks on exact-record navigation, accessible prompts, review/task status, emergency handover, responsible-Cashier follow-up, truthful report/filter labels, role links, recovery guidance, and load/error/refresh behavior at existing desktop/mobile sizes. No real GCash transfer, live wallet, destructive Store restore, or production data repair is needed.

## Out of Scope

- Application implementation, live database changes, production deployment, real money transfers, and live restore/migration during this specification session.
- New Critical cash conditions, Stock Issue thresholds/escalation policy, replacement discount detection, or historical migration/deletion for retired development alerts.
- Combined Workspace authority, technical-account business bypasses, extra Super Administrator lifecycle permissions, second-person approval requirements, or Administrator failed-exchange cancellation authority.
- Cross-drawer funding, a pending funding-request subsystem, a full-ledger export, GCash-app transfer integration, new fee schedules, provider-expense/profit accounting, or new GCash charts/summary cards in Store Overview.
- Automatic period rollover, finalized-period rewriting/reopening, Calendar-based trading gates, an independent holiday/open model, or automatic settlement of carried-forward obligations.
- Historical stock reconstruction, silent cost/quantity repair, changing unrelated earned Gross Profit semantics, a new PDF generator, replacement technical comparison reporting, or additional Promotion editing/deletion features.
- Deleting or overwriting original receipts, refunds, closing counts, exchange movements, actor attribution, review conclusions, or Protected Audit Records; equating review with repayment, staff debt, or stock execution.
- General access to another Cashier's carts, a new workflow engine, speculative abstraction, new test infrastructure, or destructive production-data cleanup.

## Further Notes

The user explicitly invoked to-spec against the completed [Administrator workflow review](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/discussions/administrator-workflow-review.md) in this new session, satisfying its requirement for explicit agreement before specification writing. Preserve all accepted choices through Q59; the earlier session's decision to defer specification writing is not a cancellation of this request. The test approach was explicitly confirmed before publication.

This specification deliberately changes ADR-0009's allowance of Super Administrator credentials alone for in-person business supervisor approval: eligible Administrator assignment is now required, including additional access, with permitted self-approval. It preserves active-Workspace separation and the narrow per-action credential exception. ADR-0001's operational/technical boundaries and ordinary Administrator protections otherwise remain authoritative, refined by the explicit narrow Super Administrator create/disable decision.

The GCash completion-date rule deliberately supersedes the earlier [Administrator GCash Overview specification](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/specs/administrator-gcash-overview.md) creation-time reporting basis. Its user-facing Waive action becomes Mark reviewed, and its previous exclusions do not negate the explicitly reopened emergency handover, Money history, correction, funding, follow-up, and fee-return decisions here. Preserve its other balance/filter/export/evidence safeguards and the wider [GCash Service specification](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/specs/gcash-service-spec.md).

The [Fiscal Period lifecycle specification](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/specs/fiscal-period-lifecycle.md) remains authoritative, clarified here to distinguish counted/reconciled custody from actual settlement of a carried-forward exchange. The [encrypted backup and Store Migration specification](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/specs/encrypted-backup-and-store-migration.md) and ADR-0017 retain protected Administrator restore authority; authorized takeover refines who may finish verification/reopening without weakening technical identity approval. Older glossary/context statements that still say Database Restore is Super Administrator-only must not revoke that accepted authority. ADR-0019 and the [remote-monitoring specification](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/blob/main/docs/specs/owner-remote-monitoring-cloudflare.md) independently restrict remote access.

Source exploration confirmed existing Dashboard reversal/discount paths, generic cash-review destinations and inconsistent threshold comparisons, existing GCash service custody/correction/approval entry points, and reusable workflow/browser tests. These are source findings, not claims of live UI, runtime permission, or database verification. Implementation must verify affected callers and actual persisted states, especially historical completion dates, review requirements, costing provenance, and responsibility access. Do not fabricate evidence or silently relax policy to accommodate an incompatible historical record; report concrete conflicts for resolution.

This is one consolidated specification. Any later implementation tickets must retain the cross-workflow invariants and all accepted decisions; decomposition must not drop obligations because an earlier narrower specification excluded them.
title: Administrator workflow alignment and accountable corrections

## Parent

#318

## What to build

body:
# Owner Remote Monitoring through Cloudflare

## Problem Statement

The Store owner wants to monitor staff and Store activity from a phone or laptop while away from the Store. RetailMind will run on a dedicated Windows Store PC; a localhost address cannot be reached from outside the Store. The owner wants a stable link available whenever that PC and its internet connection are running, without giving staff remote access or allowing remote changes. The existing local Windows deployment plan instead describes an installed private-network client and remote staff workflows.

## Solution

Give the owner a stable HTTPS browser link to the existing RetailMind installation through a named Cloudflare Tunnel. Cloudflare Access admits only the owner's exact email through a one-time PIN; RetailMind then requires the owner's normal sign-in. The remote route shows existing Store overview, staff activity, Cashier Shift, and report information. It rejects Store and account changes, sales, Cash Refunds, backups, and bulk downloads. Local checkout remains on the Store PC and works during an internet outage; remote monitoring is unavailable when the PC, required services, or internet connection is down.

## User Stories

1. As the Store owner, I want a stable browser address, so that I can bookmark RetailMind on my phone or laptop.
2. As the Store owner, I want to connect without installing a private-network app, so that I can check the Store from an ordinary browser.
3. As the Store owner, I want only my approved email to pass the Cloudflare gate, so that other people cannot reach the RetailMind login page remotely.
4. As the Store owner, I want a one-time PIN sent to my email, so that the first gate verifies control of that mailbox.
5. As the Store owner, I want my normal RetailMind sign-in after the Cloudflare gate, so that my existing account and Workspace rules remain in force.
6. As the Store owner, I want to see the existing Store overview, so that I can check current operational summaries away from the Store.
7. As the Store owner, I want to see existing staff activity and Cashier Shift information, so that I can monitor work recorded by the application.
8. As the Store owner, I want to read existing Store Reports, so that I can review business results remotely.
9. As the Store owner, I want monitoring pages to work on my phone and laptop, so that device choice does not prevent access.
10. As the Store owner, I want remote pages and assets to load under the stable HTTPS address, so that links and navigation work without returning me to localhost.
11. As the Store owner, I want my remote session to expire and sign out normally, so that an unattended browser does not retain access indefinitely.
12. As the Store owner, I want all remote Store and account changes blocked, so that monitoring cannot accidentally alter operations.
13. As the Store owner, I want direct and disguised write requests blocked, so that a hidden button or alternate URL cannot bypass read-only access.
14. As the Store owner, I want sales and Cash Refunds restricted to the Store, so that a remote browser cannot operate the physical register.
15. As the Store owner, I want database backups and bulk downloads unavailable remotely, so that monitoring does not expose large sets of sensitive records.
16. As the Store owner, I want local authorized administration to keep working, so that the remote restriction does not remove Store-side capabilities.
17. As a Cashier, I want local checkout to work during an internet outage, so that losing Cloudflare connectivity does not stop Store sales.
18. As the Store owner, I want the tunnel to recover after a Windows reboot, so that nobody must manually start a development control panel.
19. As the Store owner, I want a clear understanding that remote monitoring stops when the PC, application services, or internet stops, so that I do not mistake it for cloud hosting.
20. As the Store owner, I want to control the domain and Cloudflare account, so that the remote address and access policy remain under Store ownership.
21. As the Store owner, I want any domain or service cost reviewed before purchase, so that setup creates no unapproved expense.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Existing host:** Keep the Store PC and its local database as the sole live installation. Reuse standalone Apache/PHP and MySQL/MariaDB Windows services from the local deployment plan. Start `cloudflared` as a Windows service. Do not rely on Laragon at boot.
- **Stable tunnel:** Use a named Cloudflare Tunnel and an owner-controlled domain in Cloudflare. The tunnel connects outward to Cloudflare; no router port forwarding or inbound database access is needed. Create the Access application before publishing the route.
- **Owner gate:** Configure an Access Allow policy for the owner's exact email, with one-time PIN login. Do not use an all-email, email-domain, or Everyone rule. Require Access token validation at the tunnel. Preserve RetailMind's own login, session policy, and active Workspace permissions.
- **Read-only remote ingress:** Expose only approved monitoring pages and supporting assets, authentication, and session operations through the remote route. Deny other routes at a trusted server boundary. Audit every reachable handler, including side-effecting GET requests, alternate endpoints, and multi-role Workspace switching. HTTP method alone is not a sufficient write classifier. Keep backups and bulk exports unreachable.
- **Local versus remote:** The boundary must distinguish trusted tunnel ingress from local checkout. A proxy's loopback source address and arbitrary forwarding headers do not establish local trust. The selected routing arrangement must remain sound when the same owner account is used locally and remotely.
- **Existing screens:** Reuse the current Store overview, staff and Cashier Shift activity, and Store Reports. No new live-tracking screen or monitoring platform. Any existing navigation that leads to a denied action should not promise that action remotely; server denial remains authoritative.
- **Origins and database:** Verify URL base path, relative links, assets, redirects, session cookies, CSRF, and HTTPS under local and remote origins. Current database configuration infers a hosted database from a public host name; select the Store PC's local database through trusted deployment configuration. Ensure remote session cookies are secure even if the tunnel-to-Apache hop is HTTP. Do not trust client-supplied scheme headers.
- **Availability:** Remote access works only while the PC, Apache, database, `cloudflared`, and internet are available. Local checkout and printing continue during an ISP outage as required by the local deployment plan.
- **Scope revision:** This replaces the remote-access portion of the earlier local Windows deployment plan: no approved-staff remote workflows or installed private-network client. Its local hosting, backup, recovery, and offline-checkout requirements remain applicable. No new schema or public API is required by the agreed feature.

## Testing Decisions

- **Primary seam: deployed browser and direct HTTP behavior.** Use the existing Administrator dashboard, login/session, and cashier browser/HTTP test patterns. Test what an owner or attacker can observe and change, not tunnel configuration strings or private helper calls.
- Verify the approved owner passes Access and RetailMind login, opens each selected monitoring page, follows links, and remains on the remote HTTPS origin. An unapproved email cannot reach RetailMind. Check phone and laptop viewport behavior through the existing responsive browser patterns.
- With a valid owner session, directly request representative mutation, alternate-route, GET-action, backup, export, sale, and Cash Refund endpoints through the remote ingress. Assert denial and unchanged persisted Store/account state. Exercise a multi-role account. Confirm the same actions still follow normal authorization locally.
- Verify session cookie security and normal sign-out/expiry on the remote origin, and confirm the public hostname reaches the local database rather than a hosted database.
- **Windows acceptance:** Reboot the Store PC and verify Apache, database, and tunnel availability without Laragon. Disconnect the ISP while keeping the PC running; confirm a fresh local checkout and receipt flow work while the remote route stops. Restore connectivity and verify monitoring returns. Shut down the PC and verify remote access stops.
- Prior art includes existing Administrator dashboard browser and route tests, login/session browser tests, cashier checkout and refund browser workflows, and the Windows boot/outage checks already specified for local deployment. Add only the cases needed to prove this route's distinct access and read-only boundary.

## Out of Scope

- Remote staff access, remote inventory changes, full remote administration, remote sales, and remote Cash Refunds.
- New live staff tracking, camera monitoring, a new dashboard, cloud database replication, and automatic failover.
- Quick Tunnels with changing URLs, public anonymous access, open router ports, and direct database access.
- Database backup/download access through the monitoring route. Existing local backup and recovery work is governed by the local deployment plan.
- Buying a domain, subscribing to a paid plan, or activating the production tunnel as part of writing this specification.

## Further Notes

This specification follows the confirmed Owner Remote Monitoring decision in ADR-0019 and supersedes only the remote-access requirements of local Windows deployment issue #271. Before implementation, identify the owner-controlled Cloudflare domain and exact owner email, review any cost, and inventory the route allowlist and all reachable write/download actions. Cloudflare Tunnel provides reachability; Cloudflare Access gates identity; RetailMind enforces its own roles and the remote read-only boundary.
title: Owner-only remote monitoring through Cloudflare Tunnel

## What to build

Inventory Managers can conduct stock management workflows (Products, Inventory Counts, Stock Receiving, Stock Issue reviews, and Supplier Pullouts) on portable tablets using attached barcode scanners and touch inputs. Scans outside form editing inspect existing products or trigger a "Product not found" prompt without auto-creating records; scans during explicit product editing target only the selected barcode field without advancing or submitting forms. Entered inventory form values persist durably across reloads, browser closures, and tablet restarts with user-isolated Resume/Discard options. Form submissions include idempotency tracking so interrupted network connections or lost server responses can safely retry without duplicating Stock Receiving records or stock movements.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Barcode scans outside product editing open the matching product or show a "Product not found" alert; no silent products are created.
- [ ] During product entry, barcode scans populate only the actively selected barcode field and never overwrite name, price, quantity, or submit the form.
- [ ] Duplicate barcode validation is enforced during product entry.
- [ ] Entered form values for Inventory Counts, Stock Receiving, Stock Issues, and Supplier Pullouts persist in durable local storage across browser reloads, closures, and device restarts.
- [ ] Draft recovery presents Resume and Discard choices, isolated strictly to the same authenticated user account.
- [ ] Drafts are automatically cleared upon confirmed successful server submission or explicit discard, and retained upon validation errors.
- [ ] Storage unavailability alerts operator clearly without silent loss of persistence expectations.
- [ ] Restored drafts re-validate active user permissions, product state, and current business rules before final commit.
- [ ] Stock Receiving and inventory submissions utilize idempotency tokens to reconcile lost server responses and prevent duplicate records or double stock movements on retry.

# Optimize role workspaces for tablets and mobile monitoring

## Problem Statement

Cashiers need reliable PC and tablet checkout with attached scanners and access to the Store's PC-connected thermal printer. Inventory Managers need to work throughout the Store on portable tablets without losing entered values or returning to a PC to complete shelf work. The Administrator needs convenient phone monitoring. Existing responsive layouts and emulated checks do not establish physical iPad, Android, scanner, or printer compatibility. The owner likes the existing tablet POS layout and wants it preserved.

## Solution

Optimize each workspace around its work: retain PC and tablet POS, make Inventory Manager workflows practical on tablets, and prioritize Administrator monitoring on phones. Support Safari and Chrome on iPad and Chrome on Android tablets, portrait and landscape, attached keyboard-style scanners, and saved-receipt printing through the Store PC's thermal printer. Preserve all entered inventory values as recoverable drafts without silently creating Products, posting offline stock changes, or duplicating completed operations.

## User Stories

1. As a Cashier, I want the current tablet POS layout retained, so that familiar checkout remains efficient.
2. As a Cashier, I want to complete checkout by touch, so that a tablet does not require a physical keyboard.
3. As a Cashier, I want keyboard and scanner efficiency retained on PC, so that tablet improvements do not slow counter work.
4. As a Cashier, I want product search, cart editing, totals, and payment actions reachable, so that I can complete sales without fighting the layout.
5. As a Cashier, I want GCash Services, Cashier Shifts, and Cash Refunds usable on a tablet, so that related counter tasks remain practical.
6. As a Cashier, I want consecutive scans to resolve correctly, so that selling several items does not lose or misdirect scanner input.
7. As a tablet operator, I want USB wireless-receiver and Bluetooth keyboard-style scanner connections supported on compatible hardware, so that I can reuse attached scanners.
8. As a tablet operator, I want iPad Safari, iPad Chrome, and Android Chrome workflows verified, so that browser choice does not unexpectedly break my work.
9. As a tablet operator, I want portrait and landscape support, so that I can use the device comfortably.
10. As a tablet operator, I want rotation to preserve my active cart or form, so that changing orientation does not discard work.
11. As a tablet operator, I want fields and actions reachable with the on-screen keyboard open, so that text entry does not block completion.
12. As a Cashier, I want the saved receipt preview shown after checkout, so that I can review the completed transaction.
13. As a Cashier, I want Print to Store Printer from my tablet, so that the thermal printer connected to the Store PC prints the saved receipt.
14. As a Cashier, I want direct PC-routed printing without selecting an iPad printer, so that printing is a simple action at the counter.
15. As a Cashier, I want existing PC receipt printing retained, so that both cashier device types remain usable.
16. As a Cashier, I want printing failures to leave my completed sale intact, so that printer availability does not undo checkout.
17. As a Cashier, I want to retry printing a saved receipt, so that I never need another checkout to obtain a paper copy.
18. As a Cashier, I want a warning when print delivery is uncertain, so that I can check for an existing copy before reprinting.
19. As a Cashier, I want repeated print requests to avoid new sales or stock deductions, so that a printing problem cannot change transaction records.
20. As an Inventory Manager, I want Products, Inventory Counts, Stock Receiving, Stock Issue reviews, and Supplier Pullouts usable on a portable tablet, so that I can finish shelf work without returning to a PC.
21. As an Inventory Manager, I want tablet-friendly stock lookup and quantity entry, so that I can work near the goods being counted or received.
22. As an Inventory Manager, I want a scan outside editing to open an existing Product, so that I can quickly inspect it.
23. As an Inventory Manager, I want an unknown scan to show a Product-not-found prompt, so that I understand why lookup failed.
24. As an Inventory Manager, I want unknown scans to create nothing, so that the catalog does not accumulate silent or incomplete Products.
25. As an Inventory Manager, I want Product creation to remain explicit, so that I control when a new Product is added.
26. As an Inventory Manager, I want to scan into a selected barcode field during explicit Product entry, so that I do not manually transcribe the identifier.
27. As an Inventory Manager, I want scans to leave name, price, quantity, and other unrelated fields untouched, so that scanner input cannot corrupt a form.
28. As an Inventory Manager, I want a scan to avoid submitting or advancing a Product form, so that I retain control of review and completion.
29. As an Inventory Manager, I want duplicate barcode validation retained, so that different Products cannot accidentally share conflicting identifiers.
30. As an Inventory Manager, I want all entered inventory values retained when saving is interrupted, so that connectivity failures do not force re-entry.
31. As an Inventory Manager, I want a clear unsaved warning and success only after server confirmation, so that I know whether inventory actually changed.
32. As an Inventory Manager, I want drafts to survive refresh, browser closure, and tablet restart, so that unfinished work can be resumed.
33. As an Inventory Manager, I want Resume and Discard choices, so that I decide what happens to unfinished work.
34. As an Inventory Manager, I want drafts available only to the same signed-in user, so that another operator on a shared tablet cannot inspect or restore my work.
35. As an Inventory Manager, I want a draft cleared after confirmed submission or explicit discard, so that completed work does not return as an unfinished task.
36. As an Inventory Manager, I want draft recovery to avoid automatic stock posting, so that resuming work cannot silently change inventory.
37. As an Inventory Manager, I want interrupted submission retries to avoid duplicate Stock Receiving and stock changes, so that response loss cannot inflate or reduce stock twice.
38. As an Inventory Manager, I want restored values checked against current permissions and Product state, so that an old draft cannot bypass current rules.
39. As an Inventory Manager, I want entered values retained after validation errors, so that correcting a mistake does not require rebuilding the form.
40. As an Administrator, I want Store Overview, GCash Overview, notifications, and report summaries easy to read on my phone, so that I can monitor the Store while away from my PC.
41. As an Administrator, I want monitoring summaries to open relevant details, so that I can investigate exceptions on my phone.
42. As an Administrator, I want Stock Issue Oversight to remain read-only, so that monitoring does not change operational authority.
43. As an Administrator, I want authorized actions to remain accessible while detailed administration stays comfortable on PC, so that device optimization does not remove existing capabilities.
44. As a Store operator, I want readable failures, touch controls, keyboard focus, and reachable dialogs across target devices, so that errors and accessibility needs do not block work.

## Implementation Decisions

- Preserve the existing server-rendered application, role workspaces, house components, responsive system, and accepted tablet POS composition. Inspect existing behavior first and repair demonstrated gaps rather than replacing functioning pages or creating a separate tablet application.
- Primary scope: Cashier POS, GCash Services, Cashier Shifts, Cash Refunds, and receipt presentation; Inventory Manager Products, Inventory Counts, Stock Receiving, Stock Issue reviews, and Supplier Pullouts; Administrator Store Overview, GCash Overview, notifications, report summaries, and Stock Issue Oversight. Retain PC usability and existing authorized access.
- Cover iPad Safari, iPad Chrome, and Android Chrome in portrait and landscape. Preserve active work during rotation and keep focused fields and primary actions reachable when the software keyboard is present. Exact device models and supported OS/browser versions must be recorded during acceptance; none are invented by this specification.
- Reuse existing keyboard-style scanner handling and Product lookup. The confirmed USB arrangement is a wireless scanner receiver connected through a tablet adapter; Bluetooth is also required on compatible hardware. Use Enter-terminated input where supported. The owner reports Android testing, not physical iPad validation.
- Scope scanner handling to context. Outside Product editing, resolve an existing Product or show Product not found. During Product editing, accept a scan only into an explicitly selected barcode field. Do not redirect scans into unrelated fields, auto-advance, auto-submit, or auto-create Products. Preserve identifier uniqueness checks and existing POS scan semantics.
- Reuse saved Sale Receipt and Refund Receipt presentation and configured thermal paper width. Keep the receipt preview and provide Print to Store Printer, routing the saved receipt to the existing XP-58IID connected to the Store PC. The direct route must not require the tablet browser's printer-selection dialog. Existing authorized PC printing remains available.
- Implement the smallest PC-side print delivery path that meets the contract. A tablet browser's print dialog alone is insufficient. The tablet reaches the PC through its local network address or hostname; localhost on the tablet refers to the tablet. The PC and its printing service must be available. Select bridge/worker technology during implementation rather than assume the current browser helper already provides this integration.
- Print submission must identify an existing authorized receipt and configured printer destination; it must not accept arbitrary executable commands or unrestricted printer targets. Enforce active-workspace authorization and request protections at the application boundary, and protect PC-side delivery from unauthenticated network requests. Bind any PC worker to its intended Store deployment.
- Separate sale/refund completion from printing. Print jobs, repeated taps, and retries must never invoke checkout again or repeat stock changes. Report saved-receipt and printing status distinctly. When job outcome is uncertain, require an informed reprint choice rather than silently replaying an ambiguous job. Do not equate queue acceptance with confirmed physical paper output.
- Extend existing inventory draft behavior to retain every entered form value for the in-scope inventory entry workflows, not merely the visible page or a subset of receiving fields. Preserve form context and necessary identifiers, with the same signed-in user's Resume / Discard choices after reload, browser closure, and device restart.
- Draft isolation is an authorization requirement on shared devices, not just a user identifier in a readable browser key. Select storage that meets recovery and isolation requirements; do not expose another user's values. Show a clear preservation failure if durable storage is unavailable. Do not claim browser-data deletion, eviction, or device-loss recovery without evidence from the chosen design.
- Keep drafts separate from committed inventory. Clear after confirmed submission or explicit discard; retain on recoverable errors. Never submit automatically when restoring a draft or reconnecting. Revalidate current permissions, Products, quantities, and existing business rules before final submission.
- Distinguish unsent work from a server-committed operation whose response was lost. Reconcile uncertain outcomes and reuse existing operation identity/idempotency patterns where suitable; safe retry must not repeat stock changes. Inventory saving remains server-confirmed, not offline posting.
- Reuse existing receiving draft logic, stock-change validation, checkout attempt handling, role authorization, and shared responsive components before adding new mechanisms. Any persistence or job schema changes must be limited to the confirmed draft, reconciliation, and print-delivery contracts; exact tables and APIs are implementation choices.
- Preserve Store versus technical authority and active Workspace boundaries. Administrator Stock Issue Oversight remains read-only. Device class does not grant or remove roles. Preserve nontechnical Operator Alerts and keep technical details in existing logs.

## Testing Decisions

- The primary seam is the existing authenticated browser/HTTP workflow, extended rather than replaced. The owner accepted real-device workflow checks and no-duplicate-operation checks during the design discussion. Test visible outcomes and persisted business effects, not CSS strings, private helpers, exact timing thresholds, or an implementation-shaped mock graph.
- Reuse existing responsive system/component, cashier UI, keyboard scan, inventory scan, checkout attempt, receipt dialog, receiving draft, and Administrator dashboard browser coverage. Existing stock receiving and inventory reconciliation integration tests provide prior art for checking persisted quantities and records. Use disposable databases for stock-changing tests.
- Verify accepted POS layout and PC keyboard/scanner behavior alongside touch checkout, cart editing, modal actions, scrolling, orientation changes, and software-keyboard reachability on the target tablet browser matrix. Test relevant empty, populated, long-content, validation-error, and network-error states.
- Verify consecutive scans, explicit Add Product barcode entry, unknown-code prompts without creation, duplicate identifiers, unrelated-field protection, Enter handling, and no scan-triggered submission or wizard advancement. Exercise both USB-receiver and Bluetooth hardware where compatible; synthetic keyboard events alone do not establish hardware support.
- Verify every entered inventory value survives reload and browser restart, with Resume / Discard, same-user isolation, validation-error retention, clear-on-success, clear-on-discard, and no automatic posting. Use a physical tablet restart for that acceptance claim. Check storage-unavailable feedback and changed Product/permission validation.
- Simulate a connection failure before submission and a lost response after a successful server commit. Retry through the user flow and assert exactly one Stock Receiving or stock mutation. The second case must prove reconciliation, not merely form retention.
- For printing, use the saved-receipt print request boundary plus the smallest necessary PC delivery integration check. Verify authorization, duplicate taps, unavailable PC/printer, uncertain delivery, explicit reprint, and no extra sale/refund or stock movement. A fake or test spooler may prove job behavior, but not thermal output.
- On actual iPad Safari, iPad Chrome, and Android Chrome, verify the end-to-end local-network print route to the PC and physical XP-58IID. Inspect long names, totals, configured paper width, clipping, and repeat/reprint behavior. Record OS/browser, scanner, adapter, printer, and connection details. Do not claim a device pass if that hardware was unavailable.
- Verify phone-width Administrator summaries, drill-downs, navigation, notifications, and existing authorization. Record physical phone/browser coverage separately; a responsive viewport pass is not a physical phone pass.
- Run focused existing checks appropriate to each implementation change. Report the tested matrix, skipped hardware combinations, failures, and remaining limitations without promising the absence of every possible bug.

## Out of Scope

- Replacing the accepted tablet POS layout, a separate native tablet app, or a broader visual redesign.
- Silent Product creation, automatic draft submission, offline checkout commitment, or offline inventory posting.
- Changes to role authority, multi-Store behavior, reporting definitions, forecasting behavior, or existing business validation.
- Direct tablet-to-printer Bluetooth/USB integration as a replacement for the confirmed PC-routed printer destination; selecting or purchasing new hardware.
- Cross-device draft synchronization or recovery after device loss/browser-data deletion unless separately established by the selected storage design; no such guarantee was discussed.
- Live deployment, firewall/network changes on the Store installation, or claiming physical-device acceptance based solely on emulation.

## Further Notes

The owner confirmed shared understanding and requested publication on 2026-10-25. The accepted scope includes persistent drafts and safe retry, not just responsive CSS.

The existing role-device design brief and the decision on tablet receipts through the Store PC retain the discussion context.
