## Parent

#298

## What to build

Offer explicit, confirmed permanent deletion in Users for otherwise manageable accounts with no retained business or audit history. Refuse history-linked deletion with a clear explanation that disabling is the alternative where permitted. Extend UserLifecycleService and the existing Users workflow, including ordinary Administrator targets and actors enabled by the preceding ticket.

Before implementing deletion, inventory every reference to user identities across schema, application writes, and audit storage, including actor references, target references, and logical references without foreign keys. Distinguish retained history from disposable account-owned state. The inventory determines the actual eligible set and any narrowly necessary schema adjustment; do not assume a new schema or framework is needed.

Use the shared transactional minimum-Administrator guard. Eligibility checks, necessary disposable-state cleanup, deletion, and its audit record must succeed atomically. Retain existing referential integrity and historical attribution.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the reference inventory and classification before implementing deletion, covering sales, Cashier Shifts, refunds, GCash activity, stock records, Protected Audit Records, and all other retained business/audit references.
- [ ] An authorized actor can permanently delete an eligible active or disabled account through Users after explicit confirmation. Ordinary Administrator targets follow the expanded delegated-management policy.
- [ ] Any retained business or audit reference to the identity prevents deletion, including account-creation or administrative audit entries when they link the target. Do not invent audit exemptions, erase history, null historical attribution, or weaken foreign keys/cascade business history to make an account eligible.
- [ ] Remove only necessary disposable account-owned state, such as credentials/tokens, role assignments, preferences, and notices, atomically with eligible deletion. If the existing reference model makes ordinary newly created accounts ineligible, explain that outcome rather than bypassing retained audit history.
- [ ] Preserve Super Administrator identity protection and Recovery Account isolation using attributes and complete roles. Reject self-delete and requests from unauthorized active Workspaces, including forged requests.
- [ ] Apply the same qualifying-Administrator count and common transactional lock as manual disable, demotion, and dormancy. The Super Administrator cannot bypass the minimum. Recheck current account and history eligibility atomically to avoid stale decisions.
- [ ] Record an allowed deletion under the acting account with sufficient retained target identity information to explain it. Preserve all existing Protected Audit Records; deletion auditing must not require retaining a live target foreign-key reference.
- [ ] Deleted accounts, credentials, and existing sessions can no longer authenticate or retain access. Any failure leaves account state, disposable state, and audit outcomes consistent through rollback.
- [ ] Users distinguishes protected identities, minimum-Administrator restrictions, and history-linked deletion restrictions, and gives understandable server-side rejection. Offer disabling only where the other protections allow it.
- [ ] Verify successful deletion using an actually eligible fixture, rejection for representative retained business and audit references, restrictive foreign keys, cleanup, actor/target audit attribution, lost authentication/session access, and transactional rollback through the public lifecycle boundary.
- [ ] Extend isolated MySQL integration tests using independent connections for concurrent deletion versus disable, demotion, deletion, and dormancy, asserting that qualifying Administrator access remains and history is preserved. Fixtures must represent legitimate eligibility without deleting audit records to prepare a target.
- [ ] Add browser/HTTP acceptance through the existing Users workflow for visibility, confirmation/cancellation, useful rejection, and direct unauthorized requests. Never delete real accounts/history, send real notifications, or run concurrency fixtures against production data.

## Scope limits

No soft-delete/anonymization framework, tombstones, custom roles, bulk operations, dormancy threshold changes, automatic repair of installations with no qualifying Administrator, or changes to Database Restore/backup semantics.

## Parent

## What to build

Preserve at least one active ordinary account with Administrator access when existing account-management actions disable an account or remove Administrator access, and when the Dormancy Policy automatically disables accounts. Show understandable restrictions in Users and enforce them for direct requests. Establish this protection before expanding delegated Administrator management.

Reuse UserLifecycleService and DormancyRunner. A qualifying account is active, has Administrator as a primary or additional role, and is neither a Super Administrator identity nor the Recovery Account. Use a common transactional locking strategy across mutations affecting this minimum, including dormancy. Recheck current eligibility within the transaction; locking only each target account cannot protect concurrent changes to different Administrators. Keep this seam reusable by the later permanent-delete operation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Manual disabling and removal of Administrator access leave at least one qualifying account, including when performed by the Super Administrator.
- [ ] Primary and additional Administrator assignments count identically. Disabled accounts, Super Administrator identities, and the Recovery Account do not count.
- [ ] Changing primary role while retaining Administrator access, or removing an unrelated role, does not trigger a false demotion restriction. Disabled targets are already outside the minimum count.
- [ ] Self-disable and self-demotion remain forbidden. Preserve existing self-management restrictions, protected-identity rules, active Workspace authorization, and permitted Super Administrator self-profile maintenance.
- [ ] Dormancy uses the same count and transactional protection. Preserve existing scope/exclusions, warning behavior, skipped-last-Administrator reporting, audit records, notifications, and session invalidation.
- [ ] Denied operations leave no partial account, role, or audit changes. Users distinguishes last-Administrator restrictions from protected identities, and forged requests receive useful server-side rejection.
- [ ] Extend public lifecycle and controllable-clock dormancy contracts for primary/additional roles, both authorized actor types, disabled targets, retained access, identity exclusions, and rollback. Use injected notification delivery.
- [ ] Add isolated MySQL tests with independent connections covering concurrent disable, demotion, and dormancy against different accounts, including mixed operations. Assert persisted qualifying access remains; sequential or SQLite-only checks are insufficient.
- [ ] Add focused browser/HTTP acceptance through the existing Users workflow for minimum restrictions and direct-request rejection. Tests never modify real accounts or send real notifications.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Preserve one active ordinary Administrator across manual actions and dormancy

body:
# Administrator account management and minimum active Administrator protection

## Problem Statement

Administrators cannot manage another Administrator because the current delegated-role policy permits only Cashier and Inventory Manager accounts. The Users interface consequently marks ordinary Administrator accounts as Protected, preventing routine account maintenance by other Administrators.

Manual disabling and role removal do not consistently preserve an active Administrator. Automatic Dormancy Policy protection counts only primary-role Administrators, overlooking accounts with an additional Administrator Workspace. There is no permanent-delete action for unused accounts.

## Solution

Allow an Administrator in the Administrator Workspace to manage other ordinary Administrator accounts, alongside existing staff management. Permit account creation, promotion, profile editing, password reset, role changes, status changes, and permanent deletion subject to the protections below.

Keep the Super Administrator protected from other accounts and the Recovery Account outside ordinary user management. Prevent self-disable, self-delete, and self-demotion. Preserve at least one active ordinary account with Administrator access, whether its Administrator role is primary or additional. Apply this minimum to manual actions and automatic dormancy, including actions initiated by the Super Administrator.

Only accounts without linked business or audit history may be permanently deleted. Accounts with history must remain attributable and may instead be disabled where the other protections allow it.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want to manage another ordinary Administrator, so that routine account maintenance does not require the Super Administrator.
2. As an Administrator, I want to create another Administrator account, so that Store administration can be delegated.
3. As an Administrator, I want to promote an existing Cashier or Inventory Manager to Administrator, so that staff can assume administrative responsibilities.
4. As an Administrator, I want to edit another Administrator's profile, so that account details remain correct.
5. As an Administrator, I want to reset another Administrator's password, so that their access can be recovered through the existing reset workflow.
6. As an Administrator, I want to change another Administrator's assigned operational roles, so that access matches their responsibilities.
7. As an Administrator, I want to disable another Administrator when an active Administrator will remain, so that departing staff lose access.
8. As an Administrator, I want to re-enable an eligible disabled account, so that authorized staff can return to work.
9. As an Administrator, I want to remove another account's Administrator role when an active Administrator will remain, so that unnecessary authority can be revoked.
10. As an Administrator, I want to permanently delete an unused account, so that accidental account creation can be corrected.
11. As an Administrator, I want deletion refused when business or audit history references the account, so that historical attribution remains intact.
12. As an Administrator, I want a clear explanation that a history-linked account must be disabled instead, so that I can choose an appropriate action.
13. As the Super Administrator, I want my account protected from other accounts, so that routine user management cannot compromise platform ownership.
14. As the Super Administrator, I want the Recovery Account excluded from ordinary account management, so that offline recovery remains protected.
15. As an Administrator, I want the last active ordinary Administrator protected from disabling, deletion, and loss of Administrator access, so that Store administration remains available.
16. As the Super Administrator, I want the same minimum-active-Administrator guard applied to my account-management actions, so that privileged actions cannot accidentally leave the Store without an operational Administrator.
17. As a multi-role Administrator, I want my active account counted even when Administrator is an additional role, so that protection reflects actual Administrator access.
18. As an Administrator, I want disabled accounts, the Super Administrator, and the Recovery Account excluded from the minimum count, so that the remaining Administrator is usable for ordinary administration.
19. As an Administrator, I want automatic dormancy to preserve the same minimum, so that scheduled security maintenance does not remove all ordinary Administrator access.
20. As an account holder, I want self-disable, self-delete, and self-demotion blocked, so that I cannot accidentally remove my own administrative access.
21. As an Administrator, I want the Users interface to distinguish protected identities, last-Administrator restrictions, and accounts with history, so that unavailable actions have understandable reasons.
22. As an Administrator, I want simultaneous account-management requests to preserve an active Administrator, so that individually valid requests cannot together remove every Administrator.
23. As the Super Administrator, I want account-management actions recorded without deleting existing Protected Audit Records, so that security changes remain attributable.
24. As a Cashier or Inventory Manager, I want user-management permissions to remain unavailable in my Workspace, so that this change does not grant unrelated account-management authority.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend RoleCapabilityPolicy's existing delegated account-management and role-assignment rules to include the ordinary Administrator role. Do not grant Administrators the Super Administrator role, arbitrary privileges, or platform-governance authority.
- Enforce authorization through the active Workspace. Counting assigned Administrator access for minimum protection does not combine Workspace privileges or authorize mutations from a Cashier or Inventory Manager Workspace.
- Extend UserLifecycleService and its existing Users request handling and interface. Keep shared authorization, validation, password-reset, session invalidation, notification, and audit behavior intact. Reuse the existing account-management architecture rather than adding a parallel administration subsystem.
- Protect identities by account attributes and complete role assignments, including additional roles, rather than merely the displayed primary role. Preserve the Super Administrator's existing permitted self-profile maintenance and the Recovery Account's offline lifecycle.
- A qualifying account is active, has the Administrator role as either its primary or additional assignment, and is neither a Super Administrator identity nor the Recovery Account. Count each account once, regardless of its current Workspace.
- An operation that removes qualifying Administrator access must leave at least one qualifying account. Removing an unrelated additional role or changing primary role while retaining Administrator access must not be treated as demotion out of Administrator access. A disabled Administrator is already outside the count.
- Apply the same qualifying-account rule to disable, permanent delete, role removal, and DormancyRunner. Super Administrator actions do not bypass it. Preserve existing dormancy exclusions and side effects.
- Serialize mutations affecting this minimum through a common transactional locking strategy, including scheduled dormancy. Locking only the target account is insufficient when concurrent requests affect different Administrators. Recheck eligibility atomically before committing; avoid partial changes on denial.
- Keep self-disable, self-delete, and self-demotion prohibited. Preserve existing self-management restrictions outside this explicit scope.
- Add permanent deletion for otherwise manageable accounts only when no retained business or audit history links to that identity. Preserve sales, Cashier Shifts, refunds, GCash activity, stock records, and all other retained historical references. Disable remains the alternative for history-linked accounts.
- Distinguish retained historical references from disposable account-owned state. Remove only necessary credentials, tokens, role assignments, preferences, notices, and other nonhistorical account state atomically with an eligible deletion. Inventory all references before implementation; do not remove foreign-key protection or cascade business history.
- Audit an allowed deletion under the acting account and retain sufficient target identity information to explain the deleted account. Do not delete historical audit entries merely because they mention the target; account-creation or administrative audit entries must not be silently erased to make deletion eligible. The exact eligible set must reflect existing retained references, not a newly invented exemption for audit history.
- Preserve session invalidation and forced-password-change semantics for newly allowed Administrator password resets and role/status changes. Deleted accounts and credentials must no longer authenticate.
- Expose permanent delete with an explicit confirmation and understandable rejection messages. Enforce every protection server-side even for direct requests; UI availability alone is insufficient.
- No new dependency or general soft-delete/anonymization framework is required. Retain the current account status model and database referential integrity; determine any narrowly necessary schema adjustment from the implementation inventory rather than assuming one is needed.
- This deliberately changes the ordinary-Administrator lifecycle boundary described by ADR-0001 and the current Administrator domain definition. Update that boundary and affected terminology during implementation while retaining Super Administrator technical governance, Recovery Account isolation, and ADR-0009's active Workspace rules. Preserve Protected Audit Record immutability.

## Testing Decisions

- Proposed primary seam: public UserLifecycleService operations against database fixtures, extending the existing user lifecycle contract. Assert observable permissions, persisted account state, authentication/session effects, retained history, audit outcomes, and useful rejection behavior rather than private helpers or SQL text.
- Reuse RoleCapabilityPolicy contract coverage for the expanded delegated-role matrix. Verify ordinary Administrators can manage/assign Administrator, Cashier, and Inventory Manager roles while Super Administrator assignment and unrelated capabilities remain forbidden.
- Extend the existing DormancyRunner public-runner contract using its controllable clock and injected notifier. Verify that primary and additional Administrator roles count identically and that scheduled disabling retains one qualifying account.
- Follow the existing password-reset integration coverage for password replacement, Mandatory Password Change, session invalidation, and audit behavior, adding ordinary Administrator targets and actors.
- Cover active and disabled targets; primary and additional Administrator assignments; retaining Administrator access while changing other roles; Super Administrator and Recovery Account exclusions; self-action restrictions; and both Administrator and Super Administrator actors.
- Cover successful deletion of an eligible account and rejection for business/history-linked accounts. Assert disposable state cleanup, retained actor/target attribution in the deletion audit, preserved historical records, and transactional rollback on failure. Include representative restrictive foreign-key relationships rather than testing only a permissive in-memory schema.
- Use an isolated MySQL integration fixture with independent database connections to verify concurrent disable, demotion, deletion, and dormancy cannot together remove all qualifying Administrators. SQLite-only or sequential tests cannot establish production locking correctness.
- Add focused browser/HTTP acceptance coverage through the existing Users workflow for action visibility, delete confirmation, protected-account explanations, and server-side rejection of forged requests. Avoid introducing a new test-only application boundary.
- Do not change real accounts, delete real history, send real notifications, or run concurrency fixtures against production data.
- The user confirmed these testing seams before issue publication. No application tests have been executed for this specification-only work.

## Out of Scope

- Implementing the feature during specification synthesis.
- Deleting or anonymizing accounts that have retained business or audit history, deleting historical records, weakening foreign keys, or introducing account tombstones.
- Allowing self-disable, self-delete, self-demotion, or ordinary management of the Recovery Account.
- Granting ordinary Administrators Super Administrator privileges, arbitrary privilege combinations, or platform-governance authority.
- Replacing active Workspace authorization with combined privileges.
- New account types, custom role builders, bulk account operations, changes to dormancy thresholds, or changes to the offline recovery procedure.
- Repairing existing installations with no qualifying active Administrator automatically, or changing Database Restore and backup semantics.

## Further Notes

The account-management, minimum protection, multi-role counting, recovery, self-action, and history-preserving deletion requirements were explicitly agreed during the grilling conversation on 2026-10-25. The subsequent to-spec request authorizes specification synthesis and tracker publication, not application implementation.

The user confirmed the testing plan and authorized publication to the project's GitHub Issues tracker with the ready-for-agent label. No additional product-design interview is needed.
title: Administrator account management and minimum active Administrator protection

## What to build

Make the existing authenticated GCash Overview CSV download consume reporting-owned traversal so Administrators receive every matching record without any full-overview assembly, including before traversal starts. Keep CSV staging, escaping, field mapping, and delivery in the CSV adapter; remove its page orchestration. A download is delivered only after the complete file has been successfully staged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Select the CSV path before assembling the full overview. Valid exports succeed even when overview-only retrieval is unavailable; exporting does not require recorded balances, completed-activity aggregates, unresolved reviews, reconciliation history, or Cashier choices.
- [ ] Consume the shared authorized traversal from #296 without managing page numbers or retrieving batches through the full overview. The displayed list page never truncates or offsets the export.
- [ ] The complete ordered CSV record set agrees with list selection for Philippine Today, Month-to-date, inclusive custom dates, Cashier, literal reference/Cashier/Cashier Shift searches, and exchange type. Preserve all supported historical statuses and legacy reference-only evidence.
- [ ] Preserve headings, column order, values, quoting, UTF-8 BOM, filename, response headers, formula neutralization, and exact reference strings including leading zeroes. Empty selections produce a valid header-only CSV.
- [ ] Stage the whole file before attachment headers or body. Invalid selections retain the rejected-selection response; retrieval or staging failures retain the failed-export response. No failure may deliver a partial CSV attachment.
- [ ] Existing role and active Workspace checks remain effective at the authenticated route, including authorized Administrator/Super Administrator access and Cashier rejection. Invalid or unauthorized requests cannot yield a successful attachment.
- [ ] Extend the existing authenticated Overview/CSV HTTP acceptance checks using disposable fixtures. Verify the complete expected ordered records without duplicates or omissions for empty, one-batch, exact-batch, and multi-batch selections without asserting an internal batch-size constant.
- [ ] Use the existing disposable-fixture/failure-router pattern to prove valid matching rows still export when overview-only retrieval is unavailable, retrieval failure after an initial batch prevents attachment delivery, and staging failure prevents attachment delivery. Do not introduce production test hooks, SQL-string assertions, query-count assertions, or timing thresholds.
- [ ] Retain overview checks that completed totals ignore search/type, recorded funds ignore report filters, unresolved/reconciliation reviews remain Store-wide, and refresh/pagination still work. Reuse or consolidate existing coverage rather than duplicate it.
- [ ] Run affected disposable-database integration and authenticated HTTP/browser checks; report results.

## Constraints

Reuse existing reporting and CSV facilities, including staged storage that may spill to disk. No new routes, filters, columns, formats, background jobs, dependencies, configuration, schema changes, financial-posting changes, or concurrent-write snapshot guarantees. Preserve ADR-0001 authority, ADR-0010 Receipt History boundaries, ADR-0006 receipt preservation, and the GCash Service Receipt specification. This addresses architectural friction; do not claim a measured latency improvement.

title: Share authorized GCash Service selection and bounded traversal

body:
## Problem Statement

Administrators need complete, trustworthy GCash Service exports without paying for unrelated overview calculations on every batch. Today the CSV adapter retrieves each batch by requesting the full overview again, repeating recorded-fund, completed-activity, unresolved-activity, reconciliation, and Cashier-choice work. The adapter also owns pagination orchestration that belongs with reporting selection.

This is observed architectural friction, not a measured latency regression or evidence of incorrect exports.

## Solution

Deepen the existing GCash Service reporting module so it owns matching-record selection and complete traversal. The overview and CSV export reuse the same selection rules. The CSV adapter consumes matching records, stages and escapes the file, and delivers it only after successful completion. Export no longer computes unrelated overview information, including before traversal begins.

Keep current permissions, filter meanings, history evidence, CSV format, and failure behavior.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want every matching GCash Service record exported, so that I can review the complete selected history.
2. As an Administrator, I want export to retrieve matching records without rebuilding unrelated overview information, so that work grows with the report I requested.
3. As an Administrator, I want exports to use the same selection as the transaction list, so that downloaded records agree with the displayed selection.
4. As an Administrator, I want Today interpreted in Philippine calendar time, so that the report covers the Store's operating day.
5. As an Administrator, I want Month-to-date preserved, so that regular monthly review remains familiar.
6. As an Administrator, I want inclusive custom calendar dates preserved, so that records on the final selected day are included.
7. As an Administrator, I want the Cashier selection preserved across the whole export, so that the file contains the intended records.
8. As an Administrator, I want reference, Cashier, and Cashier Shift searches preserved, so that I can investigate a specific exchange.
9. As an Administrator, I want search wildcard characters treated literally, so that a search does not unexpectedly broaden my report.
10. As an Administrator, I want Cash-In and Cash-Out selections preserved, so that I can export either exchange type independently.
11. As an Administrator, I want matching records of all currently supported statuses preserved, so that transaction history does not silently become completed-only history.
12. As an Administrator, I want legacy reference-only records identified honestly, so that missing historical evidence is not presented as recorded money movement.
13. As an Administrator, I want transaction ordering preserved, so that list and export review remain predictable.
14. As an Administrator, I want export to include records beyond the current displayed page, so that pagination never truncates my report.
15. As an Administrator, I want an empty selection to produce a valid header-only CSV, so that no matches is distinguishable from failure.
16. As an Administrator, I want invalid selections rejected before attachment delivery, so that invalid reports do not look successful.
17. As an Administrator, I want a retrieval or staging failure to prevent the download, so that I never receive a partial file presented as complete.
18. As an Administrator, I want CSV formula protection retained, so that exported text remains safe to open in spreadsheet software.
19. As an Administrator, I want CSV headings, column order, encoding, filename, and values preserved, so that existing review habits keep working.
20. As an Administrator, I want leading zeroes in GCash references preserved in exported text, so that the file retains the recorded reference.
21. As an Administrator, I want completed-activity totals governed by period and Cashier, so that local search and exchange-type filters do not change their meaning.
22. As an Administrator, I want recorded GCash Service Cash and GCash Service Wallet evidence independent of report filters, so that selected history cannot masquerade as current fund evidence.
23. As an Administrator, I want unresolved activity and reconciliation reviews to remain Store-wide, so that outstanding work is never hidden by report selection.
24. As a Super Administrator, I want existing authorized reporting access retained, so that this refactor does not change Workspace authority.
25. As a Cashier, I want existing access restrictions preserved, so that Administrator reporting does not become available through a newly exposed traversal operation.
26. As an Administrator, I want list refresh and pagination to retain their current behavior, so that export improvements do not disrupt daily review.
27. As a maintainer, I want matching selection and traversal owned by one reporting implementation, so that future fixes have locality across list and export callers.
28. As a maintainer, I want behavior checked through existing reporting seams, so that internal refactoring does not force a new abstraction or brittle tests.

## Implementation Decisions

- Deepen the existing GCash Service reporting module. Reuse existing injected PDO access, authorization, date validation, matching predicates, and record interpretation rather than introducing a generic repository or a new adapter hierarchy.
- The reporting module owns complete matching-record traversal. The CSV adapter must not manage page numbers or call the full overview to obtain each batch.
- Select the export path before any full-overview assembly. Export should not depend on recorded balances, completed-activity aggregates, unresolved reviews, reconciliation history, or Cashier-choice queries succeeding.
- Share matching selection between the existing overview operation and traversal. Preserve period, Cashier, search, exchange type, supported statuses, ordering, and legacy evidence semantics.
- Keep the existing overview interface and externally observable response fields compatible. A narrowly scoped traversal capability may be added to the existing reporting module; its concrete shape is left to implementation and must hide traversal mechanics from callers.
- Preserve three distinct meanings: completed activity follows period and Cashier; matching history additionally follows search and type and includes current historical statuses; recorded funds and outstanding reviews remain Store-wide.
- Preserve role and active Workspace checks at the existing seams. Traversal must enforce existing reporting authorization independently of full-overview assembly.
- Keep CSV-specific headings, field mapping, formula neutralization, quoting, UTF-8 BOM, filename, response headers, and complete-file staging in the CSV adapter.
- Stage the entire CSV before sending attachment headers or body. Failed validation, retrieval, or staging must not produce a partial attachment; preserve the current distinction between rejected selection and failed export.
- Traverse in bounded batches using existing database capabilities. Do not materialize all matching records in application memory merely to simplify traversal; staged CSV storage may spill to disk as it does today.
- Preserve historical reference strings and existing legacy masking. Do not infer principal, fee, or movement evidence that was never recorded.
- Preserve existing transaction ordering. This task does not introduce a new point-in-time snapshot guarantee for exports during concurrent writes.
- No schema migration, new dependency, new configuration, new public route, or change to financial posting is required.
- Preserve the authority decisions in ADR-0001 and the Receipt History distinction in ADR-0010. Do not alter receipt immutability, access, or printing decisions in ADR-0006 and the GCash Service Receipt specification.

## Testing Decisions

- Proposed primary acceptance seam: the existing authenticated GCash Overview HTTP route, including its CSV response. Use this highest existing seam to verify complete downloads, authorization, filter agreement, format, and all-or-nothing failure behavior.
- Reuse existing reporting-module integration checks with a disposable database for scope and record-selection behavior. Do not invent a new test-only interface or require public access to internal helpers.
- Existing prior art includes the GCash transaction integration suite and Administrator overview browser suite: Philippine dates, independent fund evidence, Store-wide reviews, 105-row export, legacy evidence, formula neutralization, invalid selections, and staging failure are already covered.
- Exercise empty, one-batch, exact-batch, and multi-batch selections. Assert the complete expected ordered record set without duplicates or omissions against a stable fixture; do not assert an internal batch-size constant.
- Verify export ignores the displayed list page and respects period, Cashier, literal search, and exchange-type selection across the entire matching set.
- Verify legacy records, supported statuses, reference strings, column order, encoding, and formula-leading text remain correctly represented in the downloaded file.
- Verify invalid or unauthorized requests cannot yield a successful CSV attachment. Cover retrieval failure after an initial batch and staging failure; neither may deliver partial success.
- Add a focused HTTP acceptance check using the existing disposable-fixture/failure-router pattern: exporting valid matching rows still succeeds when overview-only retrieval is unavailable. This protects the removal of unrelated work without matching SQL strings, counting exact queries, timing thresholds, or exposing new test hooks.
- Retain overview acceptance checks that completed totals ignore search/type filters, recorded funds ignore report filters, and unresolved/reconciliation reviews remain Store-wide.
- Test observable behavior through existing interfaces, not private methods, exact internal call sequences, or code structure. Replace redundant checks when consolidated behavior already covers them.
- The user confirmed the existing authenticated Overview/CSV HTTP route as the primary acceptance seam, retaining disposable-database integration checks for reporting rules.

## Out of Scope

- The separate architecture candidates for completion-result consistency and shared Cashier/Administrator record interpretation, except the minimum internal reuse necessary for reporting traversal.
- A broad rewrite or split of the GCash Service module, a general reporting framework, or a new repository abstraction.
- Changes to fee calculation, financial movement recording, Cashier Shift behavior, receipt preservation, reprinting, or opt-in printing.
- New filters, columns, reports, export formats, background jobs, progress indicators, caching, or public routes.
- New snapshot isolation guarantees for concurrent activity, arbitrary performance targets, or claims of a measured speedup.
- Schema changes, dependency additions, and unrelated interface redesign.

## Further Notes

Selected from the architecture review's strongest candidate: concentrate selection and traversal for locality, and give overview/export callers leverage through reporting depth.

Current evidence shows repeated full-overview work per export batch. Existing tests were inspected, not executed during specification. Implementation should run the affected disposable-database integration and HTTP/browser checks.

The user confirmed the proposed test seams. Apply the ready-for-agent triage label. Review date: 25 October 2026, Asia/Manila.

Let Cashiers reopen their own saved GCash Service Receipts from GCash History and Administrators reopen Store-wide receipts from GCash Overview. Reuse the shared saved-receipt modal and manual printing path for every supported completed exchange type.

Later Store/fee settings, identity changes, and linked audited corrections leave the receipt unchanged.
- [ ] Use the current printing Register's configured 58/80 mm width, with the existing 80 mm fallback when no Register resolves. Check long Store details, Cashier/Register names, and maximum-length references at both widths without clipped amounts or digits.

- [ ] Receipt retrieval, manual printing, print cancellation, and print retries are read-only and never invoke completion, resolution, or financial posting. Do not add GCash exchanges to Sales Transactions receipt history or Product sales reporting.
- [ ] Extend existing Cashier GCash History, Administrator GCash Overview, receipt-modal browser/API, and database integration checks for allowed/denied access, absent snapshots, saved-content stability, read-only printing, and 58/80 mm presentation. Exercise Cash-Out and later-completed receipts when those slices are available; those slices remain responsible for their creation paths.

## What to build

Give later completion of Needs checking Cash-In and Cash-Out exchanges the same saved customer proof as direct completion. Cover both the Cashier resolution workflow and Administrator resolution through GCash Overview without changing existing resolution authority.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Needs checking records have no completed receipt. Resolving an exchange to Completed preserves the completion-time customer receipt atomically, returns its saved-receipt locator, and opens the shared modal in the resolving workflow.

- [ ] Preserve authentication, Workspace permissions, resolution authority, shift/write checks, CSRF, protected audit, and duplicate-reference safeguards. Enforce own-only Cashier receipt retrieval and Store-wide Administrator retrieval on direct requests.
- [ ] Add an unchecked Print receipt automatically choice to each completion review in both resolution workflows. Reset the choice for every review; cancellation never prints. After successful completion, request printing once only if selected.
- [ ] Manual Print remains available after print cancellation/failure, without repeating resolution or posting money. Refresh and reopening never automatically print; Close returns to the existing workflow with correct keyboard focus.

body:
## Parent

Part of #289. Follow its confirmed GCash Service Receipt specification and exclusions.

## What to build

After successful Cash-Out, open its saved GCash Service Receipt using the shared completion, retrieval, modal, barcode, and printing path. Explain what the customer actually handed over and received for either fee method.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Atomically preserve a receipt when Cash-Out becomes Completed, return its saved-receipt locator, and open the shared GCash modal. Failed completion or protected-audit rollback leaves neither a receipt nor partial money posting; retries cannot duplicate snapshots or financial effects.
- [ ] With PHP 1,000 principal and PHP 10 Fee via GCash, show PHP 1,010 wallet received and PHP 1,000 cash paid out.
- [ ] With PHP 1,000 principal and PHP 10 cash fee, show PHP 1,000 wallet received, PHP 10 cash collected, and PHP 1,000 cash paid out separately. Do not substitute net Store balance deltas or an ambiguous total for customer-facing amounts.
- [ ] Show principal, service fee, and fee method distinctly; preserve exact monetary handling, including centavo fees. Receipt integration does not change fee rules, balances, state rules, correction authority, or existing reference checks.
- [ ] Reuse saved completion-time Store/footer, Cashier/Register, identity, timestamp, amounts, and full reference. Later settings changes and linked corrections leave the original receipt unchanged. Enforce own-only Cashier access for direct requests.
- [ ] Provide manual Print and an unchecked automatic-print choice for every Cash-Out completion review. Print automatically once only after successful persistence if selected; never on failure, refresh, or reopen. Printing cancellation/failure leaves the saved exchange available for retry.
- [ ] Reuse the centered barcode/digits and current Register 58/80 mm presentation, with no clipping for maximum reference length or long labels. Keep internal operational information private and GCash receipts separate from Product sales receipt history.
- [ ] Extend existing GCash browser/API and database integration checks for both PHP 1,000 examples, centavo fees, receipt access, rollback/retry, print behavior, immutable details, and unchanged financial posting.

body:
# GCash Service Receipts

Confirmed 2026-10-24. Implementation specification.

## Problem Statement

Cashiers can complete GCash Cash-In and Cash-Out exchanges but cannot give customers a matching receipt or reprint one from GCash history. Customers need a clear record of the exchange, its fee, and its reference. The reference should be readable and scannable on the printed receipt.

## Solution

Show a saved GCash Service Receipt after each completed exchange, using the existing POS receipt modal's appearance and centered thermal-paper preview. Center a barcode of the saved GCash reference with the reference digits beneath it. Support the existing Register's 58 mm or 80 mm paper width, manual printing, and an unchecked per-transaction automatic-print option. Cashiers can reprint their own receipts; Administrators can reprint Store-wide receipts through GCash Overview.

## User Stories

1. As a Cashier, I want a receipt after completing Cash-In, so that I can give the customer proof of the recorded exchange.
2. As a Cashier, I want a receipt after completing Cash-Out, so that I can document the cash handed over and the service fee.
3. As a Cashier, I want both Cash-Out fee methods represented accurately, so that the receipt explains cash and wallet exchanges correctly.
4. As a Cashier, I want Needs checking exchanges excluded from completed receipts, so that unfinished exchanges do not appear complete.
5. As a Cashier, I want a receipt when a Needs checking exchange is later completed, so that delayed completion has the same customer proof.
6. As a Cashier, I want the receipt modal to match the POS receipt modal, so that reviewing and printing feel familiar.
7. As a Cashier, I want the paper preview and action buttons centered, so that the modal follows the supplied POS example.
8. As a customer, I want the GCash reference barcode centered on the receipt, so that staff can scan it easily.
9. As a customer, I want readable reference digits beneath the barcode, so that the reference remains useful without a scanner.
10. As a customer, I want leading zeroes preserved, so that the printed and scanned reference match the original transfer.
11. As a customer, I want the exchange type, transaction number, and completion date/time, so that I can identify the exchange.
12. As a customer, I want Store details, Cashier, and Register identification, so that I know where and by whom the exchange was recorded.
13. As a customer, I want the principal, service fee, and fee method shown separately, so that the cost is clear.
14. As a customer, I want cash collected, cash paid out, and wallet transfers labeled accurately, so that I can check what changed hands.
15. As a Cashier, I want the customer copy to omit internal notes and Store balances, so that operational information stays private.
16. As a Cashier, I want a manual Print Receipt button, so that I can print or retry when needed.
17. As a Cashier, I want an unchecked Print receipt automatically option for each completion review, so that printing starts only when I request it.
18. As a Cashier, I want failed completions never to print, so that an unsuccessful operation cannot produce proof of completion.
19. As a Cashier, I want canceling or failing printing to leave the exchange saved, so that I can retry printing without repeating money movements.
20. As a Cashier, I want refreshes and reprints not to print automatically, so that reopening a receipt does not create unexpected copies.
21. As a Cashier, I want receipts to follow the current printing Register's 58/80 mm width, so that the layout fits the available thermal roll.
22. As a Cashier, I want to reopen my saved receipts from GCash History, so that I can replace a lost copy.
23. As an Administrator, I want to reopen Store-wide receipts from GCash Overview, so that I can investigate or reprint an exchange.
24. As a Store owner, I want receipt access to respect existing workspace permissions, so that Cashiers cannot retrieve other Cashiers' receipts.
25. As a customer, I want reprints to retain completion-time Store, Register, amount, and footer details, so that later setting changes do not rewrite my receipt.
26. As an Administrator, I want a later audited correction to leave the original receipt unchanged, so that the original exchange remains traceable.
27. As a Cashier, I want long references and labels to remain readable on narrow paper, so that information is not clipped.
28. As a Cashier, I want to close the receipt and return to the existing GCash workflow, so that receipt viewing does not start another exchange.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing GCash transaction completion and later-resolution workflows to preserve receipt details atomically when an exchange becomes Completed. A Needs checking record does not qualify. Failed or rolled-back completion must not leave a receipt.
- Persist the customer-facing Store, Register, Cashier, transaction identity, completion timestamp, exchange type, principal, fee, fee method, actual customer cash/wallet exchange amounts, reference, and footer needed for faithful reprints. Use completion-time values, not mutable current settings. Retain saved values after linked audited corrections; separate correction receipts are outside scope.
- Keep GCash Service Receipts distinct from Sale Receipts and Refund Receipts. Do not add service exchanges to Product sales or Sales Transactions receipt history. Keep GCash receipts in their existing GCash history/overview contexts.
- Reuse the existing POS receipt modal shell, shared thermal presentation, print behavior, Register width resolution, and saved-receipt conventions. Follow the supplied POS example: header and Close control, completion banner, centered actions, and centered paper preview. Use GCash-specific wording and a workflow-appropriate return action; do not label an exchange as a sale or display a fabricated change-due amount.
- Use the existing Code 128 SVG barcode renderer. Encode only the saved normalized GCash reference as text, preserving leading zeroes. Center the barcode and readable digits beneath it on both preview and print. Retain sufficient quiet space and validate readability within both roll widths. Do not truncate reference data to make it fit.
- A barcode represents a recorded reference, not independent GCash verification. No new scan-to-open or scan-to-complete workflow is introduced. Preserve existing reference capture, duplicate checks, and manual verification rules.
- Label the financial amounts by their actual purpose rather than an ambiguous total. For PHP 1,000 principal and PHP 10 fee: Cash-In collects PHP 1,010 cash and sends PHP 1,000 by wallet; Cash-Out with wallet fee receives PHP 1,010 by wallet and pays PHP 1,000 cash; Cash-Out with cash fee receives PHP 1,000 by wallet, collects PHP 10 cash, and pays PHP 1,000 cash. Do not substitute net Store balance deltas for these customer-facing amounts.
- Exclude internal notes, service cash/wallet balances, reconciliation details, and new customer name/phone collection.
- Extend successful completion responses with a saved-receipt locator suitable for opening the shared modal. Render and retrieve only persisted Completed exchange receipts. Reopening and printing are read-only and must never invoke completion or repost financial movements.
- Add an unchecked Print receipt automatically choice to each completion confirmation, including later resolution to Completed. After successful persistence, open the receipt and request printing once only if selected. Failed operations never print. Refresh, history retrieval, and reopening never automatically print. Manual Print remains available after cancellation or failure.
- Use the current printing Register's configured 58 mm or 80 mm width, with the existing 80 mm fallback when no current Register resolves. Browser and installed driver handle the printer, margins, feed, and cutting. The application does not confirm physical paper output.
- Add receipt actions to Cashier GCash History and Administrator GCash Overview. Preserve own-only Cashier access and Store-wide Administrator access, enforced on the server for direct receipt requests as well as visible actions. Receipt retrieval does not require replaying a financial write.
- Preserve existing authentication, workspace, shift/write checks, CSRF protection for writes, protected audit behavior, duplicate-reference protections, and exact monetary handling. Receipt integration must not change fees, balances, exchange state rules, or correction authority.
- The project is in development: no legacy receipt reconstruction, historical-data notices, or backfill is required. Preserve existing records without inventing receipt snapshots. Entries without a saved receipt do not expose an actionable receipt link. Maintain fresh-install/migration parity and existing backup coverage for persisted receipt data.
- Reuse existing modules and dependencies; no new barcode or printing package is needed.

## Testing Decisions

- User confirmed reuse of existing GCash browser/API workflow tests and receipt-modal tests, backed by database integration checks for saved details and permissions. Prefer these highest existing seams over a new framework or private-helper tests.
- Test externally visible outcomes: a successful completion opens its saved receipt; amounts and reference match the exchange; history retrieval returns the same receipt; unauthorized access fails; printing never changes financial state.
- Cover Cash-In and both Cash-Out fee methods, including the PHP 1,000 examples, centavo fees, and readable separate collection/payout labels.
- Cover direct completion, Needs checking without a receipt, and later resolution to Completed with a receipt. Verify failed completion and audit rollback leave neither a receipt nor partial money posting; retries do not create duplicate receipt snapshots or financial effects.
- Verify Cashier own-only retrieval and Administrator Store-wide retrieval, including direct endpoint requests for another Cashier's exchange.
- Change Store settings, Cashier display details, Register name, and fee settings after completion and verify saved receipt content remains stable. Record a linked audited correction and verify the original receipt is unchanged.
- Exercise centered modal presentation, keyboard focus/Close behavior, manual Print, unchecked defaults for every confirmation, selected automatic printing exactly once, and no automatic print on refresh or history reopen.
- Verify barcode payload and readable digits preserve the complete reference and leading zeroes. Check preview and print layout at 58/80 mm with maximum configured reference length, long Store details, and long Cashier/Register names; no clipped amounts or reference digits.
- Use existing receipt presentation fixtures and disposable database integration patterns. Verify schema setup and backup retention for added receipt data through existing project checks.
- Browser checks do not establish physical scan reliability. When hardware is available, print and scan both widths, especially the longest supported references, and check driver scaling and margins. Do not claim hardware compatibility without that check.

## Out of Scope

- Legacy-data support, historical reconstruction, backfill, and development-data cleanup.
- GCash transfers, provider verification APIs, wallet credentials, or live balance integration.
- Customer data collection, receipt photos, separate adjustment receipts, and changes to existing correction workflows.
- New scanner workflows, hardware purchases, and guaranteed printer/scanner compatibility.
- Direct device access, ESC/POS, printer discovery/selection, drawer/cutter control, and guaranteed silent printing.
- Changes to Product sales, inventory, fee rules, GCash financial posting, or other receipt layouts.

## Further Notes

- The user confirmed centered reference barcode/digits and the existing POS receipt modal appearance using a screenshot.
- The user confirmed all reprint, preservation, and later-completion decisions, and explicitly waived legacy handling because the project is in development.
- Related specifications: [GCash service](../gcash-service-spec.md), [thermal customer receipts](thermal-customer-receipts.md), and [opt-in receipt printing](opt-in-receipt-printing.md).
- Specification only. No application implementation or runtime tests are part of this task.
title: Add GCash cash-in and cash-out receipts with centered reference barcodes
