title: Restore Store state while preserving destination security

body:
## Problem Statement

The Store owner needs to restore or migrate without confusing different people, losing destination security authority, or becoming stranded after partial replacement. The encrypted-package baseline provides capture, download and read-only preflight but is not integrated into current main. Existing database-only, CLI-only SQL recovery cannot recover the complete Store through the accepted browser workflow.

## Solution

Provide destination-side, Super Administrator-controlled Identity Reconciliation and verified complete encrypted destination safety capture before destructive replacement. After interruption, the initiating administrator or a destination Super Administrator authorized before replacement can authenticate through the browser even with missing users, then restore the original safety copy or restart the exact approved incoming replacement from the beginning. Keep ordinary operations closed until coherent database, uploads and security pass verification and an authorized operator explicitly reopens them.

Extend the shared workflow. This ticket supplies preparation, safety and recovery safeguards for downstream ordinary restore delivery; it does not enable an unfinished ordinary replacement path.

## User Stories

1. As a Super Administrator, I want destination-side preparation, so that an unavailable source installation does not prevent reconciliation.
2. As a Super Administrator, I want to see source and destination people and every ID, username and email conflict, so that matching values cannot silently combine people.
3. As a Super Administrator, I want to explicitly confirm same-person links, so that attribution is deliberate and reviewable.
4. As a destination account holder, I want linked history to preserve my destination password, status, roles, security state and profile, so that import cannot change my access.
5. As a Super Administrator, I want distinct people assigned deliberately chosen unused login details, so that no identity is silently overwritten or renamed.
6. As a Super Administrator, I want to explicitly clear optional conflicting emails, so that reconciliation does not invent contact addresses.
7. As a Store owner, I want source privileged-only and Recovery Account identities retained as Historical Actors, so that history survives without imported privileged authority.
8. As a Super Administrator, I want Historical Actors excluded from authentication, reset, activation and role assignment, so that history-only identities cannot become usable accounts.
9. As a Super Administrator, I want ordinary imported roles checked against destination fixed role templates, so that staff import cannot introduce arbitrary permissions.
10. As a Store owner, I want at least one active ordinary Administrator in the reviewed result, so that operational administration survives without automatic promotion.
11. As an Administrator, I want receipts, sales, approvals and audit evidence attributed to their original people and installations, so that collisions do not rewrite history.
12. As a destination Super Administrator, I want privileged access, sealed Recovery Account state, security settings and evidence preserved together, so that the receiving installation remains authoritative.
13. As a Super Administrator, I want approval bound to the exact package and relevant destination state, so that stale preparation cannot authorize different data or access.
14. As an Administrator, I want the later restore workflow to consume valid preparation, so that I do not need authority to approve privileged reconciliation.
15. As a restoring administrator, I want a verified encrypted safety copy containing destination database and uploads, so that complete fallback exists before replacement.
16. As a Store owner, I want a separate safety-copy passphrase retained outside both servers, so that fallback does not depend on the incoming secret or surviving server.
17. As a restoring administrator, I want failed safety capture or verification to leave records and files unchanged, so that failed prerequisites cannot destroy data.
18. As an authorized recovery operator, I want browser recovery with missing or partial users, so that interruption does not require ordinary database login or terminal access.
19. As an initiating administrator, I want recovery authenticated with my own pre-restore password, so that imported accounts cannot control the pending operation.
20. As a pre-authorized destination Super Administrator, I want to recover with my own protected pre-restore authority, so that recovery is not dependent on the initiating person alone.
21. As a recovery operator, I want safety recovery without incoming material, so that losing the incoming package does not remove a valid fallback.
22. As a recovery operator, I want to restart the exact approved incoming replacement from the beginning, so that interruption does not force abandonment of an approved transfer.
23. As a Store owner, I want the original verified safety copy retained through every retry, so that partial state never becomes the fallback.
24. As a recovery operator, I want missing, changed or invalid required inputs reported while operations stay blocked, so that recovery never guesses mappings or substitutes packages.
25. As a Store operator, I want durable maintenance across requests, timeouts and worker death, so that sales and background writers cannot use partial state.
26. As a recovery operator, I want controlled sign-in, stock, receipt, image and report checks before explicit reopening, so that automated success does not imply operational readiness.
27. As a Store owner, I want old sessions rejected after replacement and recovery, so that imported session fields cannot restore stale access.
28. As a Super Administrator, I want private recovery checkpoints and append-only evidence independent of replaced tables, so that interruption cannot erase authority or outcomes.
29. As a recovery operator, I want accessible browser progress and errors without exposed secrets, so that recovery remains understandable and private.
30. As a Store owner, I want disposable test evidence and honest reporting of missing hosted proof, so that local success is not mistaken for migration readiness.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing RMSTORE1 encrypted-package contract and capture/download/read-only-preflight foundation. Integrate in a dedicated worktree preserving root WIP. Reconcile against current main; retain both encrypted-package/image/passphrase fixtures and the current GCash receipt-details round-trip assertion when resolving the known test conflict. Historical baseline tests do not establish integrated correctness.
- Reconcile the older security inventory with current retired-storage migrations. Do not recreate removed privilege, preserved-activity or emergency-session tables. Add only the targeted nullable ordinary-role reference needed for Historical Actors and necessary provenance storage. Require compatible migrated schemas on both installations; retain exact-schema package checks.
- Reuse preflight, user lifecycle rules, fixed role templates and authorization for destination review. Show conflicts and resulting access before approval. Numeric IDs, names, usernames and emails never automatically establish a same-person link. Links retain destination access/profile/status; distinct operational people require explicit unused login details. Source Recovery identities remain history-only and destination Recovery Accounts are not ordinary link targets.
- Represent Historical Actors as disabled roleless identities with no memberships, recovery flags/account rows, usable passwords, reset tokens or sessions. Retain original names/login details/roles in origin-aware provenance and unique internal historical identifiers without invented contact addresses. Enforce the invariant throughout login, sessions, reset and lifecycle/management entry points. Do not globally loosen existing role joins.
- Allocate explicit collision-free source-to-local identity and file mappings. Validate all declared foreign keys and logical actor references, including approval/revision actors, audit subjects/payloads, settings identities, notification recipients and external evidence. Keep original receipt/audit JSON snapshots unchanged; interpret embedded IDs through provenance instead of globally replacing numbers. Preserve historical names and required images without replacing protected destination profiles. Count resulting active ordinary Administrators; if absent, require an explicit eligible designation or supported account preparation, never automatic promotion.
- Preserve the destination security dependent closure: protected users identified by primary AND secondary privileged memberships and Recovery flags/account membership; complete auth/status/roles/profiles; sealed recovery state; fixed capability policy; platform settings, platform-scoped attention settings and technical forecasting configuration; classified security/recovery/platform/account-management evidence; login attempts and review watermarks; valid protected reset state; protected/platform notifications, preferences and attention state; backup and email-delivery evidence; and dependent actors/logical references. Retain evidence-only destination actors without reviving login. Preserve origin and collision-free evidence IDs. Source historical evidence cannot become active destination authority, review state, reset permission or sessions. External recovery/session state, environment credentials, URLs and application/server logs remain destination-owned.
- Bind protected preparation evidence to the approving Super Administrator, exact package, explicit identity/file mappings, conflict resolutions, any Administrator designation and resulting access. Revalidate package integrity, current authority, required credentials, relevant destination state and mappings immediately before destruction. Relevant changes invalidate approval. Ordinary Administrators may consume valid preparation later but cannot approve or alter privileged reconciliation.
- Capture affected destination database and uploads under coordinated exclusion, encrypt with a separately supplied safety passphrase, fully verify and durably retain the complete safety copy before destructive writes. Capture/encryption/storage/verification failure leaves destination records/files unchanged. Never replace the original verified safety artifact with partial state during retries. The authorized custodian retains recovery secrets outside both servers; the incoming secret is not assumed to decrypt safety material.
- Extend RecoveryStore, BackupCoordinator, StoreWriteGate and shared restore/preflight services; do not create another restore engine. Persist protected pre-restore password verifiers, operation-bound authority, approved package/plan identifiers, preserved security checkpoint, safety metadata, stages, session invalidation and append-only outcomes outside publicly served and replaceable storage. Do not persist plaintext passwords/passphrases or decrypted database/uploads as a recovery shortcut; never put secrets in URLs, logs or issue evidence.
- Browser recovery must render/authenticate without querying partial application tables. Permit only the initiator and destination Super Administrators authorized before replacement, each using their own pre-restore password. Preserve separate sealed Recovery Account rules. Require fresh authentication, operation binding, CSRF/request protection, externally maintained throttling and recovery-session expiry. Imported identities, unrelated Administrators and ordinary sessions cannot recover or reopen.
- Offer complete safety recovery using authenticated authority and its safety passphrase without incoming material. Incoming restart additionally requires the original incoming passphrase and exact approved package/plan; validate against the retained destination checkpoint, not partial live tables. Restart deterministically from the beginning with approved mappings. Missing/changed safety material, checkpoint or applicable incoming inputs fails closed. Do not implement statement-by-statement or file-offset continuation after crashes.
- Persist observable stages for preparation/safety verification, destructive start, database replacement, uploads, automated verification, operator review pending, recovery required and explicit reopened completion. Persist destructive start before the first destructive write. Use existing request/exclusive locks plus durable fencing to block ordinary requests and independent writers across requests and worker death. Missing/uncertain coordination state cannot mean success. Do not depend on transactional DDL rollback or let browser timeout release maintenance/discard safety material.
- Both recovery paths verify database, uploads, retained destination authority and attribution together. Permit controlled sign-in/stock/receipt/image/report checks while ordinary sales and background writers remain closed. Require recorded successful checks and explicit freshly authenticated reopening; record who reopened and which path completed. Invalidate every old session independently of restored account session-version fields, including across crashes and reopening. Retain original safety material and append-only outcomes across retries and review. Respect the one-active-Store constraint.
- Reach shared preparation/recovery services, browser forms/routes and request admission, authorization/session/reset/lifecycle guards, affected CLI callers, schema/provenance, history queries, fixtures, tests and operator guidance. Update domain/context and ADR explanations to distinguish accepted target from implemented behavior. Keep ordinary encrypted replacement disabled until dependent delivery is complete; downstream entry points must use shared safeguards without bypasses.
- Browser recovery requires functioning compatible application/PHP, reachable HTTPS, usable database service, durable private worker-accessible storage, reliable locking and measured capacity. Use bounded retryable execution if target limits require it. Infrastructure outage requires authorized infrastructure repair; no public bypass or automatic total-host-loss recovery is promised. Unsupported hosted forecasting stays unavailable; source jobs/models are not implicitly destination-ready.

## Testing Decisions

The user confirmed the existing browser workflow as the primary seam, backed by real MySQL/filesystem integration tests. Assert observable access, attribution, durable stages, file integrity and Store state rather than private helpers. Reuse shared production workflow boundaries and existing failure-injection fixtures.

- Extend existing encrypted-package browser tests for destination reconciliation, both authorized recovery operators, role denial, wrong credentials, CSRF, throttling/expiry, accessible errors/progress, controlled verification and explicit reopening. Missing/partial users must neither prevent valid recovery nor admit ordinary users. Preserve capture/download/preflight checks through both administrator screens; full ordinary restore rollout remains downstream.
- Extend the existing real-MySQL backup/restore integration workflow with guarded disposable source/destination databases, private uploads, the complete migrated schema and predeclared expected results. Reuse PDO interruption and writer-coordination fixtures; inject additional failures at the shared workflow boundary where necessary.
- Cover seeded numeric collisions, distinct people sharing usernames/emails, explicit links, optional-email clearing, secondary privileged memberships, source Recovery identities, ordinary-role import, destination linked-account state and zero/multiple active ordinary Administrators. Package or relevant destination-state changes invalidate preparation before destruction.
- Exercise Historical Actor refusal through real login, session, reset, activation and role-assignment paths while historical names remain visible. Check exact sales/GCash/refund/approval/revision/audit attribution, unchanged JSON snapshots, origin-aware embedded identities, preserved review state and logical recipients, and historical/protected image collisions and hashes.
- Fail safety database/upload capture, encryption, storage and verification independently; assert no destructive changes. Check private artifact access and absence of exposed plaintext credentials/data.
- Interrupt before destruction, during database replacement, during uploads, before verification and during operator review, including worker termination/timeouts and repeated crashes. Verify durable stages, concurrent writer exclusion, original safety-artifact integrity and append-only evidence across requests.
- With users missing or partial, authenticate each permitted operator independently. Reject unrelated/imported actors, forged/expired requests and wrong passwords/passphrases. Prove safety recovery without incoming material and incoming restart with exact approved package/plan/checkpoint from the beginning. Missing safety/checkpoint material never permits an unsafe restart.
- Compare exact database relationships, destination account/security state, stock/batch/ledger quantities, receipt identities/items/totals, selected reports and upload hashes. Failure keeps ordinary activity closed. Automated success leaves review pending until controlled checks and explicit authorized reopening; old sessions stay invalid afterward.
- Retain package-format hostile-input checks for wrong passphrases, tampering/truncation, incompatible schema, unsafe SQL/member paths and resource limits. Re-run relevant route, capability, lifecycle and encrypted-reset regressions on the integrated current schema.
- Use disposable data only; no live Store or Hosted Demo imports. Record exact commit/schema/runtime and executed versus deferred checks. Actual matching-runtime bidirectional hosted browser drills, effective capacity, persistence, isolation and complete failure recovery remain mandatory under the existing proof ticket. Local simulation is not hosted proof.

## Out of Scope

- General account merging, automatic identity matching, arbitrary capability import, multi-Store support and synchronization of divergent sales.
- New package formats, speculative abstractions, legacy SQL conversion and ordinary plaintext restore support.
- Full ordinary Super Administrator/Administrator restore rollout, source cutover controls and complete bidirectional readiness certification; these remain existing downstream delivery work. This ticket's recovery safeguards still require executable disposable integration/browser coverage before rollout.
- Production deployment, real Store movement, purchases, DNS changes, destructive Hosted Demo tests and further hosting writes. Prior empty temporary-site creation does not authorize application deployment or database import.
- Terminal-only recovery, unauthenticated bypasses, deleting failure markers to reopen, and automatic recovery on unavailable application infrastructure.
- Forecasting platform migration, cloud storage, new schedules and retention automation.

## Further Notes

Part of [Encrypted backups, safe Database Restore, and localhost-hosting Store Migration](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/282). This expands the existing identity-and-safety-recovery delivery ticket; retain its parentage and dependency relationships.

Accepted decisions: [Establish the reusable encrypted-backup implementation baseline](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/303), [Choose explicit identity reconciliation and destination-security preservation](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/304), [Choose complete safety-copy custody and interrupted-restore recovery](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/305), and [Choose disposable hosting proof and Store cutover readiness gates](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/306).

This synthesis adds no new human policy choice. The accepted browser/two-path recovery decision supersedes older offline/CLI wording. ADR-0017 and the parent specification remain authoritative; reconcile older documentation describing identity policy as unresolved with the closed decisions during implementation.

Downstream work remains [Restore Store state while preserving destination security](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/285), [Enable safe Administrator restore across all entry points](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/286), [Control Store Migration capture and activation](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/287), and [Prove migration and recovery in both deployment directions](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/288). Publishing this spec does not complete those deliverables.

Observed on 2026-10-25: current main is 5908190, reusable encrypted baseline is 65d800b, and root has unrelated WIP to preserve. Existing package limits are 48 MiB encrypted input, 32 MiB decoded contents, 100,000 rows, 2,000 images and 5 MiB per image; revalidate these constraints and actual fit. The disposable hosted site exists empty; deployed browser recovery, effective capacity and bidirectional readiness remain unproven.
title: Resolve identity conflicts and provide complete safety recovery

body:
## Parent

Part of #282 — Encrypted backups, safe Database Restore, and localhost-hosting Store Migration.

## What to build

Extend the existing shared Database Backup workflow so Administrator and Super Administrator can capture a coherent encrypted package containing the database and required uploaded Product/profile images, download it privately, and validate it before any replacement. Provide a read-only Super Administrator preflight using the current destination login password and the package's independent passphrase.

Reuse the existing backup, restore, coordination, authorization, and recovery boundaries. Follow #282's implementation/testing decisions and exclusions; no production deployment, purchases, live Store imports, or destructive Hosted Demo tests are authorized.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Choose a versioned authenticated package and password-based key derivation using maintained libraries supported by the checked deployment runtimes; record compatibility metadata and bounded resource requirements. Do not invent cryptography or promise removed legacy-format compatibility.
- [ ] Capture database and actual allowlisted uploads under one coordinated write pause. Exclude application code, environment secrets, unrelated files, source recovery state, and server-specific configuration. Round-trip Unicode, binary content, and valid image references.
- [ ] Update both existing administrator backup screens, guarded creation/download/history endpoints, system/scheduled capture callers, operation metadata, fixtures, and guidance coherently. Ordinary exports are encrypted only; do not retain a silent plaintext system-export path or add backup scheduling/cloud features.
- [ ] Enforce active account/session, active Workspace, CSRF where applicable, secondary-role authorization, and requester-bound downloads. Cashier and Inventory Manager cannot access packages. Keep temporary/decrypted artifacts private, clean up interrupted/expired captures, and distinguish capture readiness from delivery without claiming the browser saved a file.
- [ ] Require separate login-password and backup-passphrase fields for preflight. Wrong/currently obsolete credentials, wrong passphrases, and unsafe input fail without replacing records or uploads; never persist/log plaintext secrets or put them in filenames or URLs.
- [ ] Validate authentication, compatibility, complete/unique members, declared sizes, expansion limits, SQL statements, references, allowed destinations, and required files. Reject plaintext SQL, arbitrary SQL, truncation/tampering, traversal, absolute paths, links, executable/unexpected files, and excessive resource use.
- [ ] Define and document the explicit preserved security tables/rows and dependent references: privileged identity/authentication/authorization state including secondary memberships, sealed Recovery Account state, fixed role policy, security settings/logs, and external evidence. Identify operational replacement scope and provenance requirements; do not infer the boundary from names or password columns.
- [ ] Show actionable identity ID/username/email conflicts and validation/upload-limit results without exposing restricted records to unauthorized roles. Preflight never authorizes replacement or guesses actor identity.
- [ ] Extend real-MySQL workflow integration, focused hostile-format tests, and actual HTTP/administrator-screen coverage. Retain existing legacy recovery artifacts privately; explain off-server passphrase custody and irrecoverability if all copies are lost.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
title: Create, download, and preflight encrypted Store packages

body:
# Encrypted backups, safe Database Restore, and Store Migration

## Problem Statement

The Store owner needs recoverable backups and a dependable way to move the same Store between localhost and web hosting. A database-only SQL download leaves uploaded images behind, exposes captured records if stolen, and does not preserve the destination's privileged access when restored. Today, only the Super Administrator can restore, and full replacement also rolls back accounts, settings, and audit history.

The owner wants both Administrator roles to perform recovery without accidentally losing destination security controls, confusing historical staff identities, or operating two conflicting copies of the Store.

## Solution

Provide one encrypted, portable backup package containing a consistent database snapshot and the Store's required uploaded files. Both the Administrator and Super Administrator can create/download packages and perform Database Restore. Restore requires the current restoring user's destination login password and the separate passphrase used to create the selected package.

Support Store Migration in both directions between localhost and a separately prepared production hosting installation. Compatible application code and destination-specific configuration are installed first. Pause source operations and background writers for the final capture, transfer the package through download/upload, validate it, preserve destination security, retain a complete safety copy, and verify the destination before opening it for Store activity. Only one installation is active. This is replacement of Store state, not synchronization or merging of newer sales.

Keep destination Super Administrator and Recovery Account access, security settings, and security logs authoritative. Imported historical actions retain their correct actors. Reject ambiguous account conflicts before replacing anything. On the current hosting, Store operations may proceed after verification while forecasting remains unavailable; a compatible forecasting runtime is a later deployment choice.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want to create an encrypted backup, so that I can preserve the Store without depending on the technical owner.
2. As a Super Administrator, I want the same backup workflow, so that both authorized roles use one reliable capture process.
3. As an owner, I want the package to include Store data and uploaded Product/profile images, so that moving servers does not leave broken images behind.
4. As an owner, I want data and files captured consistently, so that the restored Store represents one coherent snapshot.
5. As an owner, I want stolen backup files to remain unreadable without their passphrase, so that possession alone does not expose Store records.
6. As an owner, I want a backup passphrase independent of login passwords, so that routine login-password changes do not invalidate backups.
7. As an owner, I want custody of the passphrase and a separate recovery copy outside both servers, so that server loss does not also destroy recovery access.
8. As an owner, I want clear guidance that losing all copies of a package's passphrase makes that package unusable, so that I do not expect a login-password reset to decrypt it.
9. As an authorized administrator, I want private, requester-bound downloads, so that another signed-in user cannot claim my temporary package.
10. As an authorized administrator, I want accurate backup history, so that capture completion is not mistaken for successful saving on my device.
11. As an Administrator, I want to perform Database Restore, so that routine recovery does not require Super Administrator presence when no security conflict exists.
12. As a Super Administrator, I want to retain restore and recovery authority, so that technical recovery remains possible.
13. As a Cashier or Inventory Manager, I must not gain backup or restore access, so that operational permissions do not expose complete Store copies.
14. As a restoring administrator, I want my current destination login password checked, so that possession of a backup is not enough to authorize replacement.
15. As a restoring administrator, I want to enter the selected backup's passphrase separately, so that authorization and decryption remain distinct.
16. As a restoring administrator, I want wrong passwords and passphrases rejected before replacement, so that mistakes leave the current Store intact.
17. As a restoring administrator, I want damaged, incomplete, incompatible, or unsafe packages rejected, so that an invalid package cannot partially replace the Store.
18. As an owner, I want a clear warning that an older snapshot replaces newer sales and other Store changes, so that I knowingly choose the recovery point.
19. As an owner, I want a verified destination safety copy saved before replacement, so that I can recover from an unsuccessful or mistaken restore.
20. As an owner, I want restore to abort if the safety copy cannot be saved, so that protection is never silently skipped.
21. As an owner, I want the Store kept closed after a partial failure, so that staff cannot sell against incomplete data or missing files.
22. As a recovery operator, I want a documented recovery procedure that works even if the users table is incomplete, so that failed replacement does not lock me out of recovery itself.
23. As a destination Super Administrator, I want my identity, credentials, role assignments, and security state preserved, so that an imported snapshot cannot replace my authority.
24. As an owner, I want the destination Recovery Account to remain usable under its existing sealed-recovery rules, so that migration does not undermine emergency access.
25. As a security owner, I want source privileged identities retained for attribution without automatically receiving destination privileged access, so that historical records survive without importing security authority.
26. As an auditor, I want every imported sale, approval, and historical action attributed to the correct person, so that colliding account IDs do not rewrite responsibility.
27. As a restoring administrator, I want conflicting account IDs, usernames, or emails reported before replacement, so that different people are never silently combined.
28. As a Super Administrator, I want a supported way to explicitly resolve reported identity conflicts before retrying, so that safe migration is possible without guessing or ad hoc database edits.
29. As a security owner, I want destination security settings and security logs preserved, so that restoring Store data cannot erase local security evidence or weaken access policy.
30. As an Administrator, I want Store sales, stock, operational staff, business settings, and history brought across, so that normal Store work continues from the selected snapshot.
31. As a security owner, I want imported restricted records kept under their existing visibility rules, so that Administrator restore access does not grant platform governance or restricted audit-screen access.
32. As an owner, I want to migrate localhost to hosting without exposing my local database publicly, so that a browser download/upload is sufficient to transfer the package.
33. As an owner, I want to migrate hosting back to localhost using the same workflow, so that changing the active host works in either direction.
34. As an owner, I want clear preparation instructions for compatible code, destination credentials, HTTPS, private storage, and resource limits, so that a backup is not mistaken for a complete server installer.
35. As an owner, I want destination configuration preserved, so that localhost URLs and credentials do not overwrite working hosting settings.
36. As an owner, I want source sales and background writers paused until cutover finishes, so that transactions cannot be stranded outside the transferred snapshot.
37. As an owner, I want verification before opening the destination, so that sign-in, stock, receipts, images, reports, and security controls are checked before selling resumes.
38. As an owner, I want a reminder to transfer fresh state before switching back after new sales, so that the inactive installation is never mistaken for an up-to-date fallback.
39. As an owner, I want the production hosting database isolated from the Hosted Demo, so that real records never replace or mingle with Demo Data.
40. As an owner, I want old forecasting jobs and source model pointers prevented from resuming on the destination, so that migration cannot silently use an invalid model or replay stale work.
41. As a Super Administrator, I want forecasting rebuilt and approved where the runtime supports it, so that forecasting resumes against the destination's actual data identity.
42. As an owner, I want verified sales and inventory to work while hosted forecasting is unavailable, so that the current hosting limitation does not block the rest of the Store.
43. As a restoring administrator, I want the new normal restore screen to accept encrypted packages only, so that plaintext SQL is not an alternate bypass.
44. As an owner, I want old SQL files retained privately until replacement encrypted backups have been restore-tested, so that introducing the new format does not destroy my existing recovery copies.
45. As a restoring administrator, I want clear progress, upload limits, rejection messages, and recovery instructions, so that I understand whether nothing changed, verification is pending, or recovery is required.
46. As a security owner, I want old sessions invalidated after restore and external restore evidence retained, so that rollback cannot revive stale access or erase who initiated replacement.
47. As an owner, I want migration and recovery proven using disposable installations, so that testing never destroys the live Store.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Reuse the existing workflow.** Extend DatabaseBackupService, DatabaseRestoreService, DatabaseSnapshotWriter, SqlBackupFormat, BackupCoordinator, RecoveryStore, StoreWriteGate, and the existing Administrator/Super Administrator screens and guarded entry points. Keep one capture/restore coordination path. Do not build a second exporter, job queue, synchronization engine, or general account-merging framework.
- **Narrow restore authorization.** Give both administrator roles explicit backup/restore authority without granting the Administrator PLATFORM_GOVERNANCE. Enforce authorization, current active account/session, active Workspace, and CSRF protection at every reachable endpoint, including legacy routes and downloads. Handle secondary role memberships consistently with the established authorization model; checking the primary role alone is insufficient.
- **Two distinct credentials.** Restore verifies the initiating administrator's current destination login password and decrypts using the package's original backup passphrase. Do not use login-password hashes as encryption keys or silently switch to login-password encryption. Never log or persist plaintext credentials, include them in filenames/URLs, or bundle a decryption key with the downloaded package. Passphrase changes for future packages do not change the secret needed for old packages.
- **Portable authenticated package.** Use a versioned format with authenticated encryption and an appropriate password-based key derivation mechanism from maintained, supported runtime libraries. Include compatibility metadata, the database snapshot, and required allowlisted uploads. Check available deployment libraries before choosing the format; do not invent cryptography. Ordinary backup output and the new ordinary restore input are encrypted packages only. Do not promise compatibility with the removed legacy encrypted format.
- **Safe package handling.** Validate decryption, complete contents, declared sizes, compatibility, database statements, references, security reconciliation, and allowed file destinations before replacement. Reject truncation, tampering, duplicate or missing members, path traversal, absolute paths, links, unexpected executable files, excessive expansion/resource use, and arbitrary SQL. Use the existing constrained SQL validation as appropriate; a checksum alone is not authentication. Reject unsafe input without overwriting destination files or Store records.
- **Coherent database and upload capture.** Cover the database and required uploaded Product/profile files under the same coordinated write pause. Define the allowlist from actual application storage. Exclude code, dependencies, environment credentials, server-specific paths, source recovery locks/state, and unrelated filesystem content. A package with only file references is not a complete migration package.
- **Private artifact lifecycle.** Keep temporary packages, decrypted staging, recovery material, and safety copies outside publicly served storage. Preserve requester binding and cleanup after delivery/expiry. Interrupted operations must not publish a partial package as complete. Backup history reports creation/delivery status truthfully and exposes only role-appropriate metadata.
- **Security boundary is an exception to full replacement.** The selected snapshot replaces Store operational records, operational accounts/roles, Store business settings, and historical records. Preserve destination privileged identities, full authentication and authorization state, Recovery Account sealing/activation data, platform security settings, security logs, and external restore evidence. Implement an explicit inventory of preserved tables/rows and dependent references; do not infer the boundary solely from table names, a password column, or primary role. Retain the fixed role/capability policy rather than importing arbitrary grants.
- **Source privileged identities and historical actors.** Retain source actors without granting source Super Administrator or Recovery Account authority. Remove imported privileged memberships; do not activate a source privileged-only account as a destination login. An existing legitimate operational role does not implicitly acquire privileged access. Preserve the correct actor for imported records and retained destination security history; never substitute a destination user merely because numeric IDs match.
- **Explicit identity conflict handling.** Preflight detects conflicting numeric identities, usernames, and emails and stops before replacement. Source and destination IDs do not prove two records are the same person. Provide a narrowly scoped, Super Administrator-controlled reconciliation/preparation procedure with explicit mappings where needed, validation of every dependent reference, and a retryable preflight. It must also work for a freshly provisioned destination whose seeded privileged IDs collide with source staff. Ordinary Administrator restore cannot resolve privileged conflicts implicitly. A supported workflow is required; instructing users to guess IDs or edit raw tables is not a complete implementation.
- **Preserved evidence remains distinguishable.** Keep existing destination security history and imported historical evidence attributable to their original identities; preserve provenance where both installations contribute records. Do not mix different actors or overwrite retained evidence through log-ID collisions. Existing Protected Audit Record visibility remains enforced. Administrator restore permission does not imply unrestricted inspection of protected records, even though an authorized holder of a decrypted complete backup can access its contents offline.
- **Safety copy covers the replacement scope.** Before destructive writes, create, verify, and retain a complete recoverable destination safety copy covering affected database records and uploads. Protect it with encryption/private storage and ensure the required decryption/recovery material survives a partially replaced database. Document which passphrase it requires. Do not overwrite the last good safety copy with partial state during a recovery retry. Abort before replacement if any part of safety capture or its verification fails.
- **Durable failure recovery.** Retain external locking, failure state, session invalidation, and append-only restore outcomes independently of the imported database. Track database/file replacement and verification so crashes cannot reopen an inconsistent Store. Recovery authenticates an authorized operator through protected pre-restore recovery state rather than trusting a partial users table; never save plaintext passwords. Provide and test a documented recovery path on localhost and the target hosting, including required console/SSH/operator access. Do not promise database DDL has transactional rollback or add an unauthenticated web bypass.
- **Transfer and activation.** Preparing a destination is separate from restoring. Use compatible application/schema versions and destination-specific database/mail/service configuration and private storage. Check required PHP extensions, limits, available memory/disk, upload allowance, and database compatibility before capture/import. Transfer via browser download/upload; no public localhost database or direct server-to-server database connection is required.
- **One active Store.** The final migration capture is taken after source sales and independent background writers are paused. Keep the source inactive through cutover. Destination verification precedes reopening for operations. Document how capture cancellation or migration abandonment returns the source to service only when the destination has not become active. The workflow is not automatic domain/DNS switching, automatic application deployment, or cross-server enforcement against an operator deliberately starting both copies.
- **Verify and invalidate sessions.** Validate database/file consistency, destination privileged/recovery access, operational sign-in, Product stock, Sale Receipts, reports, uploaded images, and job/security state before admitting ordinary Store activity. Invalidate old sessions even if restored account session-version fields match. Show a clear result and required next action rather than reporting completion before verification.
- **Forecasting portability.** Do not reactivate source model pointers or treat database-identity-bound model files as destination-ready. Prevent queued/running source work, leases, and attempts from replaying blindly after restore. Rebuild/reapprove models through existing forecasting services where supported. On current hosting, disable unsupported forecasting execution and state its unavailability clearly; do not silently serve old predictions as current destination forecasts.
- **Legacy handling.** Reject plaintext SQL in the new ordinary restore path. Keep old files private until a newly created encrypted package has been successfully restored and checked. Do not delete or relabel existing SQL/legacy encrypted artifacts or their required keys. A separate old-SQL recovery/conversion tool is not part of this change.
- **Interfaces and storage changes.** Update existing creation, download, history, restore, safety-copy, recovery-command, validation, and UI contracts coherently for the package and distinct credentials. Schema changes are permitted only where needed for explicit security/identity provenance or existing operation metadata; no speculative generic migration platform. Update existing tests/fixtures and operational instructions that currently assert plaintext export, SQL-only input, or Super Administrator-only restore.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed the testing approach during specification synthesis: reuse the existing backup/restore workflow with disposable databases and uploaded files, plus checks through the actual Administrator screens. No tests use real Store records or destructive live hosting imports.
- Use the existing workflow integration boundary as the primary seam. Exercise real database snapshot, encrypted package creation/download, restore, files, coordinator, and recovery behavior together, asserting externally observable records, access, files, and outcomes rather than private helpers or implementation text.
- Extend the current real-MySQL backup workflow integration tests, constrained SQL format tests, authorization/route coverage, and injected interrupted-restore recovery scenarios. Retain focused format tests for malformed/security-sensitive inputs that are impractical to exhaust through a browser. Keep seams few; do not replace meaningful integration behavior with mocks for every service.
- Prove both roles can create/download/restore and other roles cannot. Exercise actual HTTP authorization, active Workspace/session checks, CSRF, requester-bound downloads, current destination password verification, wrong/old passwords, and separate correct/incorrect backup passphrases. Ensure restore access does not grant general platform governance or restricted audit-screen visibility.
- Test encrypted file theft properties by checking that captured sensitive plaintext is not exposed and that incorrect passphrases, altered packages, incomplete files, unsafe archive members, resource-limit violations, arbitrary SQL, and incompatible schemas fail before destination replacement. Test normal Unicode/binary data and valid upload references round-trip.
- Use separate source/destination fixtures with different credentials, colliding account IDs, distinct people with duplicate usernames/emails, secondary privileged role assignments, a sealed Recovery Account, destination security settings/logs, and imported historical actors. Prove conflicts reject safely, explicit reconciliation works on a fresh destination, destination security survives, and historical attribution is correct after successful retry.
- Test successful replacement removes post-snapshot operational changes while preserving destination security and source operational history as specified. Prove ordinary sessions are invalidated and restored session values cannot revive them.
- Test safety capture failure leaves the existing Store unchanged. Inject failures before replacement, during database replacement, during file replacement, and before final verification. Confirm incomplete state stays blocked, the last good complete safety copy survives, recovery works with a partial users table, and successful recovery restores both files and data without an unauthenticated bypass.
- Exercise both localhost-to-hosting and hosting-to-localhost deployment shapes using disposable installations. Confirm destination URLs/credentials remain local to that installation, source activity stays paused for cutover, checks precede destination opening, and returning after new transactions requires fresh state.
- Through both administrator screens, verify understandable warnings, distinct password labels, supported file type/size, actionable conflict/recovery messages, accessible form behavior, and accurate completion/history status. Existing navigation/status behavior must still work.
- Confirm stale jobs/model pointers do not run after migration, unsupported hosted forecasting stays unavailable, and supported destinations require model rebuild/approval before forecasting resumes. Verify production and Hosted Demo storage/database remain isolated.
- Before real migration, perform a supervised restore drill on a non-production target with the matching runtime. Demonstrate off-server passphrase recovery, complete verification, and recovery after failure. A browser-only smoke test is insufficient evidence of recoverability.

## Out of Scope

- Two simultaneously operating Store installations, continuous synchronization, merging divergent sales/stock, or multi-Store support.
- Selective restoration of individual sales, Products, or arbitrary database rows as an additional feature. Preserving security is a required restore boundary, not a general selective-restore interface.
- Bundling application code, deploying the application, provisioning hosting, purchasing a VPS, changing DNS/domains, or copying environment credentials automatically.
- Running Python forecasting on unsupported hosting, a new remote forecasting service, transparent model-artifact portability, or purchasing/configuring a compatible Python server.
- New automatic backup schedules, cloud storage integration, retention automation, or redesigning the separate local-Windows deployment work. Existing planned automation must be reconciled with the new format when implemented, not silently assume plaintext output remains supported.
- A general account-merging product, automatic identity guessing, importing source privileged authority, or granting Administrator platform governance.
- Accepting arbitrary SQL or legacy encrypted formats in the new restore screen, deleting old recovery files, or implementing legacy SQL conversion/recovery tooling in this change.
- Deploying to or performing destructive tests against the live Store or the Hosted Demo.

## Further Notes

This specification synthesizes the decisions confirmed on 2026-10-24. The later question about using only an admin password was a risk discussion, not a change of decision: both current destination login password and the separate original backup passphrase remain required.

The design intentionally revisits the plaintext/full-replacement policy in ADR-0004, the recovery authority boundary in ADR-0001, and relevant backup/recovery assumptions in the local-Windows deployment specification and issue #271. The encrypted portable workflow must preserve destination security rather than reuse today's unconditional full replacement. ADR-0017 records this target; existing operational instructions describe current behavior until implementation updates them.

The recorded Hostinger site is a Hosted Demo, not authorization to replace it with real Store data. A separate production site/database and deployment compatibility checks remain prerequisites. Hostinger's current documentation places Python support on VPS rather than Web/Cloud hosting; the user accepts hosted forecasting remaining unavailable for now. No server purchase or production migration is authorized by this issue.

Losing all copies of a package's passphrase makes the package unrecoverable. An encrypted package is not proof that its creator supplied trustworthy business data: anyone holding the passphrase and a compatible exporter may construct a valid package. Continue requiring trusted backups, authorized destination login, semantic validation, explicit identity/security preservation, and a recoverable safety copy.

Implementation must update the domain/context and recovery guidance alongside the changed behavior and reconcile related planned deployment work. Do not mark the feature complete with unresolved identity mappings, incomplete security preservation, database-only safety recovery, or an untested hosting recovery path.
title: Encrypted backups, safe Database Restore, and localhost-hosting Store Migration

body:
## Parent

Part of #276. The parent specification is authoritative for scope and preservation requirements.

## What to build

Make unresolved exchanges and pending closing discrepancies visible from the landing screen across every date and Cashier. Keep their review sections consistent with that Store-wide scope, preserve history, and refresh affected displays after existing audited review actions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Landing alerts, Unresolved Activity and Reconciliation Log ignore reporting dates, Cashier selection, transaction search and type. Each alert opens its corresponding all-date, Store-wide section, with clear scope labels.
- [ ] Outstanding discrepancies count only closed sessions with an unwaived nonzero cash or wallet variance. Reconciliation history retains waived records, expected and counted funds, separate signed variances, closing attribution, waiver identity and waiver reason.
- [ ] Unresolved exchanges retain their notes and already posted partial movements. Verify & Clear explains before confirmation that it completes the exchange and posts only remaining movements; successful completion never duplicates existing movements.
- [ ] Preserve existing reference validation, wallet and physical-cash confirmations, CSRF, authorization, atomic posting and audit attribution. Keep endpoint/workspace authority unchanged, including no broader Super Administrator operational rights or direct exchange recording in this page.
- [ ] Successful verification or waiver refreshes affected outstanding counts, review records, balances and selected-period activity using each display's scope. Waiver does not erase or correct recorded variances. Preserve current selected filters and usable review controls after refresh.
- [ ] Review rows and alerts remain consistent during asynchronous filtering and action refreshes; obsolete responses cannot restore stale data. Failed loads remain visibly unavailable rather than reporting zero outstanding items or all-clear.
- [ ] Extend existing browser/HTTP and MySQL integration coverage with historical records assigned to another Cashier, waived/unwaived nonzero discrepancies, offsetting signed variances, partial movements and persisted audit records. Reuse existing negative permission, CSRF, reference and confirmation coverage; retain keyboard/dialog/mobile usability and disposable fixtures.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

body:
# Administrator GCash Overview: funds, outstanding issues, and daily activity

## Problem Statement

The Administrator needs to answer three questions quickly: what Service Cash and Service Wallet funds are recorded, which exchanges or closing discrepancies need attention, and how much completed activity and gross fees occurred today.

The existing overview can confuse missing balances with a genuine zero, label closed-session actual counts as expected balances, and count waived discrepancies as pending work. Period controls live away from the summary they affect. Transaction-list search and type selections also affect headline totals, while Cashier filtering can hide outstanding issues and leave asynchronously refreshed review sections inconsistent. A transaction count covering every status appears beside completed-only principal and fees without a sufficiently clear distinction.

## Solution

Keep the existing four sections and RetailMind visual identity. Lead Balances & Summary with separate Service Cash and Service Wallet amounts, their recording state, session responsibility and check time, and actionable Store-wide alerts. Keep any combined amount secondary.

Follow with Today-based completed activity. Put shared period and Cashier controls beside its totals; use them in Transactions too. Keep transaction search and type local to the list. Outstanding issues and review sections cover all dates and all Cashiers, independently of activity filters. Preserve traceable history, complete filtered export, and existing audited review actions and Cashier recording boundaries.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want Service Cash and Service Wallet displayed separately, so that I can assess each source of exchange funds.
2. As an Administrator, I want recorded funds before historical performance, so that I can understand the current operating position first.
3. As an Administrator, I want open-session amounts labelled Expected, so that I understand they derive from recorded movements.
4. As an Administrator, I want closed-session amounts labelled Last counted with their closing time, so that I do not mistake historical counts for current funds.
5. As an Administrator, I want missing counts displayed as Not recorded, so that unknown funds are distinguishable from a genuine zero.
6. As an Administrator, I want the session status, responsible Cashier and last actual-check time, so that I can identify responsibility and the age of the evidence.
7. As an Administrator, I want a clear explanation that recorded amounts are not a live GCash app balance, so that I understand their limits.
8. As an Administrator, I want combined funds kept secondary, so that a large combined amount does not conceal a shortage in one fund.
9. As an Administrator, I want unresolved exchanges visible on the landing screen, so that interrupted or uncertain exchanges receive attention.
10. As an Administrator, I want only unwaived closing discrepancies counted as outstanding, so that the alert describes pending review.
11. As an Administrator, I want outstanding alerts to cover every date and Cashier, so that historical reporting selections cannot hide problems.
12. As an Administrator, I want each alert to open its review section, so that I can inspect the underlying records.
13. As an Administrator, I want waived discrepancies preserved in reconciliation history, so that approval does not erase a recorded shortage or excess.
14. As an Administrator, I want Today selected initially in Philippine time, so that the page opens on the Store's current reporting day.
15. As an Administrator, I want Month-to-date and custom dates, so that I can review longer reporting periods.
16. As an Administrator, I want period controls and the selected dates beside the totals, so that their scope is apparent.
17. As an Administrator, I want a shared Cashier selection for summary activity and Transactions, so that I can review one Cashier consistently.
18. As an Administrator, I want completed exchange count, so that the headline count uses the same completion basis as the financial totals.
19. As an Administrator, I want completed Cash-In and Cash-Out principal reported separately, so that I can see the money exchanged in each direction.
20. As an Administrator, I want gross service fees split between cash and wallet, so that I can see where the fees were earned.
21. As an Administrator, I want principal distinguished from revenue and gross fees from net profit, so that I do not misread the financial measures.
22. As an Administrator, I want transaction search and type selection to narrow only the transaction list, so that headline activity retains its shared period and Cashier scope.
23. As an Administrator, I want the list count labelled as matching records, so that I understand it may include statuses beyond Completed and legacy records.
24. As an Administrator, I want transaction references, timestamps, status, Cashier and Shift attribution, so that I can trace an exchange.
25. As an Administrator, I want details showing signed cash and wallet movements, fees and linked adjustments, so that I can explain the recorded balance impact.
26. As an Administrator, I want legacy reference-only records identified honestly, so that unavailable movement data is not invented.
27. As an Administrator, I want stable pagination and full filtered CSV export, so that I can inspect or download every matching record.
28. As an Administrator, I want expected and counted closing cash and wallet with separate signed variances, so that I can inspect shortages and excesses without netting them away.
29. As an Administrator, I want waiver identity and reason retained with each discrepancy, so that its review is accountable.
30. As an Administrator, I want unresolved exchanges to retain notes and previously recorded partial movements, so that resolution does not lose or duplicate money movements.
31. As an Administrator, I want Verify & Clear to explain that it completes the exchange and records remaining movements, so that I understand the consequence before confirming.
32. As an Administrator, I want review actions protected by existing permissions, confirmations and audit records, so that review remains controlled and traceable.
33. As an authorized Cashier, I want exchange recording to remain in the Cashier workspace under existing Shift and session checks, so that cash-handling responsibility stays clear.
34. As an Administrator, I want refreshes to keep alerts, review rows and summaries consistent with their declared scope, so that stale results do not mislead me.
35. As an Administrator, I want unavailable data distinguished from zero funds or no outstanding issues, so that a failed request cannot falsely report an all-clear state.
36. As an Administrator using a keyboard or mobile screen, I want accessible tabs, dialogs and readable tables, so that all existing review tasks remain usable.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing Administrator GCash overview, its client controller and existing overview API through GCashTransactionService. Reuse the established session, balance, movement, review and export behavior; no new reporting service, framework, dependency or schema change is required by this specification.
- Preserve four sections: Balances & Summary, Transactions & Filters, Reconciliation Log, and Unresolved Activity. Retain existing RetailMind styling and responsive structure rather than replacing the visual design.
- Represent missing balance evidence distinctly from numeric zero. Open sessions expose expected balances; closed sessions expose last counted amounts and closing time. Preserve the responsible Cashier and actual-check metadata, and do not imply an open session when showing the latest closed one.
- Keep balances independent of every activity/list filter. A combined total may remain only as a secondary, accurately labelled amount; it is not a balance-sufficiency indicator.
- Apply shared start/end dates and optional Cashier selection to completed activity and transaction history. Default to Today using PhilippineTime in both initial-page and API behavior; Month-to-date runs from the first Philippine calendar day of the current month through Today. Preserve the established reporting timestamp basis and date validation.
- Display the selected reporting period beside summary controls. Transaction search and type selections affect list rows, matching-record count, pagination and CSV only. Changing shared filters updates both activity and list results without applying local list filters to headline activity.
- Return distinct completed-exchange and matching-record counts. The completed count and principal/fee totals cover Completed service exchanges in the shared reporting scope; reference-only legacy records must not invent completed exchange amounts. Matching records retain existing supported statuses and legacy history under list filters.
- Reuse existing authoritative principal and fee calculations. Report Cash-In principal, Cash-Out principal, gross cash fees and gross wallet fees separately. Do not present principal as earned revenue or fees as net profit.
- Query unresolved exchanges and reconciliation history independently of dates, Cashier selection, search and transaction type. Outstanding discrepancy counts include only unwaived nonzero closing variances; reconciliation history continues to include waived records. Each landing alert opens the corresponding all-date, Store-wide section.
- Preserve service compatibility for other GCash callers when separating query scopes and counts. Update affected initial rendering, API responses, asynchronous consumers, pagination, details and export together. Keep responses from obsolete requests from overwriting newer selections.
- After successful verification or waiver, refresh affected outstanding counts, review records, balances and selected-period totals using their respective scopes. Do not conflate a waiver with removal or correction of the counted variance.
- Preserve reference validation, both wallet/cash confirmations, CSRF protection, authorization, atomic movement posting and audit behavior. Verify & Clear completes the exchange and posts only its remaining movements. Retain the existing endpoint/workspace authority; this work grants no broader operational rights to the Super Administrator or other roles.
- Exchange recording remains in the Cashier workspace. Preserve the existing eligible-account workspace switch and open Cashier Shift/session-control requirements; do not add direct recording to this page.
- Preserve legacy labels, linked adjustments, attribution, complete filtered CSV, formula-injection protections and failure-safe export behavior. Exports follow the list's shared and local filters across every matching page.
- Retain keyboard tab navigation, accessible labels, native confirmation dialogs, bounded tables, mobile behavior and error feedback. Missing data, loading failures and invalid filters must not silently become zero balances or an all-clear statement; errors must not present fallback data as matching the rejected selection.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed reuse of existing tests on 2026-10-23. Use the existing Administrator GCash browser/HTTP suite as the primary feature boundary, with the existing GCash MySQL service integration coverage for exact totals and ledger invariants. Do not introduce a new test framework or production test interface.
- Test observable rendering, returned data, downloaded CSV, authorization outcomes and persisted movements/audit records. Avoid assertions about internal helper structure or incidental CSS.
- Exercise open, closed, never-counted and genuine-zero balance states; verify labels, timestamps and Cashier attribution. Change every reporting/list filter and verify that balance amounts remain unchanged.
- Cover Today, Month-to-date and custom dates, including Philippine day/month boundaries. Verify shared Cashier filtering, explicit period labels, distinct completed/list counts, and exact principal and fee totals.
- Use mixed-status and legacy records with multiple Cashiers and dates. Search/type changes must narrow the list and export without narrowing headline totals. Date/Cashier changes must update summary/list scope while leaving Store-wide outstanding alerts and review records intact.
- Include unresolved exchanges and waived/unwaived nonzero discrepancies outside the reporting period and assigned to another Cashier. Verify landing counts, navigation, preserved waived history and separate signed variances.
- Verify complete filtered CSV across multiple pages, matching-record counts and stable pagination, including local search/type selections and existing safe export handling.
- Verify that successful Verify & Clear and waiver refresh affected displays, preserve audit attribution, and never duplicate posted movements or remove counted variances. Reuse existing negative permission, CSRF, invalid-reference and confirmation coverage.
- Exercise delayed competing requests and failed loads: newer selections must win, and failures must not show fabricated zero balances or an all-clear result. Retain keyboard tab/dialog and desktop/mobile regression checks.
- Reuse disposable database fixtures for integration/browser tests. No production data, real GCash transfers, hardware calibration or live wallet access is needed to verify this overview feature.

## Out of Scope

- Live GCash synchronization or initiating transfers from RetailMind.
- Direct exchange recording in the Administrator workspace, new permissions, funding/replenishment workflows, emergency handover changes, or new resolution actions.
- Low-fund thresholds, alerts based on invented thresholds, charts, forecasts, multi-Store reporting or a replacement visual design.
- Provider expense accounting, net-profit reporting, fee schedule changes, principal rules or altered exchange posting semantics.
- Deleting or rewriting transaction, adjustment, audit or reconciliation history.
- Broad cleanup of older GCash documentation unrelated to this overview specification.
- Application implementation, deployment or live operations during this specification task.

## Further Notes

The user confirmed the complete design on 2026-10-23 and subsequently confirmed the proposed existing test boundaries. This specification refines Administrator overview behavior within the previously agreed GCash Service rules; it does not replace the wider service specification or authorize application implementation in this session.

Existing issues [#236](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/236) and [#237](https://github.com/ZeachDev01/retailmind/issues/237) provide earlier service requirements and operational policies. Older reference-capture documentation contains historical behavior and must not override the confirmed overview design or current movement-preserving service behavior.
title: Administrator GCash Overview: funds, outstanding issues, and daily activity
