# Administrator dashboard: clear sales, profit, and 30-day graphs

## Problem Statement

The Administrator wants to answer “How is the Store doing today, and what needs my action?” The dashboard mixes financial terms and time windows, shows only Net Sales in its main chart, and expands a large hourly/daily table that pushes historical performance down the page. Gross Sales, Net Sales, and Gross Profit are difficult to distinguish. The existing rolling performance section presents summary cards rather than a trend graph.

## Solution

Keep urgent actions first, followed by financial totals, a Sales graph, a separate Gross Profit graph, and a Last 30 Days performance graph. Preserve the existing Store identity and restrained dashboard styling.

Use one shared Today / This Week / This Month selection for the Sales and Gross Profit graphs and their totals. Default to Today. Today displays hourly results; This Week and This Month display daily results. The Sales graph compares Gross Sales and Net Sales. The separate Gross Profit graph avoids confusing revenue with profit.

Collapse the detailed hourly/daily table behind “View detailed breakdown.” Exact values remain available through chart interactions and the accessible breakdown. The separate Last 30 Days graph compares daily Net Sales and Gross Profit, with totals and percentage changes versus the previous 30 days. Show exact dates and identify ongoing intervals.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want urgent actions before financial analysis, so that I can address Store problems promptly.
2. As an Administrator, I want clearly named Gross Sales, Net Sales, and Gross Profit totals, so that I do not confuse revenue with profit.
3. As an Administrator, I want a brief explanation of each financial measure, so that I can understand the displayed amounts.
4. As an Administrator, I want Gross Sales and Net Sales in one graph, so that I can see the effect of discounts and refunds.
5. As an Administrator, I want Gross Profit in its own graph, so that I can assess profitability without confusing it with sales.
6. As an Administrator, I want Today selected initially, so that the dashboard opens on current Store activity.
7. As an Administrator, I want hourly graph intervals for Today, so that I can identify busy and quiet hours without reading a large table.
8. As an Administrator, I want daily graph intervals for This Week, so that I can compare days within the current week.
9. As an Administrator, I want daily graph intervals for This Month, so that I can understand the current month's trend.
10. As an Administrator, I want one period selection to update both graphs and their totals, so that the financial views stay aligned.
11. As an Administrator, I want exact period dates and Philippine-time labels, so that the reporting window is unambiguous.
12. As an Administrator, I want exact values on hover or tap, so that I can inspect individual intervals.
13. As an Administrator, I want details collapsed initially, so that the dashboard remains compact.
14. As an Administrator, I want to expand and collapse the breakdown with a keyboard, so that exact values remain accessible without chart interactions.
15. As an Administrator, I want a daily Last 30 Days graph, so that I can see recent performance across calendar-month boundaries.
16. As an Administrator, I want Net Sales and Gross Profit together in that graph, so that I can compare revenue and profit trends.
17. As an Administrator, I want current and previous 30-day totals with changes, so that I can assess the direction of Store performance.
18. As an Administrator, I want partial current periods identified, so that I do not mistake ongoing results for final figures.
19. As an Administrator, I want real zero activity distinguished from unavailable data, so that missing information does not look like zero sales or profit.
20. As an Administrator, I want missing costs to produce unavailable profit points, so that the graph does not invent profit.
21. As an Administrator, I want estimated costs identified, so that I understand the uncertainty in estimated profit.
22. As an Administrator, I want negative values displayed correctly, so that refund-heavy intervals and losses remain visible.
23. As an Administrator, I want charts and controls usable on a phone, so that the dashboard remains understandable on a smaller screen.
24. As an Administrator, I want period selection to survive refresh, so that updated results preserve my context.
25. As an Administrator, I want financial period controls to leave operational alerts unchanged, so that a chart choice does not silently change what needs attention.
26. As an Administrator, I want links to the existing profit report to match the selected dates, so that I can investigate the same figures.
27. As an Administrator, I want access to totals and detailed values if charts fail to load, so that I can still assess Store performance.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the existing StoreOperationsDashboardWorkspace and Administrator dashboard presentation. Reuse GrossProfitService financial calculations, existing Chart.js support, dashboard styling, period controls, and report destinations. No new dependency or database schema is needed.
- Preserve Administrator authorization and the separate operational/technical role boundaries in ADR-0001. This feature reads Store records; it does not mutate sales, refunds, costs, or inventory.
- Gross Sales means completed product sales before discounts and refunds. Net Sales equals Gross Sales minus discounts minus issued Cash Refunds. Do not relabel the existing after-discount, before-refund series as Gross Sales. Use recorded financial values and existing report rules rather than inventing a second accounting formula.
- Gross Profit equals Net Sales minus the corresponding cost of products sold, adjusted for returns according to the existing profit report. It excludes operating expenses and must never be labelled Net Profit or take-home earnings. GCash Service exchanges do not become product revenue.
- Use the established historical sale-cost provenance and refund-cost rules. Missing historical costs remain missing; do not silently substitute current product prices or costs. Distinguish recorded, estimated, incomplete, and unavailable results in plain language.
- Sales and profit are discrete interval amounts, not cumulative totals. Use grouped bars for Gross Sales versus Net Sales, consistent with the current sales graph. Use a line graph for Gross Profit and two labelled lines for the 30-day view, with a common peso axis within each graph and no dual axes. Retain stable metric colors across sections.
- Use Philippine time throughout. Today begins at midnight, weeks begin Monday, and months begin on the first calendar day. Include only events through one shared as-of time. Show elapsed empty intervals as zero; exclude future intervals rather than implying future zero activity.
- Attribute sales to completion time and Cash Refunds to issue time, including refunds of older sales. Profit buckets must reconcile to the existing profit report for the same dates and as-of time, including its refund-cost treatment. Test this explicitly rather than assuming separately calculated totals agree.
- Last 30 Days includes today and the preceding 29 calendar days through the shared as-of time. Compare against the preceding 30 complete calendar days. For example, on 23 October 2026 the current range is 24 September–23 October and the previous range is 25 August–23 September. Clearly label today/current totals as ongoing; do not imply the two windows are equally complete.
- Default the historical view to a fixed 30-day window, replacing its 7/30/90-day selector for this focused dashboard change. The historical graph remains independent of Today / This Week / This Month. Preserve existing operational count information outside financial plots; do not place transaction, discount, or exception counts on a peso axis.
- Keep operational attention queries at their existing default 30-day horizon where applicable and make that horizon visible. Chart selection must not alter operational query scope. Preserve existing alert rules and destinations; a wider attention-system redesign is outside scope.
- Show Gross Sales, Net Sales, and Gross Profit totals for the selected main period. Keep product cost and the explanation “Gross Profit excludes operating expenses” available without adding another chart. Avoid repeated period badges and repeated long headings.
- The detailed breakdown is closed initially and uses the same selected period. Include Gross Sales, discounts, refunds, Net Sales, product cost, and Gross Profit with unavailable/estimated states. Reuse a native disclosure or the existing accessible disclosure pattern rather than introducing a new interaction framework.
- Show a gap for unavailable Gross Profit intervals, never a zero or a line bridged across missing costs. Estimated intervals must be identifiable. If any interval has incomplete costs, do not present a partial known-profit sum as the complete period total; retain the report's incomplete-total policy.
- Display percentage change only when both totals are complete and the previous total is positive. When it is zero or negative, show both amounts and a plain “No comparable percentage” explanation. Label estimated comparisons and withhold comparisons involving missing costs.
- Keep controls, totals, report links, and accessible details functional if the chart library fails. Legends and readable text must identify series without relying solely on color. Respect reduced motion and provide touch and keyboard access to exact values.
- Preserve selected period in the URL and refresh/report destinations. Respect ADR-0012's existing dashboard cache lifetime and invalidation; reuse batched aggregation and avoid one full profit-report calculation per hour/day. Cache entries must include all required graph data and expire across Philippine date boundaries.

## Testing Decisions

- Prefer the existing database-backed dashboard workspace contract as the primary seam: use a controlled Clock and financial fixtures to assert externally meaningful interval values, totals, dates, and availability states. Extend the existing dashboard browser coverage for interactions and accessibility; no new service seam is needed.
- Prior art includes the Administrator dashboard workspace, route, browser, and cache tests, plus Gross Profit reporting, historical-cost, and dashboard integration tests. Reuse their fixture conventions and authorization checks.
- Cover a discounted sale, partial refund, refund of an older sale, return-cost treatment, negative interval, empty interval, missing cost, estimated cost, zero/negative previous total, and unavailable service. Assert interval sums and period totals reconcile with authoritative report calculations to currency precision.
- Verify Philippine midnight, Monday/week start, month start, a 30-day range crossing months, exact as-of inclusion, exclusion of future events, and current versus previous 30-day boundaries.
- In browser coverage, switch all three main periods and assert that both main graphs, totals, exact dates, breakdown, URL, and report destination update together while the 30-day graph and attention scope stay independent.
- Verify the breakdown is collapsed initially and can be expanded using a keyboard, touch can reveal exact values, mobile layout avoids page-level horizontal overflow, and missing/estimated values have readable explanations. Verify totals and controls still work when chart loading fails.
- Check existing caching and authorization behavior for the expanded payload, including date rollover and non-Administrator access. Tests should assert visible behavior and financial results rather than private helper names or decorative CSS class strings.
- During implementation, run the relevant existing tests and inspect desktop/mobile rendering. This specification-only task does not claim those application checks have passed.

## Out of Scope

- Application implementation, deployment, or live financial-data changes in this specification task.
- New accounting policy, net-profit accounting, operating-expense tracking, GCash accounting changes, forecasting, or cost-recovery workflows.
- New dashboard dependencies, background infrastructure, database migrations, export formats, or custom date-range controls.
- A broad navigation redesign, attention-rule overhaul, or changes to other role workspaces.

## Further Notes

The user confirmed the dashboard's daily Store-health purpose and accepted the final explanation proposing separate Sales and Gross Profit graphs plus a 30-day trend. They delegated remaining decisions and requested specification synthesis with no further interview. The testing seams above are selected from existing coverage under that delegation.

This specification supersedes overlapping financial visualization and expanded-table behavior from the earlier Store Overview Net Sales chart specification. Existing historical-cost, Cash Refund, authorization, and caching rules remain authoritative. Browser inspection was unavailable during this discussion; source review supports the current-state findings, while visual verification belongs to implementation.
title: Clarify Administrator dashboard with sales, profit, and 30-day graphs

# Cashier Selection of Administrator-created Promotions

## Problem Statement

Cashiers can enter their own discount type, value, and reason. Checkout also automatically chooses the highest eligible promotion. The Store wants Administrators to control discount rules and Cashiers to apply only an existing, applicable Promotion through a dropdown.

## Solution

Administrators continue managing Promotions through the existing workflow. Cashiers see a dropdown of Eligible Promotions for the current cart, showing names and discount amounts. Default to "No promotion"; require explicit selection and apply only one Promotion.

Remove custom discount entry and Administrator approval credentials. Administrator-created Promotions require no additional approval, including above 10%.

Revalidate when the cart changes and at checkout. If the selected Promotion becomes invalid, explain why, clear it, and require review of the updated total before payment.

## User Stories

1. As an Administrator, I want to define Promotions, so that the Store controls available discounts.
2. As an Administrator, I want existing percentage and fixed-amount rules retained, so that established Promotions remain usable.
3. As an Administrator, I want existing scope, schedule, and minimum-quantity rules retained, so that discounts apply where intended.
4. As an Administrator, I want existing activation controls retained, so that I can control availability.
5. As an Administrator, I want forged custom discounts rejected, so that bypassing the interface cannot grant a discount.
6. As a Cashier, I want a Promotion dropdown, so that I can select an existing discount without entering rules.
7. As a Cashier, I want only Eligible Promotions listed, so that available choices match the cart.
8. As a Cashier, I want names and discount amounts shown, so that I can compare choices.
9. As a Cashier, I want "No promotion" selected by default, so that discounts require an explicit choice.
10. As a Cashier, I want my selected Promotion honored even when another gives a larger discount, so that checkout respects my choice.
11. As a Cashier, I want one Promotion per sale, so that discounts cannot stack.
12. As a Cashier, I want to return to "No promotion", so that I can remove a discount before checkout.
13. As a Cashier, I want a clear empty state, so that I understand when no Promotions qualify.
14. As a Cashier, I want eligibility refreshed after cart changes, so that options reflect current items and quantities.
15. As a Cashier, I want a still-eligible selection retained and recalculated, so that its amount reflects the updated cart.
16. As a Cashier, I want invalid selections cleared with an explanation, so that I understand why they became unavailable.
17. As a Cashier, I want expiration and deactivation checked at checkout, so that outdated Promotions cannot apply.
18. As a Cashier, I want to review the updated total after invalidation, so that payment uses an acknowledged amount.
19. As a Cashier, I want Administrator-created Promotions above 10% without another password, so that approved rules need no repeated authorization.
20. As a Cashier, I want payment totals and the final quote to agree, so that I collect the correct amount.
21. As a Cashier using a keyboard or small screen, I want labeled, accessible controls, so that I can complete checkout.
22. As a Cashier, I want loading failures distinguished from no eligible choices, so that unavailable information does not appear valid.
23. As an Administrator, I want recorded sale discounts retained, so that later Promotion changes cannot rewrite history.
24. As a Cashier handling refunds, I want original-paid-amount calculations preserved, so that this change does not alter refund entitlements.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse Administrator promotion management and existing role/workspace boundaries. Cashiers cannot create or modify discount rules through checkout.
- Reuse the checkout workflow's eligibility calculation, monetary calculations, and eligible-promotion response rather than building a second promotion engine.
- Replace manual type, value, reason, and approval credentials with one Promotion selection or "No promotion".
- Send the selected Promotion identifier as untrusted checkout input. Resolve current rules and calculate amounts on the server; reject custom discount submissions and unknown or ineligible identifiers.
- Update legitimate checkout callers and quote-input tracking together.
- Default to no Promotion and remove automatic best-discount application from this workflow. Never substitute another Promotion for the selected one.
- Retain active status, inclusive schedule boundaries, cart/product/category scope, and minimum matching quantity.
- Preserve percentage/fixed calculations, matching-subtotal caps, currency rounding, and existing Sales Pack and loose-item behavior.
- Apply at most one Promotion per sale; no stacking or manual discount combination.
- Refresh eligibility and amounts after cart changes. Retain and recalculate a still-eligible selection; clear an invalid one with an explanation.
- Invalidate the reviewed quote when its inputs or applicable rules change. Revalidate at checkout and require an updated review before payment when a selected Promotion becomes invalid; never silently complete a differently priced sale.
- Administrator-created Promotions need no additional credentials, including above 10%. Remove obsolete manual-discount approval controls from this flow.
- Show names, computed monetary discounts, "No promotion", and clear empty/loading/error feedback. Failed eligibility requests must not masquerade as empty successful responses.
- Preserve labels, keyboard operation, responsive usability, payment methods, shift requirements, and fiscal-period controls.
- Preserve saved discount/Promotion details, historical receipts, and original-paid-amount refund calculations.
- Prefer existing schema and modules. No new dependency, promotion engine, or speculative configuration is required.

## Testing Decisions

- Confirmed primary seam: the existing database-backed checkout workflow, exercising quote generation and checkout through public contracts. Assert observable amounts, selected Promotion identity, rejection behavior, persistence, and stale-quote handling rather than private helpers or SQL wording.
- Confirmed supporting seam: existing cashier checkout browser tests for dropdown behavior, totals, feedback, and review invalidation. Reuse established checkout quote integration and browser coverage.
- Cover default no Promotion despite eligible choices, deliberately selecting a smaller discount, returning to no Promotion, and no stacking.
- Cover status, schedule boundaries, scope, minimum quantity, percentage/fixed calculations, matching-subtotal caps, and existing pack/piece behavior.
- Reject forged identifiers, ineligible selections, and custom discount attempts.
- Cover cart edits that retain and recalculate a selection, and edits that invalidate it and require review.
- Cover expiration and deactivation between selection, quote review, and checkout; verify no silent replacement or stale-price completion.
- Cover Promotions above 10% without additional approval and continued checkout authorization.
- Verify labels, displayed amounts, empty/error states, keyboard operation, totals, and selection-driven quote invalidation.
- Use existing receipt/refund regression coverage to verify recorded discounts and original paid amounts remain coherent.
- The user confirmed these testing seams before issue publication.

## Out of Scope

- Application implementation during this specification task.
- Cashier-created discounts, manual exceptions, stacking, or automatic best-promotion selection.
- New eligibility rules, loyalty schemes, coupon codes, customer classifications, or promotion types.
- Redesigning Administrator promotion management or expanding permissions.
- New payment methods, refund policies, historical migrations, or recalculating old discounts.
- New dependencies or a separate promotion subsystem.

## Further Notes

The user confirmed explicit selection, default "No promotion", existing eligibility, one Promotion per sale, clearing invalid selections with an explanation and renewed review, and no extra approval above 10%.

Promotion and Eligible Promotion terms are recorded in the glossary. Existing Store authority and historical receipt decisions remain applicable. No new ADR is required for this localized selection-policy change.

The user authorized publication to the project's GitHub Issues tracker with the `ready-for-agent` label. Application implementation is deferred to the resulting ticket.
title: Restrict cashier discounts to selected Administrator-created promotions

body:
## Problem Statement

The Store owner needs finalized reporting windows to remain reliable. RetailMind currently allows multiple open Fiscal Periods and overlapping date ranges, permits transactions outside every period, and closes periods without checking unfinished operational work. An overlapping open period can conceal the restrictions of a closed period. GCash and drawer cash movements do not consistently use fiscal protection.

Periods must fit owner-defined reporting ranges rather than a mandatory calendar month. Staff need actionable explanations when a transaction or closure is refused, without losing access to history or the ability to finish reconciliation.

## Solution

Provide one Administrator-governed Fiscal Period lifecycle for the Store. Permit at most one open period, disallow overlapping dates, and require consecutive periods to meet without date gaps. Require every new money or stock movement to have an open period covering its effective date.

The Administrator chooses the first range, which must include the Store's current date before trading starts. Later periods start the day after the previous period ends. Ranges may span any owner-defined number of days. Closing and opening remain explicit Administrator actions; there is no automatic rollover.

Closing is allowed only once the end date has arrived, every Cashier Shift is closed, all GCash sessions are closed and reconciled, and pending Inventory Counts dated within the period are approved or rejected. Closed periods and their dates remain fixed. Later refunds and supported corrections create traceable entries in the current open period while preserving original records.

## User Stories

1. As the Store owner, I want to define a reporting date range of any required length, so that my Fiscal Periods fit how I review the Store.
2. As an Administrator, I want to create the first period with today's date included, so that trading begins within a valid reporting window.
3. As an Administrator, I want a second open period refused, so that only one reporting window accepts transactions.
4. As an Administrator, I want overlaps refused against both open and finalized periods, so that every covered date has one unambiguous period.
5. As an Administrator, I want the next start date to follow the previous end date immediately, so that no reporting dates are skipped.
6. As an Administrator, I want to open the next period explicitly after closing the current one, so that rollover remains under my control.
7. As an Administrator, I want early closure refused, so that a still-running date range is not finalized accidentally.
8. As an Administrator, I want closure refused while any Cashier Shift remains open, so that cashier activity is finished first.
9. As an Administrator, I want closure refused while GCash sessions are open or unreconciled, so that service cash and wallet activity are settled first.
10. As an Administrator, I want closure refused while the period has pending Inventory Counts, so that unfinished stock discrepancies do not enter finalized reports later.
11. As an authorized Inventory Count reviewer, I want to approve or reject submitted counts before closure, so that actual stock differences are handled through the existing review workflow.
12. As an Administrator, I want closure blockers explained with the affected records, so that the responsible staff can finish the work.
13. As a Cashier, I want checkout refused when its date has no open period, so that sales cannot bypass fiscal protection.
14. As a Cashier, I want a later Cash Refund recorded in the current open period, so that the original sale and its closed period remain unchanged.
15. As a GCash operator, I want cash-in, cash-out, funding, and money-affecting corrections subject to fiscal protection, so that GCash follows the same reporting boundary as other Store money.
16. As a Cashier, I want drawer cash movements subject to fiscal protection, so that cash activity cannot escape period controls.
17. As an Inventory Manager, I want Stock Receiving, stock adjustments, count adjustments, opening stock, and supplier-related stock movements protected, so that stock activity follows the same reporting boundary.
18. As a staff member, I want a refused operation to leave balances and records unchanged, so that retrying after the problem is resolved is safe.
19. As a staff member, I want reports and permitted historical views to remain accessible without an open period, so that I can investigate and reconcile problems.
20. As a Cashier or GCash operator, I want session and shift closure to remain available when new transactions are blocked, so that fiscal controls do not trap unfinished sessions.
21. As an Administrator, I want to correct an open period's end date with an audit record, so that an incorrect range can be repaired responsibly.
22. As an Administrator, I want date edits refused if they exclude existing transactions, overlap another period, or break continuity, so that corrections preserve reporting integrity.
23. As an Administrator, I want reopening and edits to finalized period dates refused, so that finalized reporting windows remain stable.
24. As an authorized operator, I want supported corrections recorded as new, linked entries in the current open period, so that the original history remains traceable.
25. As the Store owner, I want existing period conflicts identified before strict enforcement starts, so that transition problems are visible without silently rewriting transactions.
26. As the Store owner, I want simultaneous actions to preserve the same rules as ordinary actions, so that concurrent requests cannot create two open periods or post into a period being closed.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing FiscalPeriodGuardService and operational service entry points. Extend their shared protection rather than adding a parallel fiscal subsystem or a dependency. Keep lifecycle validation shared across supported Administrator write routes.
- Preserve the single-Store model and Administrator workspace authority. The owner defines ranges through that workspace; do not add an owner role. Fiscal authority does not grant inventory-review or Cashier permissions. Retain authorization, CSRF protection, and existing table-specific locks.
- Validate real calendar dates and ordered, inclusive date ranges server-side. Use the existing Philippine Store-time conventions consistently for effective transaction dates and the current date, including midnight boundaries.
- Enforce at most one open period, including concurrent create requests. Reject all range intersections, including an end date reused as the next start date. The successor starts on the following calendar day, including across month, year, and leap-day boundaries.
- There may temporarily be zero open periods between explicit closure and opening. No money or stock transaction may use this gap to bypass fiscal protection. An expired period still marked open does not authorize today's activity outside its range.
- Require an open period for each new money or stock movement's effective date. Cover checkout, refunds, receiving and purchase stock, opening stock, stock-affecting product changes, adjustments, counts, Stock Issue inventory effects, supplier pullouts, GCash, drawer cash, imports, and other supported write paths. Find and close alternate-path bypasses rather than relying on disabled buttons.
- Fiscal refusal must preserve existing validation and leave the operation's records, balances, stock effects, and success audit records uncommitted. Preserve existing transaction atomicity.
- Check closure prerequisites at commit time together with period state. Prevent concurrent posting, opening of sessions/shifts, count submission, and period changes from invalidating those checks. Use the existing database transaction and locking patterns; a UI precheck alone is insufficient.
- Treat resolved Inventory Counts as approved or rejected, using existing statuses and reviewer permissions. Do not require every Product to be counted before closure. Approval records any required adjustment before finalization; rejection does not change stock.
- Reuse the GCash reconciliation model to establish that sessions are both closed and reconciled. Merely having a closed status must not conceal unresolved reconciliation work. Explain the remaining blocker using existing operational language.
- Keep read access and Cashier Shift/GCash session closure available when no period covers today. Distinguish completing reconciliation from initiating a new money or stock movement: session closure is not a general bypass for otherwise forbidden postings. Verify the existing settlement paths when implementing this distinction.
- Permit only valid forward lifecycle transitions. Closed and locked periods remain unwritable; crafted requests must not reopen them, change finalized dates, or downgrade locked state. Retain existing locks without introducing a new lock-state design.
- Allow only the Administrator to amend an open period's end date. Preserve its start date, all existing transaction coverage, nonoverlap, and continuity; record actor and before/after values through existing audit facilities. Preserve existing lifecycle audit records.
- Post later refunds and supported corrections in the current open period, linked to their originals. Do not backdate them into a closed period or modify original sales, receipts, or finalized period dates. This does not introduce new kinds of correction workflows.
- Update affected test fixtures and seed/setup paths to establish valid periods instead of depending on missing-period permission. Do not give ordinary application writes an implicit setup bypass.
- Before activation on existing data, inspect missing coverage, overlapping ranges, multiple open periods, and unfinished closure work. Preserve transactions and historical dates, and require reviewed resolution of conflicts before strict activation. Do not invent synthetic transactions, silently reassign history, edit closed dates, or treat this specification as authorization for a production-data repair.
- Show actionable, accessible operation and closure messages using existing components. Keep technical diagnostics in existing logs, following Store alert conventions. No broad fiscal-page redesign is required.

## Testing Decisions

- User-confirmed test seams: use existing service entry points with database-backed integration tests for fiscal and transaction behavior, plus the Administrator request boundary for lifecycle authorization and validation. Use a small browser smoke check only for the changed controls and actionable blocker presentation. No new testing framework or production abstraction is needed.
- Good tests call supported operations and assert user-visible results, persisted records, unchanged state after refusal, and audit behavior. Avoid tests that merely search source text or duplicate implementation conditions.
- Follow the existing Cash Refund contract, Inventory Count reconciliation, Cashier Shift reconciliation, and GCash transaction integration tests. Reuse disposable databases and fixtures. Prefer the highest existing seam that exercises the behavior; do not force unrelated workflows behind a new test facade.
- Cover custom multi-month and single-day ranges, invalid dates, reversed ranges, inclusive endpoints, leap days, Philippine midnight, first-period setup, consecutive successors, duplicate opens, overlap with open/closed/locked periods, and gaps.
- Cover absence of a matching period, an expired open period, closed and locked dates, existing table locks, and successful eligible writes. Include every newly guarded money/stock entry point and relevant alternate import or route paths.
- Verify closure refuses each blocker individually, then succeeds after the required work is resolved. Include approved and rejected counts, no submitted counts, and the absence of any requirement to count every Product.
- Verify an October sale refunded in a valid November period leaves October and the original sale unchanged and records November refund effects exactly once.
- Verify valid and invalid end-date changes, audit attribution, unauthorized and forged requests, repeated/stale closure, attempted reopening, finalized-date edits, and locked-state downgrade attempts.
- Verify reports, shift closure, and GCash reconciliation/closure remain reachable with posting blocked, without allowing a new money or stock movement into an uncovered or finalized date.
- Use the actual supported database for concurrency checks: simultaneous opens, period closure against money/stock posting, and closure against new shifts/sessions or pending count submission. Assert preserved invariants and no partial effects.
- Exercise transition diagnostics on conflicting historical fixtures and confirm there are no silent transaction/date rewrites. Verify existing workflow fixtures pass with explicit valid fiscal setup.

## Out of Scope

- Mandatory monthly, quarterly, or yearly ranges; fiscal periods as Cashier Shifts.
- Multiple Stores, branches, tenants, or concurrent operational Fiscal Periods.
- Automatic rollover, automatic reopening, retroactive edits to finalized periods, and backdated corrections into closed periods.
- Mandatory full-store stocktaking at every close, automatic approval/rejection of counts, or new review permissions.
- New financial ledgers, tax-reporting rules, accounting exports, correction transaction types, dependencies, or a general workflow engine.
- A broad interface redesign, notification project, or destructive production-data migration.

## Further Notes

Policy decisions were confirmed in the design discussion on 2026-10-22. This specification records requested behavior; no application implementation or database repair has been performed.

Current code exploration found missing-period permission, ambiguous overlap selection, insufficient lifecycle transition checks, absent closure prerequisites, and missing fiscal checks in GCash and drawer cash workflows. Existing Inventory Count approval checks both the original count date and the adjustment date, which is why pending counts must be resolved before finalization.

No actual operational database was audited during specification writing. Existing-data resolution must respect immutable history; if the discovered conflicts cannot be resolved within these agreed rules, report the concrete conflict for a separate decision instead of silently relaxing the rules.
title: Enforce one open Fiscal Period with continuous ranges and safe closure

body:
# Local Windows deployment with private remote access

## Problem Statement

The Store owner wants RetailMind to run on an existing dedicated Windows PC with one wired barcode scanner and one thermal printer. Cashiers must be able to sell when the Store's internet connection is unavailable, and the application must start whenever Windows starts without someone launching Laragon or dismissing its popup.

The owner also wants optional private internet access for approved users. A host failure must be recoverable from separately stored backups. Existing backup capture, role authorization, and scheduling components cover part of this need, but unattended deployment, durable backup archiving, and local-only cashier enforcement are not complete.

## Solution

Deploy one local RetailMind application and primary database using standalone Apache HTTP Server, PHP, and the existing MySQL/MariaDB engine. Configure Apache and the database for automatic Windows service startup, and run the existing PHP/Python background jobs through Windows scheduling independently of Laragon. Once services are ready, the Cashier opens the local browser URL; automatic browser launch or Windows sign-in is not required.

Provide optional encrypted private-network access for the owner and approved staff using an installed client on their remote devices. Remote access supports authorized reports, inventory, and administration; completing sales and Cash Refunds is restricted to the Store checkout PC. Keep application sign-in and active Workspace permissions in force through both access routes.

Create one automatic Database Backup per day, retain 30 daily recovery copies subject to storage capacity, and preserve recoverable copies on an external drive and encrypted owner-controlled cloud storage. The user accepts potential loss of approximately one day of sales and inventory changes after drive failure. Target restoration within four business hours when suitable replacement hardware and recovery credentials are available. The owner decides UPS purchase and runtime; the user maintains updates, backup alerts, and recovery.

## User Stories

1. As the Store owner, I want to use the existing Windows PC, so that deployment does not require another server.
2. As a Cashier, I want RetailMind's services to start whenever Windows boots, so that I do not need to launch a development control panel.
3. As a Cashier, I want a documented local browser address, so that I can open RetailMind once its services are ready.
4. As a Cashier, I want checkout to work while the Store's internet connection is unavailable, so that an ISP outage does not stop local sales.
5. As a Cashier, I want the existing wired barcode scanner to work, so that I can scan Products without new scanning hardware.
6. As a Cashier, I want the existing thermal printer to print and reprint Sale Receipts, so that customers receive proof of purchase.
7. As a Cashier, I want existing Cashier Shift, stock validation, and duplicate-submission protections preserved, so that deployment does not change transaction correctness.
8. As the Store owner, I want private access from an approved phone or laptop, so that I can view Store Reports away from the Store.
9. As an Inventory Manager, I want approved remote access to my existing Workspace, so that I can perform permitted inventory work away from the Store.
10. As an Administrator, I want my existing authorized administrative workflows remotely, so that I can manage the Store without visiting it.
11. As the Store owner, I want remote access limited to approved users and devices, so that the application does not require public website exposure.
12. As the Store owner, I want remote access revocable, so that a lost device or departed staff member can lose access.
13. As the Store owner, I want remote sales and Cash Refunds blocked even for a user with a Cashier role, so that checkout remains at the physical register.
14. As a multi-role user, I want active Workspace permissions preserved, so that private-network membership does not combine my assigned roles.
15. As the Store owner, I want a consistent Database Backup created daily, so that a host failure does not require rebuilding all Store records manually.
16. As the Store owner, I want 30 daily recovery copies retained, so that I can recover from a problem discovered after the latest backup.
17. As the Store owner, I want a backup copied to a separate external drive, so that the host's internal drive is not the only recovery location.
18. As the Store owner, I want encrypted cloud copies, so that a Store-site incident does not necessarily destroy every recovery copy.
19. As the Store owner, I want local backups to continue during an internet outage, so that cloud unavailability does not prevent backup capture.
20. As the maintainer, I want capture, external-copy, and cloud-copy failures distinguishable, so that I know which recovery copies actually exist.
21. As the Store owner, I want control of the cloud account and an encryption-key recovery copy outside the PC, so that recovery does not depend entirely on the maintainer.
22. As the maintainer, I want a documented replacement-PC restoration procedure, so that I can pursue the agreed four-business-hour recovery target.
23. As the Store owner, I want to understand that daily backups can lose approximately a day of records, so that the recovery limit is explicit.
24. As the maintainer, I want forecasting and notification jobs scheduled independently of Laragon, so that background operations survive the deployment change.
25. As the Store owner, I want to approve UPS capacity, runtime, and cost, so that power protection matches the Store's needs and budget.
26. As the maintainer, I want compatible application files, configuration, uploads, and forecasting artifacts included in the recovery procedure, so that a SQL file is not mistaken for a complete PC recovery package.
27. As the Store owner, I want exact recurring service prices reviewed before purchase, so that the deployment creates no unapproved subscription costs.
28. As the maintainer, I want a rehearsed boot, internet-outage, and restore checklist, so that readiness is demonstrated on the actual Windows setup.

## Implementation Decisions

- **One host and database:** The Store PC hosts the application, primary database, and current PHP/Python jobs. Remote users access the same application and data. No cloud replica, synchronization protocol, second writable database, or automatic failover is introduced.
- **Standalone Windows services:** Replace reliance on Laragon with standalone Apache and PHP integration plus the existing database engine. Preserve compatible runtime versions, required PHP extensions, application URL handling, Apache access restrictions, and filesystem permissions. Configure automatic service startup and dependency ordering; validate actual startup rather than assuming service registration proves readiness.
- **Windows scheduling:** Reuse the current asynchronous forecasting scheduler/CLI worker and notification maintenance flows. Do not introduce the legacy Flask service. Schedule work while the PC is powered on and document missed-run handling; jobs cannot run while the PC is off. Correct stale deployment instructions accordingly.
- **Local checkout availability:** Sale finalization still requires a reachable application server and database, but not a working ISP connection when both run locally. Audit required assets and operational requests for external dependencies and verify cold-start operation without internet. PC failure, service failure, or power loss remains an outage. Cached carts are not permission to finalize a sale without the server.
- **Private remote ingress:** Use an installed private-network client for approved remote devices. The specific provider, account plan, and price are setup selections rather than decisions already made. Keep the database and recovery storage unavailable through remote web access. Use encrypted remote transport, retain application authentication, and document device/user enrollment and revocation.
- **Trusted local-only authorization:** Enforce the location restriction on every sale-finalization and Cash Refund mutation, including alternate endpoints and multi-role Workspace switching. Hiding navigation or checking assigned roles alone is insufficient. Use a trustworthy distinction between local checkout ingress and private remote ingress. Do not infer trust from arbitrary client-supplied forwarding headers or assume a proxy's loopback connection makes a request local. Preserve ordinary role, Cashier Shift, validation, CSRF, and concurrency checks.
- **Browser origin and HTTPS:** Use a stable loopback origin for checkout on the host PC where supported. If another browser origin or device is introduced, validate its secure-context requirements before use. Verify Web Locks, session cookies, and generated links under the selected remote HTTPS arrangement; trust proxy metadata only from configured trusted ingress. A wired barcode scanner does not require adding phone-camera scanning.
- **Durable daily backups:** Reuse the coordinated Database Backup capture and existing SQL format. Immediately preserve successful scheduled captures in a durable protected archive rather than relying on temporary downloads. Capture completion, external-copy completion, and cloud-copy completion are separate outcomes. Validate copied artifacts and retain dated successful daily copies; failed or partial copies must not replace the last good recovery copy.
- **Retention and schedule:** Retain 30 daily recovery copies subject to provisioned capacity. The maintainer selects a daily time when the PC will be on and documents what happens when a run is missed or the PC is shut down early. Make stale/missed backups and unavailable destinations visible to the maintainer through a documented operational check or existing status surface. Do not claim a one-day loss bound after failed or missed backups.
- **Private storage and encryption:** Keep active recovery locks/state on reliable private local storage outside the application and web roots. Archive copies outward; do not turn a cloud-sync directory into the active recovery store. Encrypt cloud-bound archives before upload. Existing readable manual SQL downloads and the SQL restore format remain as defined by the backup ADR; encryption is an outer archive/storage protection layer, removed before ordinary SQL validation and restore. Restrict access to local plaintext artifacts and keep secrets out of source control, logs, and public URLs.
- **Backup destinations:** Use an external drive for recovery from host-drive failure and owner-controlled cloud storage for an additional off-site copy. Continue local capture/copy while cloud connectivity is down and report cloud staleness; upload preserved pending copies when connectivity returns. A connected external drive is not independent protection against ransomware, theft, or site loss.
- **Complete recovery:** Document preservation or reinstallation of the matching application version, configuration, required uploads, forecasting artifacts, dependencies, and private recovery records in addition to SQL. Reuse existing Super Administrator-only Database Restore validation, safety backup, Store blocking, and session invalidation. Stop independent database writers during restoration. Do not merge newer records into a full-replacement restore.
- **Recovery targets:** One daily backup with approximately one day of potential data loss supersedes the earlier one-hour proposal. Four business hours is a target conditional on suitable replacement hardware, usable backup copies, keys, credentials, and matching software; a restore drill must establish whether it is realistic. Use manual sales recording while the application is unavailable; automatic reconciliation of those records is not part of this feature.
- **Power and maintenance:** The owner retains the UPS purchase/runtime decision. Short-outage bridging and controlled shutdown are recommendations, not an approved runtime specification. Size and test against the actual connected load. Automatic Windows service startup does not guarantee the PC itself powers on after an outage; firmware and UPS behavior require separate validation. The user is responsible for updates, backup-failure review, and recovery, while the owner retains account and encryption-key recovery access.
- **Interfaces and scope:** Reuse the existing backup, restore, authorization, sales/refund, and scheduling boundaries. No new schema or public API contract was agreed in the discussion. Prefer deployment configuration and the smallest shared enforcement/automation changes needed for these requirements; update affected callers and operational documentation together.

## Testing Decisions

The user confirmed using existing browser/HTTP workflows, existing backup/restore integration coverage, and a Windows boot/outage/restore acceptance checklist. Tests assert observable outcomes rather than specific configuration text, helper calls, or internal archive layouts.

- **Primary seam: deployed application workflows.** From the local checkout browser, open a Cashier Shift, scan a Product with the wired scanner, complete a sale, print its Sale Receipt, retry a submission safely, and perform an authorized Cash Refund. Reuse existing cashier browser, receipt, refund, and offline-scanning scenarios.
- **Real ISP outage:** Disconnect internet access while keeping the PC and local services running. Test a fresh browser session/page load as well as an already-open checkout. Verify required assets load, scanning and sale finalization work, and receipts print. Browser-wide offline emulation alone is insufficient because it can also block the local server. Confirm remote access becomes unavailable without corrupting local transactions.
- **Remote authorization:** Exercise approved reports, inventory, and administration through the private route. Attempt sale and Cash Refund mutations through that route using a valid Cashier Workspace, a multi-role user, alternate mutation routes, direct HTTP requests, and spoofed forwarding headers. Verify rejection and unchanged sales, cash, and stock records. Verify the same authorized local flows still succeed and unauthorized private-network users do not bypass sign-in.
- **Backup and archive behavior:** Extend existing Database Backup/Database Restore integration coverage using disposable databases and existing overlap/concurrent-writer scenarios. Verify a consistent capture survives temporary-download cleanup, successful copies match the captured artifact, cloud archives are encrypted and recoverable, and retention preserves the required daily history.
- **Backup failures:** Simulate a missing external drive, denied write, insufficient disk space, encryption failure, lost internet/cloud credentials, and overlapping runs. Verify failures are reported without deleting or replacing the last good copy, local backup can succeed during a cloud outage, and pending cloud copies can subsequently complete. Verify a failed run is not reported as a fresh recoverable daily backup.
- **Windows startup and jobs:** Cold-boot the actual PC, confirm Apache/database readiness and scheduled-job operation without opening Laragon or an interactive control panel, and verify checkout after services become ready. Exercise early shutdown/missed schedules and startup recovery instructions. Check that the configured recovery target is not claimed merely because a task exists.
- **Secure origins and deployment boundaries:** Verify checkout recovery/browser features, session cookies, generated URLs, remote TLS, and trusted-ingress behavior. Confirm backend/private artifacts, SQL files, credentials, and database ports are not exposed through either web route.
- **Restore drill:** On an isolated suitable replacement environment, recover the owner-controlled key and archive, decrypt the trusted SQL, restore through existing safeguards, recover required non-database artifacts, and verify sign-in, Products/stock, Sale Receipts, reports, and background jobs. Measure elapsed recovery time against four business hours. Never use the live Store database as a destructive test fixture.
- **Hardware and power acceptance:** Test the actual scanner and thermal printer with the deployed browser/driver settings. If a UPS is purchased, validate supported safe shutdown and actual runtime on the chosen load without risking live transaction data. Document behavior after power returns.

## Out of Scope

- Installing, migrating, publishing the application, or purchasing services as part of this specification-writing session.
- Public website exposure, anonymous access, public router port forwarding, or remotely exposed database/admin tools.
- Cloud hosting of the primary application, multiple Stores, database replication, automatic failover, or continuous availability while the PC is off.
- Offline sale finalization without the local application server, offline payment authorization, or automatic import of manually recorded outage sales.
- A one-hour recovery-point guarantee, zero data loss, or guaranteed four-hour recovery without available replacement hardware.
- New scanning hardware, camera-scanning workflows, a new receipt design, or replacement of the existing thermal printer.
- Selecting or buying a UPS before the owner's runtime/budget decision and measured load are available.
- New forecast models, Flask hosting, new role combinations, or changes to existing restore privileges and full-replacement semantics.
- A new monitoring platform, backup-management dashboard, generalized installer framework, or provider abstraction without a demonstrated need.

## Further Notes

- This specification records the discussion on 2026-10-22. It authorizes specification publication and future implementation planning, not live deployment, destructive migration, or purchases.
- The owner must review exact recurring costs before purchase. Private-network provider, cloud provider, credentials, backup clock time, storage capacity, and UPS model/runtime remain installation-specific selections; do not invent paid commitments or embed account secrets in the issue.
- The existing scheduler documentation recognizes a dedicated Windows Store PC. Parts of the deployment checklist still describe older worker/setup assumptions and must be reconciled with the current CLI scheduling flow.
- Existing SQL capture produces temporary private artifacts rather than a durable encrypted off-PC archive. Existing Workspace authorization does not enforce the agreed location restriction. Both gaps require implementation and behavioral verification.
- The older caching ADR describes finalization as requiring an internet connection. For this deployment, the requirement is connectivity to the authoritative application server/database; with those on the checkout PC, an ISP connection is unnecessary. Preserve its server-side validation and idempotency requirements and clarify that wording in the related documentation.
- The encrypted cloud archive requirement supplements, rather than changes, the readable manual SQL download and trusted full-replacement restore policies.

# Show Refund Receipt after a completed refund

## Problem Statement

After completing a Cash Refund, the Cashier needs to see the customer's Refund Receipt immediately, without searching refund history. The Cashier must be able to review and print it without opening the print dialog automatically or risking another refund.

## Solution

Immediately show the saved Refund Receipt inline after a successful Cash Refund. Keep the original Sale Receipt unchanged. Provide a Print Refund Receipt button that opens the browser print dialog only when clicked. Retain the existing receipt fields, thermal preview, and configured paper width.

## User Stories

1. As a Cashier, I want to see the Refund Receipt immediately after a successful refund, so that I know which refund was completed.
2. As a Cashier, I want the receipt to appear without searching history, so that I can finish serving the customer.
3. As a customer, I want a separate Refund Receipt, so that I have proof of the refund.
4. As a customer, I want the original Sale Receipt preserved, so that my purchase record remains unchanged.
5. As a Cashier, I want the receipt to identify the refund and original sale, so that I can match the refund to the purchase.
6. As a customer, I want the receipt to show only items and quantities returned in this refund, so that it accurately describes this return.
7. As a customer, I want the amount for this refund shown clearly, so that I can check the money refunded.
8. As a Cashier, I want each later refund against the same sale to have its own receipt, so that separate refunds remain distinguishable.
9. As a Cashier, I want the existing payment, date and time, Cashier, Register, and reason fields retained, so that the receipt remains complete.
10. As a Cashier, I want the existing inline thermal preview retained, so that I can review the customer copy before printing.
11. As a Cashier, I want the receipt to use the configured paper width, so that it fits the available printer.
12. As a Cashier, I want printing to start only when I click Print Refund Receipt, so that I control when the browser dialog opens.
13. As a Cashier, I want to select my installed printer through the browser dialog, so that I can use the existing printing setup.
14. As a Cashier, I want canceling printing to leave the refund completed and receipt visible, so that printing cannot undo the transaction.
15. As a Cashier, I want the Print Refund Receipt button available after canceling, so that I can retry without recording another refund.
16. As a Cashier, I want refreshing the completed receipt to avoid another refund or automatic print dialog, so that refresh is safe.
17. As a Cashier, I want to reopen my saved Refund Receipt from history, so that I can provide another copy later.
18. As a customer, I want later reprints to retain the recorded receipt details, so that subsequent Store or product edits do not change my refund record.
19. As a Cashier, I want existing receipt access restrictions preserved, so that unauthorized accounts cannot retrieve customer receipts.
20. As a Cashier, I want a failed refund to show its existing error rather than a completed receipt, so that I do not mistake a failed attempt for a successful refund.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing Cash Refund completion flow, saved Refund Receipt retrieval, receipt presentation, and shared thermal print behavior. Prefer fixing an observed gap over introducing another receipt system.
- A successful refund already redirects to a GET for its saved receipt and renders an inline preview. Verify this behavior through the real completion flow; do not assume a new screen or module is needed.
- Show the receipt only after the refund transaction succeeds. A failed refund retains existing validation and error handling.
- Preserve the original Sale Receipt and append-only Cash Refund accounting. Each Refund Receipt represents exactly one refund and references the original sale.
- Keep Print Refund Receipt as an explicit action. Do not open the print dialog automatically after completion, refresh, or a history visit.
- Canceling or retrying printing must not repeat the refund. Refreshes and reprints retrieve an existing receipt without creating another transaction.
- Preserve existing receipt fields, exclusion of internal notes and stock classifications, saved transaction-time details, and current 80 mm or 58 mm paper-width behavior.
- Preserve Cashier, Store, Cashier Shift, Register lock, and receipt authorization rules.
- No new schema, public API, dependency, modal, or separate browser tab is required by this spec. Remain consistent with ADR-0006.

## Testing Decisions

- The user confirmed the existing refund completion flow as the primary verification seam: submit a valid refund, follow completion to its receipt, then exercise manual printing, canceling, and reopening.
- Assert observable behavior rather than source strings or private helper structure: the correct receipt is visible after success, its refund and original sale identifiers match, its items and amount cover only this refund, and the original sale remains unchanged.
- Cover both full and partial refunds; for multiple refunds against one sale, verify that each receipt contains only its own refund.
- Use existing Cash Refund contract and Refund Receipt browser/reprint coverage as prior art. Reuse their synthetic fixtures and isolated test databases; do not create refunds against operational data.
- Verify that completion, refresh, and reopening do not invoke printing automatically; clicking Print invokes the browser print action.
- Verify that canceling leaves the completed receipt visible and permits retry, and that printing, refresh, and reopening create no additional financial writes.
- Retain existing authorization, saved-detail stability, internal-field exclusion, and 80 mm/58 mm checks. Extend tests only where the completion path lacks coverage.
- Check the existing error path does not present a successful receipt for a failed refund.

## Out of Scope

- Automatic or silent printing, direct printer integration, printer purchase, and device-specific feed or cutter controls.
- Replacement or edited Sale Receipts, cumulative refund summaries, or retained-item receipts.
- Receipt redesign, new fields, new navigation, a receipt modal, or opening another browser tab.
- Changes to refund eligibility, approval, settlement, inventory, or accounting rules.
- Changes to Sale Receipt behavior after checkout.

## Further Notes

The final requirement is to show the receipt automatically, not print automatically. This supersedes the earlier interview answer requesting an automatic print dialog.

Code inspection indicates that the existing implementation already redirects a completed refund to its saved inline Refund Receipt. End-to-end runtime behavior has not been verified during this specification session. The resulting work should verify the requested behavior and repair any demonstrated gap; no application change is necessary if the existing flow satisfies the acceptance criteria.
title: Show Refund Receipt immediately after a completed refund

# Role-based Notifications

Status: Product decisions and test approach confirmed on 2026-10-21. Ready for implementation; implementation has not started.

## Problem Statement

Staff receive Notifications unrelated to their responsibilities. Routine inventory alerts reach Administrators and Cashiers, technical model-training failures reach operational staff, and users with secondary roles can miss relevant updates. A shared user inbox mixes Workspaces, making unread counts and read actions unreliable indicators of each role's work.

Administrator attention currently treats every pending Stock Issue as an escalation. Required work can also be suppressed by inconsistent preference handling, while repeated checks can generate unnecessary alerts. Existing development Notifications reflect these inconsistent rules.

## Solution

Route Notifications according to responsibility across every assigned role, and show each Workspace only its relevant updates. Keep required-action in-app Notifications enabled, retain optional routine reminders and daily email, escalate significant inventory exceptions to the Administrator, and notify again only on escalation or recurrence after resolution.

| Workspace | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Super Administrator | Platform security, locked accounts, backup and restore failures, system health, and technical Demand Forecast failures. |
| Administrator | Cash discrepancies, unusual discounts, sales reversals, Fiscal Period deadlines, and serious or overdue inventory exceptions. |
| Inventory Manager | Low stock, replenishment, expiry and Supplier Pullout reminders, unusual demand, and Stock Issues awaiting review. |
| Cashier | Own workflow updates, including Stock Issues returned, approved, or rejected; relevant stock warnings during checkout. |

Administrator inventory oversight remains read-only. Routine replenishment alerts do not fill Cashier inboxes. Correct existing development Notifications without changing operational records.

## User Stories

1. As a Super Administrator, I want security and locked-account alerts, so that I can protect platform access.
2. As a Super Administrator, I want backup, restore, and system-health alerts, so that I can investigate technical failures.
3. As a Super Administrator, I want technical Demand Forecast failure alerts, so that operational staff do not receive internal error details.
4. As an Administrator, I want cash discrepancies, unusual discounts, and sales reversals highlighted, so that I can investigate Store exceptions.
5. As an Administrator, I want Fiscal Period deadline alerts, so that I can complete compliance work.
6. As an Administrator, I want serious or overdue Stock Issues escalated, so that I can oversee risk without deciding inventory adjustments.
7. As an Administrator, I want out-of-stock products and overdue expired-stock collection escalated, so that I can follow up with Inventory Managers.
8. As an Inventory Manager, I want routine low-stock and replenishment alerts, so that I can plan stock purchases.
9. As an Inventory Manager, I want expiry and Supplier Pullout reminders, so that I can prepare goods for collection.
10. As an Inventory Manager, I want unusual-demand alerts, so that I can review replenishment needs.
11. As an Inventory Manager, I want new and resubmitted Stock Issues promptly, so that I can review reports.
12. As a Cashier, I want my returned Stock Issues highlighted, so that I can correct and resubmit them.
13. As a Cashier, I want approval and rejection updates for my Stock Issues, so that I know their outcomes.
14. As a Cashier, I want relevant stock warnings during checkout, so that I can respond while serving a customer.
15. As a Cashier, I want replenishment alerts routed to Inventory Managers, so that my inbox remains relevant.
16. As a multi-role staff member, I want eligibility based on every assigned role, so that a secondary role does not miss its work.
17. As a multi-role staff member, I want the active Workspace's list and bell count, so that I can identify that role's unread updates.
18. As a multi-role staff member, I want read actions isolated by Workspace, so that reading one role's updates does not clear another role's unread work.
19. As an account administrator, I want role removal to revoke access to that role's Notifications, so that former assignments do not retain visibility.
20. As a staff member, I want required-action in-app alerts to remain enabled, so that preference changes do not hide required work.
21. As a staff member, I want routine reminders and email to remain optional, so that I can control optional delivery.
22. As an email recipient, I want new or escalated conditions emailed through the daily run, so that unchanged conditions do not create daily duplicates.
23. As a staff member, I want unresolved required work to remain visible after reading, so that reading is not mistaken for resolution.
24. As a staff member, I want another alert when a resolved condition returns or an active condition escalates, so that meaningful changes receive attention.
25. As a developer, I want existing development alerts corrected and current conditions regenerated, so that demonstrations match the agreed role rules.
26. As a reporting Cashier, I want valid Stock Issue workflow updates retained during cleanup, so that useful history survives.
27. As a staff member, I want my Notifications protected from other users, so that Workspace filtering preserves account isolation.

## Implementation Decisions

- Reuse the existing Notification service, Attention rules and signal source, Stock Issue workflow, daily notification runner, and shared authorization and Workspace mechanisms. Correct both transaction-driven and scheduled producers consistently.
- Determine recipients from all currently assigned roles and active-account eligibility. Primary-role-only selection is insufficient. Keep role permissions separate; Notification eligibility does not grant authority to perform the linked action.
- Maintain a reliable recipient Workspace association for filtering, unread counts, read mutations, and destinations. Exact storage representation is an implementation choice; use the smallest consistent extension to existing persistence.
- Scope lists, categories, counts, individual read actions, bulk read actions, and links to both the signed-in user and active Workspace. Do not rely on hidden links as authorization.
- New or resubmitted Stock Issues notify eligible Inventory Managers immediately through the workflow. Returned, approved, and rejected reports notify their reporting Cashier.
- Stock Issues escalate when pending for at least 24 hours OR valued at PHP 5,000 or more. Reuse existing configurable thresholds. Counting all pending reports alone must not trigger escalation. Preserve the existing per-report value calculation rather than treating the total value of unrelated reports as a serious individual report.
- Products becoming out of stock escalate to Administrator oversight. Expired stock remaining uncollected 24 hours after expiry also escalates. Reuse the Store's inventory and Stock Batch conventions and Philippine time; stock that is no longer present must not continue generating an active expiry condition.
- Routine low stock and approaching expiry remain Inventory Manager concerns. Checkout warnings remain contextual Cashier feedback.
- Required-action in-app delivery overrides optional-delivery preferences for security failures, pending Stock Issue reviews, returned reports, and escalated exceptions. Routine reminders and email remain optional. Do not treat the entire Notification Category as mandatory when its individual conditions differ.
- Keep email on the existing daily notification run. Only newly triggered or escalated conditions are eligible, subject to email preferences and available recipient addresses. There is no immediate-email guarantee. Email-only recipients must also be deduplicated.
- Use stable condition identity and lifecycle state. Repeated checks of an unchanged condition must not insert or email another alert. Reading does not resolve a condition. Notify again on escalation or recurrence after actual resolution; required unresolved work remains visible independently of unread status.
- Send technical model-training failures to the Super Administrator. Operational recipients must not receive raw internal error details.
- Correct existing development Notifications: remove misrouted generated alerts, regenerate alerts for current conditions under the agreed rules, and retain valid Stock Issue workflow updates. Identify the development target explicitly before mutation. Do not change sales, inventory, or Stock Issue records. Cleanup must be safe to repeat without duplicate current alerts.
- Preserve authorization, user ownership, CSRF protection, escaped content, and the existing accessible list and read controls.

## Testing Decisions

- Confirmed approach: extend existing notification browser coverage and existing service contracts. Prefer these established seams over new testing interfaces.
- Test externally observable recipient selection, delivery, Workspace visibility, unread counts, read mutations, and condition lifecycle. Avoid assertions that merely mirror internal SQL or private implementation details.
- Exercise the Notification page, bell, and read actions with disposable-database fixtures: each role, a user with multiple roles, a secondary-role-only recipient, role removal, disabled accounts, and another signed-in user's isolation.
- Retain existing category, All/Unread, Show more, read-state preservation, CSRF, and responsive accessibility checks where changed behavior touches them.
- Extend the Attention rule contract for the role split and escalation boundaries immediately below and at 24 hours and PHP 5,000. Confirm that an ordinary new pending report does not escalate.
- Use existing Stock Issue workflow contracts for new/resubmitted manager alerts and returned/approved/rejected reporting-Cashier updates.
- Extend existing daily-notification and inventory-alert fixtures for optional preferences, mandatory overrides, email-only recipients, out-of-stock transitions, expiry escalation boundaries, no remaining expired stock, unchanged reruns, resolution, escalation, and recurrence.
- Verify that development cleanup preserves valid workflow history and operational records, removes misrouted generated alerts, and remains safe on a second run.
- Use the existing injectable clock and disposable database patterns. Never run destructive fixture or cleanup checks against an unidentified configured Store database.

## Out of Scope

- Changing role permissions or giving Administrators inventory execution authority.
- New sales, payment, refund, shift, procurement, or inventory workflows.
- SMS, push notifications, a new messaging provider, or real-time email delivery.
- A broad notification UI redesign, unrelated refactoring, or speculative delivery settings.
- Production notification-history deletion or modification of sales, inventory, or Stock Issue records during development cleanup.
- Guaranteed immediate delivery for conditions detected only by a scheduled run.

## Further Notes

- Product decisions were confirmed through eleven discussion questions on 2026-10-21, including optional daily email. The user also confirmed the existing browser-test and service-contract seams before publication.
- This specification preserves the existing single-Store role-authority split and uses the project's Notification, Workspace, Stock Issue, Supplier Pullout, and role vocabulary.
- Code inspection confirmed partial role routing, broad low-stock recipients, technical training failures sent to operational roles, primary-role-only recipient queries, and a user-wide inbox without Workspace separation.
- The existing Attention rule contract passed during investigation. That verifies current behavior only; this feature has not been implemented or validated.
- Actual scheduler configuration and email delivery remain unverified. Thresholds establish eligibility; detection and delivery depend on the relevant workflow or successful scheduled run.
title: Route notifications by assigned role and active workspace

#256

## What to build

The current Replenishment Recommendations entry point becomes the selected stock-based shopping table. Inventory Managers see which active Products need buying, exact Base Unit quantities, Receiving Unit shopping guidance, and understandable reasons. Recommendations remain optional guidance; actual goods are recorded separately through Stock Receiving.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preserve exactly the selected seven columns: Priority, Product, On hand, Reorder at, Target, Suggested purchase, and Why. Include all active Products and retain useful search/filter/receiving actions. Default order is Out of stock, Low stock, then In stock, with deterministic ties.
- [ ] Use existing recorded-stock semantics consistently across affected stock-status and low-stock consumers: stock at or below zero is Out of stock, positive stock at or below Reorder Level is Low stock, and stock above it is In stock. Safety Stock is included in Reorder Level, never a second independent trigger. Do not introduce expiry-adjusted availability.
- [ ] Null Target Stock is explicitly unconfigured, distinct from a zero suggestion, for every stock state. Show Not set and Set target stock while retaining stock status. Authorized Inventory Managers can reach the existing Product editor; oversight workspaces gain no edit rights.
- [ ] With a configured target, stock above Reorder Level produces no purchase even below target or with an MOQ. At or below the trigger, suggest the larger of target minus stock and MOQ. Never add Safety Stock or round to multiples of MOQ or Units per Package.
- [ ] Show exact suggested Base Units and a Receiving Unit breakdown using actual labels and saved Units per Package. Omit empty package counts, zero remainders, and redundant breakdowns for a multiplier of one. A Receiving Unit breakdown neither claims unopened Sales Pack availability nor changes stock form.
- [ ] Stock 15, reorder 20, target 60, MOQ 1, and 12 bottles per case produces 45 bottles and 3 cases plus 9 loose bottles; stock 0 and target 48 produces 48 bottles and 4 cases. MOQ 50 raises a deficit of 45 to 50; MOQ 10 leaves 45. Explain MOQ overshoot accurately. Valid Safety Stock changes do not independently change suggestions.
- [ ] Show the stock-settings basis and remove forecast/readiness messaging that implies it determines these quantities. Ready/missing forecasts, Observation Mode, and recommendation suspension do not change this formula. Preserve separate forecast services, history, tests, and governance; do not add a mode selector or trigger forecast work.
- [ ] Keep visible status text with red/amber/green treatments, semantic headers, keyboard access, essential values on narrow screens, and existing role view permissions. Cover all four selected example rows, seven headers, units, priority order, setup guidance, and read-only behavior in focused existing browser checks.
- [ ] Extend the existing Product save-to-recommendation workflow with disposable database assertions for trigger boundaries, null targets including In stock, MOQ behavior, valid Safety Stock changes, and forecast independence. Update response consumers and fixtures affected by the recommendation contract. Reading or refreshing does not mutate stock.

## Coordination

Coordinate with #253 so Base Units are counted exactly once and Receiving Units remain distinct from Sales Packs. Preserve historical receiving multipliers and existing receiving-conversion checks. Reuse existing implementation and test seams; no new end-to-end test architecture or unrelated catalog refactor.
